children.text: saṅkalpa-kalpa-druma
children.translated_text: <s>Saṅkalpa-kalpadruma</s> (The Wish-fulfilling Tree of Resolve)

children.text: śrīrādhādāmodarābhyāṃ namaḥ1
children.translated_text: Obeisance to Śrī <s>Rādhā</s> and <s>Dāmodara</s>.

children.text:
śrī-kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇa-caitanya sa-sanātana-rūpaka |
gopāla raghunāthāpta vraja-vallabha pāhi mām ||1||2
nanda-nandana ity uktas trailokyānanda-vardhanaḥ |
children.translated_text: He who is called '<s>Nanda-nandana</s>' (Son of Nanda), the increaser of the bliss of the three worlds,

children.text: anādi-janma-siddhānāṃ gopīnāṃ patir eva yaḥ3 ||2
children.translated_text: who is indeed the lord of the <s>gopīs</s> (cowherd women) whose perfection has been established since beginningless births —

children.text: navīna-nīrada-śyāmaṃ taṃ rājīva-vilocanam |
children.translated_text: him, dark as a fresh rain-cloud, with lotus-eyes,

children.text: vallavī-nandanaṃ vande kṛṣṇaṃ gopāla-rūpinam ||3
children.translated_text: the delight of the cowherd women, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> in the form of <s>Gopāla</s> (the cowherder), I worship.

children.text: yugmam
children.translated_text: A pair of verses

children.text: vṛndāraṇye jaran jīvaḥ kaścit prāha manaḥ prati |
children.translated_text: Growing old in <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, <s>Jīva</s> once said to his own mind:

children.text: mriyase sāmprataṃ5 mūḍhaḥ gūḍhām etāṃ sudhāṃ piba ||4
children.translated_text: 'You are dying now, O fool — drink this hidden nectar!'

children.text: tāṃ pibann eva he svānta svaṃ ca gokula-saṅgatam |
children.translated_text: 'Even as you drink it, O my heart, [visualize] yourself as connected with <s>Gokula</s>,

children.text: sevāṃ ca vāñchitāṃ kāñcid bhāva-bhedena bhāvaya ||5
children.translated_text: and contemplate some desired service with a particular devotional mood (<s>bhāva</s>).'

children.text: maṅgalaḥ sarva-lokānāṃ gopa-kṣauṇībhṛd-aṅgajaḥ |
children.translated_text: The son of the cowherd king, auspicious for all worlds,

children.text: bhavyaṃ pallavayan pāyād vallavī-jana-vallabhaḥ ||6
children.translated_text: causing the good to blossom, may he protect — the beloved of the cowherd women!

children.text: aho bakīty6 ādikīrtiḥ kṛṣṇas tu bhagavān svayam |7
children.translated_text: He whose fame begins with 'Aho <s>bakī</s>' — <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> is indeed the Supreme Lord (<s>Bhagavān</s>) himself;

children.text: asti yas tasya pitrāditayā citrāya k ptavān ||7
children.translated_text: he who, through the affection of his father and others, created that wonderful [display].

children.text: stutas tad bhūribhāgyeti8 tathā cetthaṃ satām iti9 |
children.translated_text: He who was praised as 'O greatly fortunate one!' and also as 'Thus indeed among the saintly,' and

children.text: nemaṃ viriñca ity10evaṃ nāyaṃ śriya iti11 vrajaḥ ||8
children.translated_text: 'Not even <s>Viriñca</s> (Brahmā)' — and 'Not even <s>Śrī</s> (the Goddess of Fortune)' — such is <s>Vraja</s>.

children.text: yas taṃ ko vāśrayen nātra kṣitāv indriyavān naraḥ |
children.translated_text: Who among the sentient beings on this earth would not take refuge in him?

children.text: tasmād bhrātar nija-trātaḥ svānta svāntas tam āśraya ||9
children.translated_text: Therefore, O brother, O heart, protected by your own [Lord], take refuge in him, O my heart!

children.text: tribhiḥ kulakam
children.translated_text: A group of three verses

children.text: upadeśaṃ deśa-rūpaṃ mama mānaya mānasa |
children.translated_text: Honor this instruction in the form of a domain, O mind!

children.text: sudhā-dhārā-dharaḥ so'yaṃ kalpaḥ syāt kalpa-bhūruhaḥ ||10||
children.translated_text: This bearer of the stream of nectar would be the <s>kalpa</s> (cosmic tree), the wish-fulfilling tree.
O Śrī <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, <s>Kṛṣṇa Caitanya</s>, together with <s>Sanātana</s> and <s>Rūpa</s>, O <s>Gopāla</s>, beloved of <s>Raghunātha</s>, O beloved of <s>Vraja</s>, protect me!

children.text: mūlaṃ janmādi-līlāsya skandhaḥ syān nitya-līlatā |
children.translated_text: Its root is the pastime (<s>līlā</s>) of birth and so on; its trunk is the eternal pastime;

children.text: śākhās tat-tad-ṛtu-ślokāḥ phalaṃ premamayī sthitiḥ ||11||
children.translated_text: its branches are the verses describing each season; its fruit is the state suffused with <s>prema</s> (divine love).

children.text: atha mahā-kulakena janmādi-līlā ||
children.translated_text: Now, the pastimes of birth and so forth, in a great group of verses:

children.text: yas tantramantrayor guptam uktaḥ śrīnandanandanaḥ |
children.translated_text: He who is proclaimed as Śrī <s>Nanda-nandana</s> (Son of Nanda), hidden in both <s>tantra</s> and <s>mantra</s>,

children.text: tadrūpatāṃ nijāṃ vyāñjīt kutaścit kutukād bhuvi ||12||
children.translated_text: manifested his own essential form on earth, out of some playful curiosity.

children.text: yaḥ prāg iti12 hi padyābhyāṃ nandātmajatayā svataḥ |
children.translated_text: He who was first [described] by those two verses beginning 'He who...,' as the son of <s>Nanda</s> by his own nature,

children.text: vāsudevatayā kāryavaśād gargeṇa niścitaḥ ||13||
children.translated_text: and as <s>Vāsudeva</s> by force of circumstance, was determined by <s>Garga</s>.

children.text: 1. (b) śrī-śrī-rādhā-kṛṣṇābhyāṃ namaḥ; 2. Gcp 1v1; 3. GautT. 2.24; there: aneka-janma-śuddhānām, Gcp 15.72 aneka-janma-siddhānāṃ; 4. (b) not found; 5. (b) mriyate 'sāmpratam; 6, BhP iii.2.23; 7. BhP i.3.28||; 8. BhP x.14.34||; 9. BhP x.12.11; 10. BhP x.9.20; 11. BhP x.47.60; 12. BhP x.8.14
yaḥ śrī-nanda-yaśodāntar-hṛdi sphūrtiṃ gatas tataḥ |
children.translated_text: He who, having entered as an inspiration within the hearts of Śrī <s>Nanda</s> and <s>Yaśodā</s>, then

children.text: udyaṃś cakre dugdha-sindhor indor janma-viḍambanam ||14||
children.translated_text: rising, created an imitation of the birth of the moon from the ocean of milk.
[Textual notes and references to Bhāgavata Purāṇa passages]

children.text: yaḥ sarva-rddhi-vrajaṃ nanda-vrajaṃ svaṃ janma-mātrataḥ |
children.translated_text: He who, by his birth alone, made <s>Nanda's</s> <s>Vraja</s> — [already] the abode of all prosperity —

children.text: ramāṇāṃ jāyamānānām ārāmaṃ1 dhāma nirmame ||15||
children.translated_text: into a pleasure-garden, a dwelling-place of joys being born.

children.text: yaḥ sva-mādhurya-pīyūṣaṃ sampūrya2 pariveśayan |
children.translated_text: He who, filling [all] with the nectar of his own sweetness and distributing it,

children.text: jigāya mohinī-rūpaṃ kṣīra-nīradhi-tīragam ||16||
children.translated_text: surpassed the <s>Mohinī</s> form [of Viṣṇu] standing on the shore of the ocean of milk.

children.text:
yaḥ kṛpāṃ janmanā vyañjan pūtanām api pūtatām |
nītāṃ dhātrī-gatiṃ sphītāṃ cākārṣīn nūtanārbhakaḥ ||17||3
yaḥ komala-padāgreṇa śakaṭaṃ tad viśaṅkaṭam |
children.translated_text: He who, with the tip of his tender foot, the cart — that formidable [demon] —

children.text: sva-jyotsnāvaraṇaṃ matvā cikṣepākṣepavān iva ||18||
children.translated_text: considering it a covering of his own moonlight, kicked it away, as though in displeasure.
He who, manifesting compassion through his birth, led even <s>Pūtanā</s> to purity, to the exalted destination of a wet-nurse — he, the newborn infant, attracted [her].

children.text: yaḥ pūjita-pada-kṣepa-kūjita-smita-rociṣām |
children.translated_text: He who, with the splendor of his worshipped foot-steps, cooing, and radiant smiles,

children.text: śobhayā lobhayāmāsa bālikāḥ kula-pālikāḥ ||19||
children.translated_text: enchanted the young girls, the protectresses of the household, with charm.

children.text: yaḥ sva-nāmādyam āsādya gargād vargān nijān anu |
children.translated_text: He who, having received his own names at the outset from <s>Garga</s>, to his own kinsmen

children.text: harṣaṃ vavarṣa nyag jalpann om itthaṃ somajin-mukhaḥ ||20||
children.translated_text: showered forth joy, babbling softly, 'Om, thus!' — he whose face was [bright] like the moon.

children.text: yas tṛṇāvartam āsādya sadyaḥ saṃvarta-vartanam |
children.translated_text: He who, upon encountering <s>Tṛṇāvarta</s>, instantly whirling him about with cosmic-dissolution force,

children.text: saṃvartayaṃs tam āninye viparīta-parītatām ||21||
children.translated_text: led that [demon] into the opposite of his own whirling — reversed helplessness.

children.text: yaḥ śrī-rāmaṃ nijārāmaṃ saṅgacchann accha-khelayā |
children.translated_text: He who, encountering Śrī <s>Rāma</s> (Balarāma), his own [brother and] delight, through pure play,

children.text: bālān ānandayan nanda-rāja-keśari-nandanaḥ ||22||
children.translated_text: delighting the boys — the lion-cub son of King <s>Nanda</s>.

children.text: yaḥ puṇḍraṃ rocanārucyaṃ kañcukaṃ kāñcana-prabham |
children.translated_text: He who [received] the <s>puṇḍra</s> (forehead mark) bright with <s>rocanā</s> (yellow pigment), a garment of golden luster,

children.text: dadhan mātus tat tadāsīd utsaṅgasī yad ājani ||23||
children.translated_text: and curd from his mother — that was [the scene] when he was born upon her lap.

children.text: yaḥ kurvan kardama-krīḍāṃ nirvyājam anayā dhṛtaḥ |
children.translated_text: He who, engaging in play in the mud without guile, was held by her;

children.text: dvayoḥ sukhena duḥkhena snigdhān digdhān vinirmame ||24||
children.translated_text: through the pleasure and pain of both, he made the affectionate ones anointed [with love].

children.text: yaḥ samaṃ sahajātena raṅgann aṅgaṇa-kardame |
children.translated_text: He who, playing with his co-born [brother] in the courtyard mud,

children.text: kiñcit kātara-dhīḥ paśyan mātaraṃ drutam īyivān4 ||25||
children.translated_text: somewhat timid in mind, looking at his mother, ran quickly [to her].

children.text: yas tayāliṅgitaḥ sā smitaṃ stanyam ananya-dhīḥ |
children.translated_text: He who was embraced by her; he, single-minded, drank her breast milk with a smile,

children.text: apāyi suṣṭhu cāpyāyi smitaṃ bibhrad udaikṣi ca ||26||
children.translated_text: was well nourished, and was seen bearing a smile.

children.text: yas tadā mātur āninye sarvaṃ vismṛti-vismṛtam |
children.translated_text: He who then brought to his mother a complete forgetting of all forgetting,

children.text: vadann iva sa5saṃmugdha-bāla-siṃhāvalokanaḥ ||27||
children.translated_text: as if speaking — with the sideways glance of a bewildered young lion.

children.text: yas tadā mṛttikāṃ bhakṣann alakṣyam anayā dhṛtaḥ |
children.translated_text: He who, while eating earth unnoticed, was caught by her —

children.text: dayayā kiṃ bhayād asyās trātaḥ srāg yoga-māyayā ||28||
children.translated_text: was he [acting] out of compassion or out of fear of her? He was protected swiftly by <s>Yogamāyā</s> (divine illusion).

children.text: yaḥ śrī-rāmānvayī kāmān nanāṭa saha-pāṭavam6 |
children.translated_text: He who, accompanying Śrī <s>Rāma</s> (Balarāma), roaming with desires, displaying skill,

children.text: vṛddhānāṃ sukham ṛddhānāṃ kurvāṇas tāla-pālanam ||29||
children.translated_text: creating happiness for the prosperous elders, protecting the palm trees.

children.text: yaḥ krīṇan kara-vibhraṣṭa-mūlyatve 'py amitaṃ phalam |
children.translated_text: He who, while buying, though the payment slipped from his hand, [received] boundless fruit;

children.text: phalāny ananyalabhyoani dade vikrīṇatīṃ prati ||30||
children.translated_text: he gave fruits unobtainable by others to the woman selling [them].

children.text: 1. (a) oṃ mārāmaṃ; 2. (b) sarvatra; 3. this verse missing from (b); 4. (b) iyivān; 5. (b) suo; 6. (b) sahapāṭavaḥ
children.translated_text: [Textual notes and variant readings]

children.text: yas tarṇakān purā muñcann añcan bāla-balānvitaḥ |
children.translated_text: He who, releasing his own calves earlier, moving with childish strength,

children.text: dohānukaraṇaṃ kurvan sukha-dohāya k ptavān ||31||
children.translated_text: imitating milking, created [conditions] for easy milking.

children.text: yaḥ karṣann api vatsasya pucchaṃ saṅkarṣaṇānvitaḥ |
children.translated_text: He who, even pulling the tail of a calf, together with <s>Saṅkarṣaṇa</s> (Balarāma),

children.text: tena karṣaṃ vrajan bhrātṛ-bhāyābhiḥ paryahasyata ||32||
children.translated_text: being dragged by it, was laughed at by the [other] brothers' wives.

children.text: yaḥ kurvann api gavyānāṃ cauryaṃ bhavyāya didyute |
children.translated_text: He who, even while stealing dairy products, shone for the auspicious;

children.text: yasya tābhir vivādaś ca sukha-saṃvāda-siddhaye ||33||
children.translated_text: and whose quarrel with those [gopīs] was for the accomplishment of sweet conversation.

children.text: yaḥ svaṃ dāmodaraṃ śrṇvan sāmoda-vrīḍam añcati |
children.translated_text: He who, upon hearing [the name] '<s>Dāmodara</s>' (Bound-by-a-rope) applied to himself, swelled with joy and bashfulness,

children.text: prasū-śikṣāmaya-snehād bālya1svehāntarād api ||34||
children.translated_text: from the affection born of his mother's discipline, and also from the inner sweetness of childhood.

children.text: yaḥ suṣṭhu khelayāviṣṭaḥ sva-mātrā praṇayān muhuḥ |
children.translated_text: He who, thoroughly absorbed in play, though called repeatedly by his mother with affection —

children.text: kṛṣṇa kṛṣṇāravindākṣety2 āhūto 'py āśu nāyayau ||35||
children.translated_text: '<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, lotus-eyed one!' — did not come quickly.

children.text: yaḥ śrī-vṛndāvanaṃ prāñcan bhrātrā saha vanāspadam |
children.translated_text: He who, going forth to Śrī <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, that abode of forests, with his brother,

children.text: hāsayan bhāsayāmāsa3 mātarau yātarau mithaḥ ||36||
children.translated_text: causing laughter, illuminated the two mothers as they vied with each other.

children.text: yaḥ śrī-vṛndāvane labdhe prārabdha-krīḍam anvabhūt |
children.translated_text: He who, having obtained Śrī <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, commenced his play, and experienced

children.text: rāma-dāmādibhiḥ sakhyaṃ tat-prakhyaṃ bhramarādibhiḥ ||37||
children.translated_text: friendship with <s>Rāma</s> (Balarāma), <s>Dāma</s>, and others — friendship [as natural as] that with bees and the like.

children.text: yaḥ śrī-rāmeṇa tatrāpi vīkṣya prītim agāt parām |
children.translated_text: He who, together with Śrī <s>Rāma</s>, seeing [them] there too, attained the highest delight —

children.text: vṛndāvanaṃ govardhanaṃ yamunā-pulināni ca4 ||38||
children.translated_text: <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, <s>Govardhana</s>, and the banks of the <s>Yamunā</s>.

children.text: yaḥ prāpta-madhya-kaumāraḥ pitrā sārdhaṃ vanaṃ vrajan |
children.translated_text: He who, having reached the middle of boyhood (<s>kaumāra</s>), going to the forest with his father,

children.text: pṛcchan nāmāni dhāmāni paśyan mudam avāptavān ||39||
children.translated_text: asking the names and abodes [of places], seeing [them], obtained joy.

children.text: yaḥ krīḍan śiśur avrīḍam agrajena vrajendrajaḥ |
children.translated_text: He who, as a child playing shamelessly with his elder brother, the son of the king of <s>Vraja</s>,

children.text: jalpājalpi mithaś cakre hastāhasti padāpadi ||40||
children.translated_text: engaged in mutual babbling, clapping hand to hand and stepping foot to foot.

children.text: yaś cārayan nijān vatsān vatsakaṃ nāma dānavam |
children.translated_text: He who, while tending his own calves, [encountered] the demon named <s>Vatsa</s>,

children.text: bakaṃ bakavad-ākāraṃ dārayan muktam ārdayat ||41||
children.translated_text: and <s>Baka</s>, whose form was like a crane — tearing them apart, the liberated one slew [them].

children.text: yaḥ svair viharaṇaṃ cakre meṣī-haraṇa-saṃjñitam |
children.translated_text: He who performed sports called 'stealing of the she-goats' with his own [companions],

children.text: vyomaṃ ca vyomatāṃ ninye kurvantaṃ pratilomatām ||42||
children.translated_text: and led <s>Vyoma</s> [the demon] to the state of [mere] sky, as he was acting contrarily.

children.text: yaḥ kurvaṃs tam aghaṃ khaṇḍaṃ vidher agham ataḥ param |
children.translated_text: He who, destroying that [demon] <s>Agha</s>, and [performing] the supreme transgression of <s>Vidhi's</s> (Brahmā's) providence,

children.text: ninye sva-jyotiṣi prāñcaṃ tad arvāg bhakti-tejasi ||43||
children.translated_text: led [<s>Brahmā</s>] to his own light, the earlier one, and that which follows, to the splendor of <s>bhakti</s> (devotion).

children.text: yaḥ kaumāram atikramya ramya-paugaṇḍa-maṇḍanaḥ |
children.translated_text: He who, passing beyond boyhood (<s>kaumāra</s>), adorned with delightful pre-adolescence (<s>paugaṇḍa</s>),

children.text: cakre gopālatāṃ gacchan loka-pālaka-pālatām ||44||
children.translated_text: becoming a cowherd (<s>gopāla</s>), assumed the protection of the protectors of the worlds.

children.text: yaḥ kāla-kūṭa-niṣpiṣṭa-cetanān vraja-ketanān |
children.translated_text: He who revived the residents of <s>Vraja</s>, whose consciousness had been crushed by the deadly poison of <s>Kāliya</s>,

children.text: cetayāmāsa kṛpayā locanāmṛta-vṛṣṭibhiḥ ||45||
children.translated_text: with compassion, through showers of the nectar of his glances.

children.text: yaḥ kāliyam api vyaktaṃ nijāṅghri-yuga-mudrayā |
children.translated_text: He who clearly [impressed] <s>Kāliya</s> too with the seal of his own two feet,

children.text: vyañjan mameti śaraṇāgatān anyān arañjayat ||46||
children.translated_text: manifesting 'he is mine,' and delighted the others who had taken refuge.

children.text: yaḥ śukena vraja-premāspadatvenettham īritaḥ |
children.translated_text: He who was thus proclaimed by <s>Śuka</s> as the abode of the love of <s>Vraja</s> —

children.text: kṛṣṇe 'rpitātma-suhṛd ity ādi procya praśocya ca ||47||
children.translated_text: 'One who has offered his self and friends to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>' — having declared and lamented thus:

children.text: 1. (b) bālyaṃ; 2. BhP x.11.15; 3. (b) bhāṣayāmāsa; 4. BhP x.11.36
children.translated_text: [Textual notes and references to Bhāgavata Purāṇa passages]

children.text: ābāla-vṛddha-vanitāḥ sarve 'ṅga1 paśu-vṛttayaḥ |
children.translated_text: From children to the elderly and women — all, O dear one, having the nature of cattle (<s>paśu</s>),

children.text: nirjagmur gokulād dīnāḥ kṛṣṇa-darśana-lālasāḥ ||48||
children.translated_text: went forth from <s>Gokula</s>, wretched, longing for the sight of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>.

children.text: 2[mahākulakāntar yugmakam]2
children.translated_text: [A pair of verses within a great group]

children.text: yas tasmin sambhrame rodhān niṣkrame3 vraja-kanyakāḥ |
children.translated_text: He who, in that commotion, upon the emergence [of the gopīs] from the barriers, the maidens of <s>Vraja</s> —

children.text: mene tāḥ prathamaṃ paśyan svaṃ kṛtārthaṃ kṛtāv iha ||49||
children.translated_text: seeing them for the first time, considered himself fulfilled, fulfilled in this [world].

children.text: yas tadā dahanaṃ goṣṭha-premnākṛṣṭa-vivecanaḥ |
children.translated_text: He who then, his discrimination drawn away by the love of the cowherd settlement, [swallowed] the fire;

children.text: premnas tasya parīkṣārtham iva drāg apibat prabhuḥ ||50||
children.translated_text: as if to test that love, the Lord swiftly drank [the forest fire].

children.text: yaḥ sparśād anṛtīkurvan viṣaṃ viṣadharaṃ ca tam |
children.translated_text: He who, by his touch, making the poison and the serpent himself unreal,

children.text: svāśritān amṛtīkartuṃ kṛtī kaimutyam aikṣayat ||51||
children.translated_text: showed, being adept, the a fortiori — [his power] to make those who take refuge in him immortal.

children.text: tas tu bhāṇḍīram āsādya malla-tāṇḍavam ācaran |
children.translated_text: Then, reaching [the tree] <s>Bhāṇḍīra</s>, performing wrestling-dance —

children.text: subhadra-4maṇḍalī-bhadra-bhadravardhana-gobhaṭāḥ ||52||
children.translated_text: the cow-warriors <s>Subhadra</s>, <s>Maṇḍalī</s>, <s>Bhadra</s>, and <s>Bhadravardhana</s>,

children.text: yakṣendra-bhaṭa ity5 evaṃ k pta-saṅgaiḥ kumārakaḥ |
children.translated_text: the warrior of the <s>Yakṣa</s>-king — thus with organized teams, the boy

children.text: savayobhiḥ sukhaṃ lebhe yatra kāścit kumārikāḥ ||53||
children.translated_text: obtained happiness with his age-mates, where some young girls [were present]:

children.text: gopālī pālikā dhanyā viśākhā dhyāna-niṣṭhikā6 |
children.translated_text: <s>Gopālī</s>, <s>Pālikā</s>, <s>Dhanyā</s>, <s>Viśākhā</s>, <s>Dhyānaniṣṭhikā</s>,

children.text: rādhānurādhā somābhā tārakā daśamī tathā7 ||54||
children.translated_text: <s>Rādhā</s>, <s>Anurādhā</s>, <s>Somābhā</s>, <s>Tārakā</s>, and the tenth likewise.

children.text: kautukāya gatā yāsu mallī mallīti narma-kṛt |
children.translated_text: Having gone among them for sport — 'Jasmine! Jasmine!' — the jester,

children.text: madhvājya-nibham āsvādya yābhiḥ k ptaṃ sma mādyati ||55||
children.translated_text: tasting [their company], sweet as honey and ghee, rejoiced through what was done with them.

children.text: pūrvavan mahākulakāntaś caturbhir anvayaḥ
children.translated_text: As before, the end of a great group, with a sequence of four

children.text: yaḥ kāmye kāmyake gatvā saraḥ sāgara-sannibhaṃ |
children.translated_text: He who, having gone to the beautiful <s>Kāmyaka</s> [forest], to a lake resembling the ocean,

children.text: laṅkākalpākṛtākalpaṃ nityaṃ dīvyati saṅgibhiḥ ||56||
children.translated_text: of indescribable beauty like <s>Laṅkā</s>, eternally sports with his companions.

children.text: yaḥ kaiśoraṃ tataḥ sajjan vasantam iva ṣaṭpadaḥ |
children.translated_text: He who then, entering adolescence (<s>kaiśora</s>), like a bee [entering] spring,

children.text: lolayann ātmanaś cittaṃ lolayāmāsa padminīḥ ||57||
children.translated_text: agitating the mind of himself, agitated the lotus-women.

children.text: yas tā vraja-ramā nitya-preyasīḥ kutukātmanā |
children.translated_text: He who, those cowherd beauties of <s>Vraja</s>, his eternal beloveds, with his playful nature,

children.text: līlā-śaktyānyathā-bhānaṃ nītā guptam arañjayat ||58||
children.translated_text: by the power of his <s>līlā</s> (divine play), secretly led to a different perception and delighted them.

children.text: yaḥ śrī-rāmeṇa dhenūnāṃ rakṣāyāṃ dhenukāsuram |
children.translated_text: He who, together with Śrī <s>Rāma</s> (Balarāma), in the protection of the cows, slew the demon <s>Dhenuka</s>,

children.text: nighnan vighnam apākārṣīd akārṣīd abhayaṃ divi ||59||
children.translated_text: removing the obstacle and creating fearlessness in the heavens.

children.text: yaś cakre dhenum ādāya sāyaṃ vrajam upāgataḥ |
children.translated_text: He who, having taken the cows, arriving at <s>Vraja</s> in the evening,

children.text: pūrva-rāgaṃ kiśorīṇām apūrvaṃ vyativīkṣayā ||60||
children.translated_text: created the first love (<s>pūrva-rāga</s>) of the young maidens, unprecedented, through sidelong glances.

children.text: yaḥ pūrvaṃ lajjayā dūta-kāma-lekhādy-upāyatām |
children.translated_text: He who, at first abandoning through shyness the means of messengers, love-letters, and the like,

children.text: vijahan nija-netrāntaṃ ninye nūtana-dūtatām ||61||
children.translated_text: led the corner of his own eye to a new ambassadorship.

children.text: yas tāsu sphuṭam āsajya virajya laghu sarvataḥ |
children.translated_text: He who, openly attaching [himself] to those [gopīs] and then quickly becoming detached from all,

children.text: tad-aṅga-saṅga-bhikṣārthaṃ veṇu-śikṣām asādhayat ||62||
children.translated_text: for the sake of begging the contact of their limbs, mastered the instruction of the flute.

children.text: yaś cetanācetanāliṃ karṣann apy āśu veṇunā |
children.translated_text: He who, though attracting the entire array of conscious and unconscious beings with the flute,

children.text: tāḥ kraṣṭuṃ suṣṭhu nāśaknod yatas tā lajjayā sitāḥ ||63||
children.translated_text: could not properly draw those [gopīs], because they were bound by shyness.

children.text: 1. (b) sarvāṅgo; 2. missing from (b); 3. (b) niṣkrāntā; 4. (b) śubhadra; 5. BRS iii.3.23; 6. (b) odhyānaniṣṭhikāḥ; 7. BhaviṣyaP iv (cf. KS p112); 8yaḥ śrī-bhāṇḍīra-nāmānaṃ baṭaṃ śaśvad aṭann adhāt |
children.translated_text: [Textual notes and variant readings]

children.text: nānā-krīḍāṃ sa-nīḍānām adabhraṃ bibhrad utsavam ||64||
children.translated_text: He who, constantly roaming near the banyan tree named Śrī <s>Bhāṇḍīra</s>, established it [as a sacred site], abundantly bearing the celebration of various sports with nests [of birds].

children.text: yaḥ śrīdāmnā sudāmnā ca bhadrasenārjunādibhiḥ |
children.translated_text: He who, with <s>Śrīdāma</s>, <s>Sudāma</s>, <s>Bhadrasena</s>, <s>Arjuna</s>, and others,

children.text: khelā-dambha-balāc cakre tat-pralamba-pralambhanam ||65||
children.translated_text: through the mock-strength of play, accomplished the defeat of the [demon] <s>Pralamba</s> through deception.

children.text: yaḥ pralambaṃ lambamānaṃ jīvanād bala-tejasā |
children.translated_text: He who, having reduced <s>Pralamba</s>, who was hanging [from <s>Balarāma</s>], from life by the splendor of <s>Bala</s> (Balarāma),

children.text: vidhāya vidadhe tīvrān1 navaśaktiṃ davīyasīm ||67||
children.translated_text: thereby established a fierce new power far beyond [the ordinary].

children.text: yaḥ kānane sudīrghāhe nidāghe kṛta-kelikaḥ |
aparāhṇe preyasīnām ānandaṃ vidadhe yathā |68||
children.translated_text: in the afternoon, created joy for his beloveds in such a manner —
He who, in the forest during the long hot days of summer, having performed his sports,

children.text: gopīnāṃ paramānandam āsīd govinda-darśane |
children.translated_text: the supreme bliss of the <s>gopīs</s> was in the sight of <s>Govinda</s>;

children.text: kṣaṇaṃ yuga-śatam iva yāsāṃ yena vinābhavat2 ||69||
children.translated_text: for whom a moment without him was like a hundred <s>yugas</s> (ages).

children.text: pūrvavad yugmakam
children.translated_text: A pair of verses as before

children.text: yaḥ sadā dṛṣṭi-kṛd vṛṣṭi-varṣā-rūpa-niśā-kṣaye |
children.translated_text: He who, always creating a shower of glances, at the passing of the rainy season's nights,

children.text: śaradaṃ prātar āsādya priyāṇām ahṛtāndhatām ||70||
children.translated_text: reaching autumn in the morning, stole the blindness [of darkness] from his beloveds.

children.text: yaḥ śrīgovardhanapremasvapremadhanajīviṣu |
children.translated_text: He who, among his own kinsmen who lived by the love of Śrī <s>Govardhana</s> and the wealth of his own love,

children.text: sva-gotreṣv api sañcāryānyān apy āryān aśikṣayat ||71||
children.translated_text: taught even noble others the moving [nature of devotion].

children.text: yaḥ śrī-govardhanaṃ bibhrac chakra-vibhraṣṭa-garvatām |
children.translated_text: He who, lifting Śrī <s>Govardhana</s>, led <s>Śakra</s> (Indra), whose pride was shattered,

children.text: ninye goṣṭhaṃ yad unninye śreṣṭhaṃ sva-preṣṭhajātiṣu ||72||
children.translated_text: to [a state of] fallen arrogance; [and] elevated the cowherd settlement to the highest among his own dear [devotees].

children.text: śrī-govindatāṃ vindann avindad viśva-nanditām |
children.translated_text: He who, attaining the state of <s>Śrī Govinda</s>, found universal delight,

children.text: yan mithaḥ śakra-jantūnāṃ naitryāvyadhita śambhutām ||73||
children.translated_text: whose mutual friendship among <s>Indra</s>'s creatures did not disturb his auspicious nature. ||73||

children.text: yaḥ pāśi-lokād ānīya pitaraṃ mātṛ-jīvanam |
children.translated_text: He who, bringing his father from the realm of <s>Pāśī</s> (the Noose-bearer, i.e., <s>Varuṇa</s>), the life of his mother,

children.text: ajīvayad vrajaṃ sarvaṃ taṃ vinā gata-jīvanam ||74||
children.translated_text: revived all of <s>Vraja</s>, which without him had lost its life. ||74||

children.text: yaḥ svānāṃ vraja-lokānāṃ hṛdokās tān viśokayan |
children.translated_text: He who, dwelling in the hearts of his own people of <s>Vraja</s>, removing their sorrows,

children.text: teṣāṃ svasya ca golokaṃ nitya-lokam alokayat ||75||
children.translated_text: revealed to them and to himself <s>Goloka</s>, the eternal world. ||75||

children.text: yaś citta-vāsasī nītvā kumārīṇāṃ paraṃ dade |
children.translated_text: He who, having taken the garments of the maidens, bestowed the supreme [gift],

children.text: na pūrvaṃ yena tā baddhāḥ sambaddhā nityam ātmani ||76||
children.translated_text: by which those who were not previously bound became forever bound to him. ||76||

children.text: yaḥ sva-vaṃśikayā moha-bādhitāṃ rādhikām anu |
children.translated_text: He who, through his own flute, regarding <s>Rādhikā</s> afflicted by bewilderment,

children.text: pūrṇāḥ pulindya ity3ādi vṛttaṃ vṛttaṃ vinirmame ||77||
children.translated_text: composed the episode beginning with 'the <s>Pulinda</s> women are fulfilled' — episode after episode. ||77||

children.text: yaḥ sakhīn akhilāgrīyān grīṣmāntaḥ prema-sampadā |
children.translated_text: He who, at the end of summer, with the wealth of <s>prema</s> (divine love), called

children.text: saṃmadād ājuhāvāmūn kramād evaṃ mudāṃ pradaḥ ||78||
children.translated_text: all his foremost companions in order, thus bestowing joy: ||78||

children.text: he stokakṛṣṇa he aṃśo śrīdāman subalārjuna |
children.translated_text: 'O <s>Stokakṛṣṇa</s>! O <s>Aṃśu</s>! O <s>Śrīdāman</s>! <s>Subala</s>! <s>Arjuna</s>!

children.text: viśāla vṛṣabhaujasvin devaprastha varūthapa4 ||79||
children.translated_text: <s>Viśāla</s>! <s>Vṛṣabha</s>! <s>Ojasvin</s>! <s>Devaprastha</s>! <s>Varūthapa</s>!' ||79||

children.text: evam āhūya bhūyas tān narma-sūnṛta-gīr vṛtam |
children.translated_text: Having thus called them, he again spoke to those surrounded by affectionate and truthful words,

children.text: āha vṛndāvana-sthānāṃ sthāvarāṇāṃ varāṃ gatim ||80||
children.translated_text: about the excellent destination of the immovable beings dwelling in <s>Vṛndāvana</s>. ||80||

children.text: pūrvavat tribhiḥ
children.translated_text: As before, with three verses.

children.text: yas tāsāṃ yajña-patnīnāṃ mahima-sneha-vṛddhaye |
children.translated_text: He who, to increase the glory and affection of those wives of the <s>yajña</s> (sacrifice),

children.text: bubhukṣāṃ sakhibhir vyañjann anna-bhikṣāṃ1 vinirmame ||81||
children.translated_text: displaying hunger along with his companions, contrived to beg for food. ||81||

children.text: yas tatrāśoka-vanyāyāṃ dhanyāyāṃ sakhibhiḥ saha |
children.translated_text: He who, playing in that blessed, grief-free grove with his companions,

children.text: krīḍan nirvarṇitas tābhiḥ śyāmam ityādi2 varṇitaḥ ||82||
children.translated_text: was observed by those [<s>gopīs</s>] and described beginning with 'dark-complexioned' and so on. ||82||

children.text: yaḥ sadā narma-śarmārthī madhumaṅgala-nāminam |
children.translated_text: He who, always seeking the joy of merriment, engaging

children.text: narma-mantriṇam āsajya bhojyan mitrāṇy arañjayat ||83||
children.translated_text: the one named <s>Madhumaṅgala</s> as his minister of mirth, delighted his friends with feasting. ||83||

children.text: yaḥ sva-jīvana-jīvānāṃ cātakīnām ivāmbudaḥ |
children.translated_text: He who, like a rain-cloud for <s>cātakī</s> birds whose life depends on him,

children.text: sva-jīvanena tādātmyam akarod vraja-subhruvām ||84||
children.translated_text: created identity with the beautiful-browed women of <s>Vraja</s> through his own life. ||84||

children.text: yaḥ pareṣāṃ hrepaṇatāṃ śakti-saṅkhyālpatāṃ vidan |
children.translated_text: He who, knowing the humiliation and the limited powers of others,

children.text: guptāgaṇya-svakāntāsu vaṃśī-dūtīm amanyata ||85||
children.translated_text: regarded his flute as the messenger to his secretly innumerable beloveds. ||85||

children.text: yaś cirād eva muralī-śikṣāyāṃ vīkṣya pūrṇatām |
children.translated_text: He who, having long perceived the perfection in his flute's training,

children.text: tayā mādya-priyās tūrṇaṃ pūrṇaṃ mene svam añjasā ||86||
children.translated_text: through her, considered himself complete at once, being dear to the intoxicated ones. ||86||

children.text: yas tyāga-vyāja-bhṛn-narma vyājahāra priyāḥ prati |
children.translated_text: He who, bearing the pretext of renunciation as sport, jested with his beloveds,

children.text: pratinarma-priyā-vṛndād vindan śarmānvavindata ||87||
children.translated_text: and from the group of beloveds fond of counter-jesting, found bliss upon bliss. ||87||

children.text: yaḥ sadā yoga-māyākhyāṃ śaktim āsaktitaḥ śritaḥ |
children.translated_text: He who always lovingly relied upon the power called <s>Yogamāyā</s>,

children.text: paurṇamāsīm iti nāmāsīd vraje yāsīt tapasvinī ||88||
children.translated_text: whose name was <s>Paurṇamāsī</s>, who was the ascetic woman residing in <s>Vraja</s>. ||88||

children.text: yas tayā divyayā śaktyānantadhānanta-subhruvām |
children.translated_text: He who, through that divine power, bearing infinitely many beautiful-browed women,

children.text: bibhrad vinā sa-narmādi-śarmālabhata sarvadā ||89||
children.translated_text: without [effort], attained the bliss of playful love at all times. ||89||

children.text: yaḥ kṛtvā rāsa-khelāyāṃ mudaṃ dvandvaṃ punar mudam |
children.translated_text: He who, having created joy in the <s>Rāsa</s> dance, [formed] pairs, and then more joy,

children.text: kheleyam iti tad vyañjann amumudad amūḥ priyāḥ ||90||
children.translated_text: manifesting 'Let me play!' — delighted those beloved ones. ||90||

children.text: yas tyajann api tāḥ sarvāḥ parvātanuta kutracit |
children.translated_text: He who, even while abandoning all of them, extended the festival somewhere,

children.text: apy eṇa-patnīty-ādyaṃ3 yat tatra karṇāmṛtaṃ matam ||91||
children.translated_text: and that [passage] beginning with 'even the doe-wives' is considered a nectar for the ears. ||91||

children.text: yas tāsāṃ jayatīty4 ādi vilāpād vyagratāṃ gataḥ |
children.translated_text: He who, becoming distressed by their lamentation beginning with 'victory to you!',

children.text: tāsām āvirabhūd5 evaṃ sudhībhir adhivarṇitaḥ ||92||
children.translated_text: manifested himself to them — thus he has been described by the wise. ||92||

children.text: yāsāṃ stana-kāśmīra-śasta-vastrāsanaṃ gataḥ |
children.translated_text: He who, having taken as his seat the garments anointed with the saffron from their breasts,

children.text: rarāja tāra-kārāja-rājat-pulina-dhāmani ||93||
children.translated_text: shone resplendent upon the brilliant sandy bank radiant as a cluster of stars. ||93||

children.text: yaḥ prahelikayā tāsāṃ sva-parājayam āmṛśan |
children.translated_text: He who, through enigmatic speech, touching upon his own defeat before them,

children.text: na pāraye 'ham ity6 ādi rītyā svaṃ matavān ṛṇī ||94||
children.translated_text: by the manner of 'I am unable' and so forth, considered himself a debtor. ||94||

children.text: yaḥ śyāmaḥ svarṇa-gaurībhiḥ parāṃ śobhāṃ yayau yathā |
children.translated_text: He who, dark-complexioned among golden-fair women, attained supreme beauty — as

children.text: tatrātiśuśubhe rājann bhagavān iti7 sat-prathā ||95||
children.translated_text: the celebrated saying goes: 'There the Blessed Lord shone exceedingly, O King.' ||95||

children.text:
yas tāsāṃ sva-vihāreṇa śrāntānāṃ mukha-paṅkajam |
prāmṛjat karuṇaḥ premnā śantamenāṅga-pāṇinā ||96||8
yaḥ krīḍan vāri-vanayor vikrīḍa9 iva tāḥ punaḥ |
children.translated_text: He who, playing in water and groves, sporting again with them,

children.text: anunīya vinirṇīya sva-saṅgaṃ nilayaṃ gataḥ ||97||
children.translated_text: having consoled and guided them, went to his abode with their company. ||97||
He who, compassionate, with love wiped the lotus-faces of those wearied by his own pastimes, with his gentle hand. ||96||

children.text: 1. (a) vyañjann anna-bhikṣā; (b) vyañjan anna-bhikṣām; 2. BhP x.23.22; 3. BhP x.30.11; 4. BhP x.31.1; 5. BhP x.32.2; 6. BhP x.32.22; 7. BhP x.33.6; 8. BhP x.33.21; 9. (b) cikrīḍa yas tīrtha-vyājam avrājīd vrajena vanam āmbikam |
children.translated_text: 1. (a) vyañjann anna-bhikṣā; (b) vyañjan anna-bhikṣām; 2. BhP x.23.22; 3. BhP x.30.11; 4. BhP x.31.1; 5. BhP x.32.2; 6. BhP x.32.22; 7. BhP x.33.6; 8. BhP x.33.21; 9. (b) cikrīḍa

children.text: yatrāśeṣeṇa veśena cchalayāmāsa cābalāḥ ||98||
children.translated_text: He who went to the <s>Āmbikā</s> forest from <s>Vraja</s> under the pretext of a <s>tīrtha</s> (pilgrimage), and there completely deceived the women with [various] disguises. ||98||

children.text: yaḥ sarva-jīvanaṃ jīvaṃ vitaran pitaraṃ prati |
children.translated_text: He who, bestowing life-giving vitality upon his father,

children.text: padāsarpan spṛśan sarpaṃ muneḥ śāpād apākarot ||99||
children.translated_text: stepping upon and touching the serpent, removed the curse of the sage. ||99||

children.text: yaḥ sudarśanatāṃ ninye mahā-sarpaṃ kudarśanam |
children.translated_text: He who transformed the ugly great serpent into one of beautiful appearance,

children.text: kāruṇya-kāruḥ kañcāraṃ1 na cakārāpi dāruṇam ||100||
children.translated_text: the artisan of compassion, did not commit even a bit of cruelty. ||100||

children.text: yaḥ pūrvaṃ nirmame horī-parvaṃ yakṣasya dhūrvaṇam2 |
children.translated_text: He who previously created the <s>Holī</s> festival as the crushing of the <s>Yakṣa</s>,

children.text: antaryāmivat tan3 manye tādṛggrāmīṇaparvasu ||101||
children.translated_text: as if the Inner Controller — I think [he did so] on such village festivals. ||101||

children.text: yaḥ prātar-ādi-jāḥ krīḍāḥ kurvaṃs tāsu sphurann api |
children.translated_text: He who, performing the sports arising from morning onward, though manifesting in those,

children.text: ślokānāṃ yugma-saṅghena ślokitas tābhir anvaham ||102||
children.translated_text: was praised daily by them with assemblages of paired verses. ||102||

children.text: yaḥ śrī-govardhane rāsa-vardhanecchā-vivardhaneyaḥ |
children.translated_text: He who, upon <s>Śrī Govardhana</s>, with the desire for the enhancement of the <s>Rāsa</s> ever increasing,

children.text: saṃgamya preyasī-saṅghaṃ narma-saṅgara-raṅgavān ||103||
children.translated_text: having assembled with the company of his beloveds, was full of the arena of playful combat. ||103||

children.text: goṣṭha-prakoṣṭhataḥ kruṣṭaṃ śrutvāriṣṭa-kṛtaṃ kaṭu |
children.translated_text: Having heard the harsh cry made by <s>Ariṣṭa</s> from the courtyard of the cowshed,

children.text: tatra saṃgatya saṃyatya taṃ nihatya mudaṃ gataḥ ||104||
children.translated_text: he went there, met him, subdued him, slew him, and attained joy. ||104||

children.text: punaḥ śīghraṃ giriṃ gacchan saṅginībhiḥ sabhaṅgibhiḥ |
children.translated_text: Again, swiftly going to the hill with his consorts who moved gracefully,

children.text: rāsam ullāsayāmāsa bhāsayāmāsa cākhilam ||105||
children.translated_text: he made the <s>Rāsa</s> dance overflow with delight and illuminated everything. ||105||

children.text: pūrvavat tribhiḥ
children.translated_text: As before, with three verses.

children.text: yaḥ kuṇḍaṃ puṇḍarīkākṣas tan nirmāya sunarma-kṛt |
children.translated_text: He, the lotus-eyed One, having constructed the lake (<s>kuṇḍa</s>), that maker of beautiful sport,

children.text: śrī-rādhikāṃ dhanyam anyat kārayāmāsa sāra-bhṛt ||106||
children.translated_text: the essence-bearer, caused <s>Śrī Rādhikā</s> to make another blessed [lake]. ||106||

children.text: kaṃseneśinaṃ4 goṣṭha-kleśinaṃ vāji-veśinam |
children.translated_text: He who made the one who vexed the cowshed, the one in horse-disguise, sent by <s>Kaṃsa</s> —

children.text: keśine5 keśinaṃ cakre yamasya prativeśinam ||107||
children.translated_text: <s>Keśī</s>, the maned one — a neighbor of <s>Yama</s> (the god of death). ||107||

children.text: yaḥ pitrādy-anurāgeṇa citrābhaḥ sarva-vismṛtiḥ |
children.translated_text: He who, with his radiant affection for his father and others, in complete self-forgetfulness,

children.text: kaṃsaṃ dhvaṃsakam apy ārcchān na hantuṃ gantu-kāmatām ||108||
children.translated_text: did not desire to go even to destroy <s>Kaṃsa</s>, the destroyer. ||108||

children.text: yaḥ snigdha-smitayā dṛṣṭyā vācā pīyūṣa-kalpayā |
children.translated_text: He who, with an affectionate smiling glance, with speech like nectar,

children.text: caritreṇānavadyena śrī-niketena cātmanā ||109||
children.translated_text: with irreproachable conduct, and with his own self as the abode of <s>Śrī</s> (beauty), ||109||

children.text: imaṃ lokam amuñcābhiramayan sutarāṃ vrajam |
children.translated_text: not leaving this world, delighted it exceedingly, especially <s>Vraja</s>,

children.text: reme kṣaṇadayā datta-kṣaṇa-strī-kṣaṇa-sauhṛdaḥ ||110||
children.translated_text: and sported as one whose friendship with women was given momentarily by the night. ||110||

children.text: pūrvavad yugmakam
children.translated_text: As before, a pair of verses.

children.text: yas tathā saha gopībhiś cikrīḍa vrajarājajaḥ |
children.translated_text: He, the prince of <s>Vraja</s>, sported with the <s>gopīs</s> in such a way

children.text: yathābda-koṭi-pratimaḥ kṣaṇas tena vinābhavat7 ||111||
children.translated_text: that a single moment without him seemed like ten million years. ||111||

children.text: yaḥ kāntā-mukha-candrāṇāṃ bhāsā bhāsini8 dig-gaṇe |
children.translated_text: He who, when the directions shone with the radiance of the moon-faces of his beloveds,

children.text: rāga-sāgara-nirmagnaś calituṃ nāpi ca kṣamaḥ ||112||
children.translated_text: being submerged in the ocean of passion (<s>rāga</s>), was not even able to stir. ||112||

children.text: kiñcit tad-vyakti-vātāli-lajjā-vīci-vicālitaḥ |
children.translated_text: But slightly agitated by the waves of modesty [stirred by] the breezes of their self-expression,

children.text: kaṃsa-ghātamiṣāpāta-nijecchābhāsam āgataḥ ||113||
children.translated_text: he arrived at an appearance of his own wish to depart, under the pretext of slaying <s>Kaṃsa</s>. ||113||

children.text: 1. (a) kañjāraṃ, (b) kaṃ cāriṃ; 2. (b) dharṣaṇam; 3. (a) antaryāmīva tano; 4. (b) kaṃseneśitam; 5. (b) veśinaṃ; 6. not found in (b); 7. vip v.23.57; 8. (b) bhāsinam
children.translated_text: 1. (a) kañjāraṃ, (b) kaṃ cāriṃ; 2. (b) dharṣaṇam; 3. (a) antaryāmīva tano; 4. (b) kaṃseneśitam; 5. (b) veśinaṃ; 6. not found in (b); 7. vip v.23.57; 8. (b) bhāsinam

children.text: taṭasthatām aṭann urīcakre madhuparīgatim |
children.translated_text: Remaining aloof, he accepted the journey to <s>Mathurā</s>;

children.text: āḥ kiṃ vācyā vraje yācyā prāṇimātre tanoḥ sthitiḥ ||114||
children.translated_text: Alas! What more can be said? In <s>Vraja</s>, one could beg every living creature for the body's sustenance. ||114||

children.text: pūrvavat tribhiḥ
children.translated_text: As before, with three verses.

children.text: yaḥ svāṃs tattadguṇaḥ sarvān alaṃ hātuṃ na te ca yam |
children.translated_text: He who, possessing such and such qualities, was fully capable of leaving all his own, yet they could not [leave] him;

children.text: āstāṃ vraje premaśūrā dūrād eva tathā kathā ||115||
children.translated_text: let alone in <s>Vraja</s>, where the heroes of <s>prema</s> (love) are — even from afar, the story is the same. ||115||

children.text: yaḥ pṛthvyā prathamaskandhe dharmāgrevarṇitān guṇān |1
children.translated_text: He whose qualities, described at the beginning of the first book (<s>skandha</s>) of [the <s>Bhāgavata</s>] on earth as foremost in <s>dharma</s>,

children.text: nityam āptas tathātrāpi varṇyaḥ sann avakarṇyatām ||116||
children.translated_text: are eternally attained — even here being worthy of description, let them be heard. ||116||

children.text: sarvānandapradānandakandas tadvadguṇāvaliḥ |
children.translated_text: He is the root of bliss that bestows all joy; likewise is his garland of qualities;

children.text: sarvaparvadamāhātmyād varaḥ sarvata īśvaraḥ ||117||
children.translated_text: by the greatness of his glory at every festival, he is supreme, the Lord of all. ||117||

children.text: sarvadā vṛddhibhāgṛddhiḥ sarvārādhanabhūdhanam |
children.translated_text: His prosperity ever increases in all ways; he is the treasure for all worship;

children.text: svarūparūpasādguṇyapuṇyakṛt karmaśarmadaḥ ||118||
children.translated_text: he creates merit through the excellence of his essential form and beauty, and bestows happiness through [his] actions. ||118||

children.text: dṛṣṭiḥ pratisudhāvṛṣṭiprabhasundaratāprabhaḥ2 |
children.translated_text: His glance is radiant with beauty like a shower of nectar;

children.text: varṇānāṃ syandadiṅmātrāt3 karṇānandakarasvaraḥ4 ||119||
children.translated_text: his voice delights the ears by the mere flow of syllables in all directions. ||119||

children.text: aśvāsānām api śvāsakārisaurabhagauravaḥ |
children.translated_text: Even for the breathless, his fragrance is such that it causes [them to] breathe — so great is its majesty;

children.text: adharaspṛṣṭanīrādisṛṣṭaśrīrasanārasaḥ ||120||
children.translated_text: the beauty of his lips touching the nectar and other [substances] creates the essence of taste. ||120||

children.text: svasparśisparśanāsparśād viśvatāpāpayāpanaḥ |
children.translated_text: By the mere touch of one who touches him — without touching — he removes the heat of the entire world;

children.text: jagataḥ śucitādhāma nāmadhāmasmṛtīḍitaḥ ||121||
children.translated_text: he is the abode of purity for the world, praised by the remembrance of his name and abode. ||121||

children.text: anantasaccidānandajyotirdyotikalevaraḥ |
children.translated_text: His body illuminates the light of infinite being, consciousness, and bliss (<s>saccidānanda</s>);

children.text: vapuraṃśukayor aṃśusampad viṣṇuramājayī ||122||
children.translated_text: in the splendor of [his] body and garments, he conquers even <s>Viṣṇu</s> in radiance. ||122||

children.text: jagaddūṣaṇaśobhābhṛd vibhūṣaṇavibhūṣaṇaḥ |
children.translated_text: He who adorns the beauty that embellishes the world, the ornament of ornaments;

children.text: tūrṇaṃ yathāruci vyāpirucidhāryaguṇākṛtiḥ ||123||
children.translated_text: swiftly, according to his pleasure, he assumes all-pervading beauty and qualities of form. ||123||

children.text: lakṣmīdṛkpakṣma5viṣkambhilakṣmalakṣitavigrahaḥ |
children.translated_text: His body is marked with auspicious signs that arrest the glance of <s>Lakṣmī</s>;

children.text: śaṅkhacakrādicihnaśrīdurnihnavanijasthitiḥ ||124||
children.translated_text: the beauty of [his] insignia — conch, discus, and the rest — is difficult to conceal, like the nature of a merchant. ||124||

children.text: jetuṃ svam apy aviśrāntaṃ śaśvadvalgu6balāvaliḥ |
children.translated_text: His unceasing array of charming powers [strives] to conquer even himself;

children.text: kiśoratāmanaḥsāracoratāviśvamohanaḥ ||125||
children.translated_text: his adolescence, the essence stealing the mind, is the enchanter of the entire world. ||125||

children.text: vilāsahāsalīlāsyakṛtalāsyakalājayaḥ |
children.translated_text: He who conquers all arts through the graceful play of coquetry, laughter, <s>līlā</s> (divine sport), and dancing;

children.text: vikārarahitākāraḥ sphuratpremavikāravān ||126||
children.translated_text: his form is free from [material] transformation, yet overflowing with the transformations of <s>prema</s> (love). ||126||

children.text: purāpi nava ity evaṃ purāṇādiviniścitaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Ever ancient, yet ever new' — thus determined by the <s>Purāṇas</s> and other [scriptures];

children.text: anūtanatanūḥ7 śrīmān sadā nūtanavattanuḥ ||127||
children.translated_text: the glorious one whose body is ever un-old, yet always appears as if new. ||127||

children.text: sarveṣāṃ manasaḥ kartuṃ pramanas tāṃ sphuranmanāḥ |
children.translated_text: Capable of captivating the minds of all, his mind shining forth,

children.text: vaidagdhīdigdhasadvṛddhi8cāturīpracurīkaraḥ ||128||
children.translated_text: he who abundantly spreads the cleverness anointed with true skill and growth. ||128||

children.text: viśveṣāṃ buddhikṛd buddhiḥ siddhīnām api siddhikṛt |
children.translated_text: The intelligence of all intelligences, the perfector of all <s>siddhis</s> (perfections);

children.text: dakṣatālakṣaśikṣākṛd dakṣatābhir vilakṣaṇaḥ ||129||
children.translated_text: the instructor of a hundred thousand skills of dexterity, distinguished by his dexterities. ||129||

children.text: tucchopakāritābindusindhukārī kṛtajñataḥ |
children.translated_text: Out of gratitude, he who transforms even a drop of trifling service into an ocean;

children.text:
1. BhP i.16.27||-30||; 2. (b) oprabhā; 3. (b) diṅmātrao; 4 (a) karaṇānanda(?); 5 (b) pakṣa; 6 (a) ovalgād; 7. (b) tanuḥ; 8. (b) obuddhio
sudṛḍhavratatāvrātatrātaśaśvadanuvrataḥ ||130||
children.translated_text: of firmly kept vows, ever faithful to those who are devoted — constantly devoted in return. ||130||

children.text: nijamaryādayā baddhaśrutimaryādaceṣṭitaḥ |
children.translated_text: His conduct is bound by his own propriety, which sets the standard for the <s>Śrutis</s> (scriptures);

children.text: ceṣṭitaṃ1 tāvad āstāṃ tad dṛṣṭamātras tathā guṇaḥ ||131||
children.translated_text: let his conduct be set aside — such is his quality even merely upon being seen. ||131||

children.text: yajñajñaḥ kāladeśādiprajñaḥ sarvajñaśekharaḥ |
children.translated_text: Knower of <s>yajña</s> (sacrifice), knower of time, place, and the rest; the crest-jewel of the omniscient;

children.text: sarvajñatām avajñāya prajñatātarkitākhilaḥ ||132||
children.translated_text: disregarding omniscience, he who comprehends all through wisdom beyond logic. ||132||

children.text: dhīratā sthiratā śobhi vīratā niratāntaraḥ |
children.translated_text: Resplendent with steadfastness, constancy, and heroism, devoted without interruption;

children.text: kṣāntyā dāntyā ca śāntyā ca saha kāntyā svayaṃ vṛtaḥ ||133||
children.translated_text: he is himself attended by forbearance, self-control, peace, and radiance. ||133||

children.text: dharmadānanidānaśrīḥ śūraḥ2 suratamānasaḥ |
children.translated_text: He whose glory is the foundation of <s>dharma</s> and generosity; heroic, with a mind delighting in love;

children.text: mānyasāmānyavardhiṣṇumānyatākriyatāpriyaḥ3 ||134||
children.translated_text: he who loves to honor the honorable and increase the esteem of the estimable. ||134||

children.text: akṣīṇavinayaḥ suṣṭhu lajjitaḥ kūṭavarjitaḥ |
children.translated_text: Of undiminished modesty, thoroughly humble, free from deceit;

children.text: kīrtipratāpapūrtibhyāṃ kṛtasallokajūrtikaḥ ||135||
children.translated_text: through fame, valor, and abundance, he creates a stir throughout the world. ||135||

children.text: sādhūnāṃ mādhurīdānān nityaṃ sādhusamāśrayaḥ |
children.translated_text: Through the gift of sweetness to the saintly, he is always the refuge of the virtuous;

children.text: dviṣāṃ ca muktikṛn muktibhāgākarṣiguṇāmbudhiḥ ||136||
children.translated_text: he who grants liberation even to enemies — an ocean of qualities that attract those worthy of liberation. ||136||

children.text: nānābhāṣālisambhāṣo deva4paryantadevanaḥ |
children.translated_text: Conversant in many languages, playful up to the gods themselves;

children.text: pratyagvādiny api prīti5satyatāsphuradīritaḥ ||137||
children.translated_text: even when speaking contrarily, the truth of his affection shines in his utterance. ||137||

children.text: vāvadūkaḥ6 sudhīmūkasthitikārisudhīdharaḥ |
children.translated_text: Eloquent, yet maintaining the composure of the wise who remain silent;

children.text: dṛṣṭamātratayā sarvabudhatāṃ7 budhatāguruḥ ||138||
children.translated_text: a teacher of intelligence who awakens all understanding by mere sight. ||138||

children.text: yogyānām api yogyāśī8 raṅkāṅām api śaṅkaraḥ |
children.translated_text: The wisher of well-being even for the worthy, the benefactor (<s>Śaṅkara</s>) even for the wretched;

children.text: śaraṇāgatarakṣāyāḥ śaraṇaṃ śarmakarmaṭhaḥ ||139||
children.translated_text: the refuge and the diligent bestower of happiness for the protection of those who take shelter. ||139||

children.text: na ca bhaktiṃ vināsakti9binduḥ sindhuvad antaraḥ |
children.translated_text: Without devotion, not even a drop of attachment — [yet he is] like an ocean for the sincere;

children.text: samaḥ sarvatra bhaktānāṃ bhakta ity apy asau samaḥ ||140||
children.translated_text: equal everywhere, yet among devotees he is equally called 'a devotee.' ||140||

children.text: bhaktānāṃ bhaktatānandī premasthemavaśīkṛtaḥ |
children.translated_text: He delights in the devotion of his devotees, controlled by the firmness of <s>prema</s> (love);

children.text: tattadrūpaguṇakrīḍākṛtasvāvadhivismayaḥ ||141||
children.translated_text: he is astonished beyond his own limits by the play of their various forms and qualities. ||141||

children.text: snehābhiṣekād viśveṣāṃ prājyasāmrājyapūjitaḥ |
children.translated_text: Through the anointing of affection by all, he is worshipped with abundant sovereignty;

children.text: sarvatra snehapīyūṣavarṣinityanavambudaḥ ||142||
children.translated_text: he is the ever-new rain-cloud showering the nectar of love everywhere. ||142||

children.text: goṣṭhavṛndāṭavīśaṃsivaṃśīgānamadhūnmadaḥ |
children.translated_text: Intoxicated by the honeyed song of the flute praising <s>Vṛndāvana</s> forest and the cowshed;

children.text: nijapriyāvalībhāgyaspṛhiviṣṇupriyārcitaḥ ||143||
children.translated_text: worshipped by <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s consorts who envy the fortune of his own row of beloveds. ||143||

children.text: kiṃ bahūktena sūktena sūktena śrūyatām idam |
children.translated_text: What use of many words, even well-spoken ones? Let this [well-said truth] be heard:

children.text: kṛṣṇa eva hi kṛṣṇaḥ syāt kṛṣṇaḥ syāt kṛṣṇa eva hi ||144||
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> alone is indeed <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>; <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> alone can be <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> indeed. ||144||

children.text: pūrvavad ekonatriṃśabhiḥ
children.translated_text: As before, with twenty-nine verses.

children.text: yas tādṛgguṇavān goṣṭhaṃ nātyantaṃ tyaktum arhati |
children.translated_text: He who, possessing such qualities, is not able to utterly abandon the cowshed,

children.text: tādṛgguṇānvayipremnā tasya baddhaś ca tad yathā ||145||
children.translated_text: and is bound by the love of those following such qualities — that is as follows: ||145||

children.text: dustyajaś cānurāgo 'smin sarveṣāṃ no vrajaukasām |
children.translated_text: The attachment of all of us, the residents of <s>Vraja</s>, to him is indeed difficult to abandon;

children.text: yaḥ sajjan kāliyakroḍaṃ vrajaṃ sajjantam āmtani |
children.translated_text: he who, entering the coils of <s>Kāliya</s>, [saved] <s>Vraja</s> which was clinging [to life]

children.text: nanda te tanaye 'smāsu tasyāpy autpattikaḥ katham? ||1461
children.translated_text: O <s>Nanda</s>, how could the innate [love] in your son toward us [arise]? ||146||

children.text: pūrvavad eva yugmakam
children.translated_text: A couplet as before

children.text: 1. (b) ceṣṭataḥ; 2. (b) śūrao; 3. (b) oparaḥ; 4. (a) osambhāṣād eva; 5. (b) prītiḥ; 6. (b) vāvadūkao; 7. (b) budhatāo; 8. (a) yogyāśā; 9. (a) vināsaktiṃ
children.translated_text: 1. (b) ceṣṭataḥ; 2. (b) śūrao; 3. (b) oparaḥ; 4. (a) osambhāṣād eva; 5. (b) prītiḥ; 6. (b) vāvadūkao; 7. (b) budhatāo; 8. (a) yogyāśā; 9. (a) vināsaktiṃ [variant readings]

children.text: vimṛśann unmamajja drāg varṣan harṣaṃ jagaty api ||147
children.translated_text: He who, reflecting, quickly emerged, showering joy upon the world as well. ||147||

children.text: yaḥ śakre vakratāṃ paśyan premnā yan vrajavaśyatām |
children.translated_text: He who, seeing crookedness in <s>Śakra</s> (Indra), and going with love to the control of <s>Vraja</s>,

children.text: hṛdy arthaṃ tam imaṃ vidvān atra vyānag yathārthatām ||148
children.translated_text: the wise one, discerning the inner meaning, expressed here [its] true significance. ||148||

children.text: tasmān maccharaṇaṃ goṣṭaṃ mannāthaṃ matparigraham |
children.translated_text: 'Therefore my refuge is the cow-pasture, my lord is [its lord], my possession [is Vraja].'

children.text: gopāye svātmayogena so 'yaṃ me vrata āhitaḥ ||149*fn
children.translated_text: 'I protect [it] through the yoga of my own self — this is the vow established by me.' ||149||

children.text: pūrvavad eva yugmakam
children.translated_text: A couplet as before

children.text: yaḥ saṅkalpaṃ vyadhād evaṃkiñca bhūdharadhāraṇam |
children.translated_text: He who made such a resolve — moreover, the lifting of the mountain (<s>Govardhana</s>) —

children.text: saptatarāpy ahorātrām stanmātraṅgīkṛtisthitiḥ ||150||
children.translated_text: for seven days and nights, standing with it held merely by one arm. ||150||

children.text: kiṃ ca yaḥ sakhivatseṣu luñciteṣu viriñcinā |
children.translated_text: Furthermore, he who, when the calves of his friends were stolen by <s>Viriñci</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>),

children.text: sasarjāntyāṃs tadākāran paraṃ svenāpareṇa na ||151||
children.translated_text: created their final forms by himself, by his own [power] and not by another's. ||151||

children.text: tathāpy anirvṛtiṃ gacchaṃs tān āyacchad viriñcitaḥ |
children.translated_text: Yet, not attaining satisfaction, he retrieved them from <s>Viriñci</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>),

children.text: svapremādhikatatpremavaśatām āsadad yataḥ ||152||
children.translated_text: because his own love, being greater than that [manifested] love, came under the sway of the original [forms]. ||152||

children.text: pūrvavad eva yugmakam
children.translated_text: A couplet as before

children.text: yas tān svasmin baka-graste grastehā-prāṇatā-mitān |
children.translated_text: He who, when those [friends] were swallowed by <s>Baka</s> (the crane demon), knowing them to be of such limited life-force,

children.text: sva-mātra-prāṇa-pātrāṅgān vidan vindann api sthitaḥ ||153||
children.translated_text: yet recognizing them as vessels of life equal to himself, remained [undisturbed]. ||153||

children.text: yas teṣv agha-nigīrṇeṣu svayaṃ kīrṇe hatāṃ vrajan |
children.translated_text: He who, when they were devoured by <s>Agha</s> (the serpent demon), himself entering the midst of the destroyed,

children.text: tad-galāntar viśann ātma-nirviśeṣān viveda tān ||154||
children.translated_text: going into the interior of that [demon's] throat, perceived them as non-different from himself. ||154||

children.text: yas tatrāpy adbhutaṃ prema śrīman-nanda-yaśodayoḥ |
children.translated_text: He who, even there, recalled the wondrous love

children.text: dampatyor nitarām āsīd gopa-gopīṣv iti smaran ||155||
children.translated_text: that existed especially between the blessed <s>Nanda</s> and <s>Yaśodā</s> as a couple, and among the <s>gopas</s> and <s>gopīs</s>. ||155||

children.text: sadāpi vedavad veda tad aśeṣavidāṃ varaḥ |
children.translated_text: He, the best among all-knowers, always knows as the <s>Vedas</s> know —

children.text: yad eva śukadevādyā vādyābhaṃ jagur uccakaiḥ ||156||
children.translated_text: that very thing which <s>Śukadeva</s> and others loudly proclaimed as worthy of celebration. ||156||

children.text: pūrvavad yugmakam
children.translated_text: A couplet as before

children.text: yaḥ svīyām ṛṇitāṃ vyaktāṃ tyaktāṃ kartum aśaknuvan |
children.translated_text: He who, unable to make his own indebtedness [to the <s>gopīs</s>] manifest and discharged,

children.text: na pāraye 'ham ity5 ādyaṃ pratijajñe priyāḥ prati ||157||
children.translated_text: made the first declaration to his beloveds: 'I am unable [to repay you].' ||157||

children.text: yaḥ kaṃsādyān dantavakra-prāntān6 sāntān7 vinirmame |
children.translated_text: He who destroyed <s>Kaṃsa</s> and the rest up to <s>Dantavakra</s> and pacified them —

children.text: tad vinā vrajam āgantuṃ śāntiḥ syān8 nety acintayat ||158||
children.translated_text: he reflected, 'Without that, would there be peace for me to come to <s>Vraja</s>? No.' ||158||

children.text: yas tan-madhye samutkaṇṭhām utkaṇṭhāṃ śamayann iva |
children.translated_text: He who, in their midst, as if calming [his own] intense longing,

children.text: svasthān kartuṃ vrajāntaḥ-sthān muhuḥ sāntvanam ādadhe ||159
children.translated_text: repeatedly offered consolation to make those within <s>Vraja</s> at ease. ||159||

children.text: yaḥ sva-prasthāna-samaye "śarīra-sthā imā nahi |
children.translated_text: He who, at the time of his departure, understood: 'These [beloveds] are not merely

children.text: bhaveyur" iti sañjajñe pratijajñe9 nijāgatim ||160||
children.translated_text: situated in [my] body [alone]' — and [thus] promised his own return. ||160||

children.text: 1. BhP x.26||.13; 2. (b) hṛdyārtham; 3. BhP x.25.18; 4. (b) svena pareṇa; 5. BhP x.32||.22; 6. (b) oprāptān; 7. (a) so 'ntān; 8. (a) śāntuḥ syāṃ (?); 9. (a) pratiyajñe;
yas tatra śukadevena drāghita-ślāghitaṃ1 stutaḥ |
children.translated_text: He who was praised by <s>Śukadeva</s> with extensively lauded verses,

children.text: ubhayeṣāṃ prema-sāmyaṃ vyañjatā vyañjitāspadaḥ ||161||
children.translated_text: the one whose abode was revealed by [<s>Śukadeva</s>] who demonstrated the equality of love between both parties. ||161||
1. BhP x.26.13; 2. (b) hṛdyārtham; 3. BhP x.25.18; 4. (b) svena pareṇa; 5. BhP x.32.22; 6. (b) oprāptān; 7. (a) so 'ntān; 8. (a) śāntuḥ syāṃ (?); 9. (a) pratiyajñe [variant readings and references]

children.text:
tās tathā tapyatīr vīkṣya sva-prasthāne yadūttamaḥ |
sāntvayāmāsa sapremair āyasya iti dyotakaiḥ ||162||2
  [pūrvavad yugmakam]
yaḥ kaṃsa-ghnaḥ śaśaṃsedaṃ hari-vaṃśe 'py anūditam3 |
niśvāsā yasya vedāḥ syus tad etat katham anyathā? |163||
children.translated_text: 'He whose exhalations are the <s>Vedas</s>' — how could this be otherwise? ||163||

Seeing them burning thus at his departure, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the best of the <s>Yadus</s>, consoled them with loving words indicating 'I shall come [back].' ||162|| [A couplet as before] He who, the slayer of <s>Kaṃsa</s>, proclaimed this — which is also echoed in the <s>Harivaṃśa</s> —

children.text:
ahaṃ sa eva go-madhye gopaiḥ saha vanecaraḥ |
prītimān vicariṣyāmi kāmacārī yathā gajaḥ ||164||4
pūrvavad yugmakam
children.translated_text: A couplet as before

children.text: yaḥ kaṃse lambhita-dhvaṃse svaṃ vinātivilambitam |
children.translated_text: He who, when the destruction of <s>Kaṃsa</s> was accomplished, [seeing] his father delaying excessively without [returning to] him,

children.text: kurvantaṃ pitaraṃ proce "śoceḥ katham itaḥ pitaḥ ||165
children.translated_text: said to his father: 'Why do you grieve thus, O father? ||165||

children.text:
yāta yūyaṃ vrajaṃ tāta vayaṃ ca sneha-duḥkhitān |
jñātīn vo draṣṭum eṣyāmo vidhāya suhṛdāṃ sukham ||166||5
children.translated_text: 'Go, all of you, to <s>Vraja</s>, O dear father! And we shall come to see our relatives who are distressed by love, having accomplished the welfare of [our] friends.' ||166||

children.text: snehena duḥkhitān ity etat procya snehavastuni |
children.translated_text: Having said 'distressed by love' — by this, regarding the substance of love,

children.text: atṛptiṃ vyānag atrāpi draṣṭum ity eva darśanam ||167||
children.translated_text: he revealed his own insatiability; and here too, 'to see' means seeing alone [is the purpose]. ||167||
'I, that very same one, in the midst of the cows, wandering with the cowherds in the forest, delighted, shall roam freely, like an elephant moving at will.' ||164||

children.text: puruṣārthatayāvocad bhāvikālatayāpi ca |
children.translated_text: He spoke of it as a human purpose (<s>puruṣārtha</s>) and also as pertaining to a future time;

children.text: adṛpter bhāvikālasya cānantyāt tadanantakam ||168||
children.translated_text: because of the insatiability and the infinity of the future time, it [the seeing] too is infinite. ||168||

children.text: tātajñātipadābhyāṃ ca tad yuktam idam uktavān |
children.translated_text: And by the two words 'father' and 'relatives,' this is what he fittingly said:

children.text: suhṛdāṃ sukham ity ākhyāsyate yadvat tathā nahi ||169||
children.translated_text: 'The welfare of friends' — what will be described is not exactly as [it appears]. ||169||

children.text: suhṛcchabdenopakāryopakāritvaṃ pratīyate |
children.translated_text: By the word 'friend' (<s>suhṛd</s>), the relationship of benefactor and beneficiary is understood.

children.text: sukhaṃ ca suhṛdāṃ gamyam upakāramayaṃ param ||170||
children.translated_text: And the happiness of friends is to be understood as entirely consisting of mutual benefit. ||170||

children.text: vidhāyeti ca pūrvasya kālasya cchinnarūpatām |
children.translated_text: By the word 'having accomplished' (<s>vidhāya</s>), indicating the terminable nature of the prior period,

children.text: nirdiśaṃs tadvidhānasya nyadiśat cchinnarūpatām ||171||
children.translated_text: he indicated the terminable nature of that accomplishment [of others' welfare]. ||171||

children.text: tasmāt teṣāṃ śatruvadhaḥ sukhaṃ yat tat samāpsyati |
children.translated_text: Therefore, the slaying of their enemies — whatever happiness that may be — will come to an end;

children.text: jñātīnāṃ snehaśīlānāṃ tat tu vo na samāpsyati ||172||
children.translated_text: but for relatives who are by nature loving, that [happiness of reunion] will not come to an end. ||172||

children.text: iti procyedam avyāñjīt teṣāṃ dhairyapradaṃ6 param |
children.translated_text: Having said this, he expressed what gives them supreme steadfastness:

children.text: māgadhādivadhāntasthaṃ7 svasthatā dhāma yad bhavet ||173||
children.translated_text: the abode of well-being that would come after the slaying of <s>Māgadha</s> (Jarāsandha) and the rest. ||173||

children.text: jarāsandhādiśatrūṇāṃ pratibandhān upekṣya ca |
children.translated_text: Disregarding the obstacles posed by enemies such as <s>Jarāsandha</s> and the rest,

children.text: yady eṣyāmy anusandhānaṃ kuryus tatrāpi te dviṣaḥ ||174||
children.translated_text: 'If I were to come [to Vraja], those enemies would make an attack there too.' ||174||

children.text: sveṣām eva pratijñāya vrajāgamanam īśvaraḥ |
children.translated_text: Having promised the return to <s>Vraja</s> to his own [people], the Lord

children.text: na yūyam atrāyāteti vyajya vyāñjīd idaṃ punaḥ ||175||
children.translated_text: [said:] 'You should not come here' — and having hinted at this, he further expressed: ||175||

children.text: yadi vātra bhavantaḥ syur gamāgamavidhāyinaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Even if you were here, being the arrangers of coming and going,

children.text: tathāpy acchinnamatsnehaṃ jñātvā hanyur vrajaṃ dviṣaḥ ||176||
children.translated_text: even then, knowing my unbroken love [for Vraja], the enemies would attack <s>Vraja</s>.' ||176||

children.text: 1. (b) drāghitaḥ ślāghitaḥ; 2. BhP x.39.35; 3. (b) anuditam; 4. hv 78.35; 5. BhP x.45.23; 6. (b) opradaḥ; 7. (b) osthao
children.translated_text: 1. (b) drāghitaḥ ślāghitaḥ; 2. BhP x.39.35; 3. (b) anuditam; 4. HV 78.35; 5. BhP x.45.23; 6. (b) opradaḥ; 7. (b) osthao [variant readings and references]

children.text: tasmāt tāvad dhīrabhāvaṃ vidhatta vrajasaṃsadi |
children.translated_text: 'Therefore, for now, maintain courageous composure in the assembly of <s>Vraja</s>;

children.text: māṃ ca yuṣmatpriyaṃ nityaṃ lālanaṃ ca samāpsyatha ||177||
children.translated_text: and you shall always obtain me, your beloved, and [my] fondling.' ||177||

children.text: pūrvavan navabhiḥ
children.translated_text: As before, with nine (verses)

children.text: yaḥ saṅgatya guror gehāt pratatya svavrajasmṛtim |
children.translated_text: He who, having returned from the house of the <s>guru</s>, extending his remembrance of his own <s>Vraja</s>,

children.text: prāhiṇod uddhavaṃ vaktuṃ suniścitam idaṃ yathā ||178||
children.translated_text: sent <s>Uddhava</s> to convey this definite [message] as follows: ||178||

children.text:
hatvā kaṃsaṃ raṅgamedhye pratīpaṃ sarvasātvatām |
yad āha vaḥ samāgatya kṛṣṇaḥ satyaṃ karoti tat ||179||1
āgamiṣyaty adīrgheṇa kālena vrajam acyutaḥ |
priyaṃ vidhāsyate pitror bhagavān sātvatāṃ patiḥ ||180||2
pūrvavad tribhiḥ
children.translated_text: As before, with three (verses)

children.text: yaḥ sāsram uddhavaṃ sāsraḥ patis tāsāṃ svayaṃ rahaḥ |
children.translated_text: He who, tearful, the husband of those [<s>gopīs</s>], himself in private, tearfully

children.text: asaṅkocam avocetthaṃ preṣṭham ekāntinaṃ kvacit ||181||
children.translated_text: spoke without reserve thus to his dearest, exclusive [devotee <s>Uddhava</s>], once: ||181||

'Having slain <s>Kaṃsa</s> in the arena, the adversary of all the <s>Sātvatas</s> — what <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> said to you upon meeting, he makes that true.' ||179|| '<s>Acyuta</s> (the Infallible One) will come to <s>Vraja</s> before long. The Blessed Lord, the master of the <s>Sātvatas</s>, will bring joy to his parents.' ||180||

children.text: gṛhītvā pāṇinā pāṇiṃ prapannārtiharo hariḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Taking [his] hand in [his own] hand, <s>Hari</s>, the remover of the suffering of those who surrender, [said]:',

children.text: gacchoddhava vrajaṃ saumya pitror naḥ prītim āvaha ||182||
children.translated_text: 'Go, <s>Uddhava</s>, to <s>Vraja</s>, O gentle one; bring joy to our parents.' ||182||

children.text: gopīnāṃ madviyogādhiṃ matsandeśair vimocaya |
children.translated_text: 'Relieve the <s>gopīs</s> of the anguish of separation from me through my messages.'

children.text: tā manmanaskā matprāṇā madarthe tyaktadaihikāḥ ||183||
children.translated_text: 'They whose minds are fixed on me, whose life-breaths are me, who have abandoned bodily [concerns] for my sake —' ||183||

children.text: mām eva dayitaṃ preṣṭham ātmānaṃ manasā gatāḥ |
children.translated_text: 'They who have gone to me alone, their beloved, the dearest, as their very self, in their minds;'

children.text: ye tyaktalokadharmāś ca madarthe tān bibharmy aham ||184||
children.translated_text: 'they who have abandoned worldly duties for my sake — them I sustain.' ||184||

children.text: mayi tāḥ preyasāṃ preṣṭhe dūrasthe gokulastriyaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'When I, the dearest of the dear, am far away, the women of <s>Gokula</s>,

children.text: smarantyo 'ṅga vimuhyanti virahautkaṇṭhyavihvalāḥ ||185||
children.translated_text: remembering me, O dear one, become bewildered, overwhelmed by the agitation of longing in separation.' ||185||

children.text:
dhārayanty atikṛcchreṇa prāyaḥ prāṇān kathañcana |
pratyāgamanasandeśair vallavyo me madātmikāḥ ||186||3
pūrvavat ṣaḍbhiḥ
children.translated_text: As before, with six (verses)

children.text: yas tathā procya yat pratyāyayat tac ca vilocyatām |
children.translated_text: He who, having spoken thus, what he then made them believe — let that be examined;

children.text: yad vilocanamātreṇa bhramas te śvabhratāṃ vrajet ||187||
children.translated_text: by the mere examination of which, your delusion would fall into an abyss. ||187||
'With extreme difficulty they somehow barely hold on to their life-breaths. Through messages promising [my] return, the cowherd women who are of my very nature [shall be consoled].' ||186||

children.text: mām evety ādinā tāsām antaḥpatir ahaṃ param |
children.translated_text: By [the words] 'me alone' (<s>mām eva</s>) and the rest, [he established that] 'I am truly the inner lord of those [<s>gopīs</s>];

children.text: bahir vyavahṛtir lokadṛṣṭeti spaṣṭam ātanot ||188||
children.translated_text: the external conduct is for the world's perception' — this he clearly set forth. ||188||

children.text: yat pitror ity urīcakre pitṛtvaṃ vallavendrayoḥ |
children.translated_text: That by [the words] 'of [our] parents' he acknowledged the parenthood of the chief of the cowherds (<s>Nanda</s>) —

children.text: tasmād vallavamānitvam ātmānaś ca vyajijñapat ||189||
children.translated_text: thereby he made known his own status as a cowherd and their [fatherhood]. ||189||

children.text: tatra cāha na ity etad bahuvācipadād idam |
children.translated_text: And there, by [the word] 'our' (<s>naḥ</s>) — from this word denoting plurality —

children.text: mayi jāte tayoḥ putre rāme tvayi ca putratā ||190||
children.translated_text: '<s>Rāma</s> being born as their son, and you too being [their] son' — [thus sonship is indicated]. ||190||

children.text: tataś ca tāḥ prati prākhyad vallavyo ma iti sphuṭam |
children.translated_text: And then, to them [the <s>gopīs</s>], he declared, saying 'the cowherd women, my' (<s>vallavyo me</s>) clearly,

children.text: yad amūṣu svadāratve4 vyānañja svayam añjasā ||191||
children.translated_text: whereby he himself directly expressed his own status as their husband. ||191||

children.text: maddāratvaṃca tāsāṃ tāḥ sadā yasmān madātmikāḥ |
children.translated_text: And the status of those [<s>gopīs</s>] as his wives — because they are always 'of my nature' (<s>madātmikāḥ</s>);

children.text: madātmakatvam āśu syād abhedāc chaktitadvatoḥ ||192||
children.translated_text: their being 'of his nature' follows swiftly from the non-difference of <s>śakti</s> (power) and its possessor. ||192||
1. BhP x.46.35; 2. BhP x.46.34; 3. BhP x.46.2-6; 4. (b) otvaṃ [variant readings and references]

children.text: iti vyañjan manmanaskā ity uktaṃ nātyapaikṣataḥ |
children.translated_text: Thus expressing [this], [the words] 'whose minds are fixed on me' (<s>manmanaskāḥ</s>) have been said — he did not consider it excessive.

children.text: na cānyavad ihāpekṣyam anyad ity apy amanyata ||193||
children.translated_text: Nor did he think that anything else needed to be separately considered here, unlike in other cases. ||193||

children.text: dhārayantīti ca procya pratyāgamanam uddiśan |
children.translated_text: And having said 'they hold on' (<s>dhārayanti</s>), indicating his return,

children.text: vallavyo ma iti prākhyat tasmād eva nyajīgamat ||194||
children.translated_text: he declared 'the cowherd women, my' (<s>vallavyo me</s>) — and from that very [declaration] he descended [i.e., committed to return]. ||194||

children.text: gamanaṃ mama taj jajñe svām avaśyaṃ kṛtiṃ prati |
children.translated_text: 'That going of mine [to them] arose for the fulfillment of my own [promised] action;

children.text: āgamya svīyatāṃ tāsāṃ pūrayiṣyāmy adūrataḥ ||195||
children.translated_text: having come, I shall fulfill the belonging of those [<s>gopīs</s>] to me, before long.' ||195||

children.text: pūrvavad navabhiḥ
children.translated_text: As before, with nine (verses)

children.text: yas tāsu bahudhā jñānaṃ nidiśyāpi mudhā vidan |
children.translated_text: He who, though having instructed them in knowledge in many ways, knowing it to be in vain,

children.text: sākṣād ātmīyasamprāpti1 sākṣād eva nidiṣṭavān ||196||
children.translated_text: directly indicated the direct attainment of himself. ||196||

children.text:
mayy āveśya manaḥ kṛṣṇe vimuktāśesavṛtti yat |
anusmarantyo māṃ nityam acirān mām upaiṣyatha ||197||2
yā mayā krīḍatā rātryāṃ vane 'smin vraja āsthitāḥ |
alabdharāsāḥ kalyāṇyo māpur madvīryacintayā ||198||3
pūrvavad tribhiḥ
children.translated_text: As before, with three (verses)

children.text: yas tadā sandiśan sandīpitam etad vinirmame |
children.translated_text: He who, instructing them at that time, kindled this [fire of love] —

children.text: tad etac chṛṇu maccitta guptavittaṃ manuṣva ca ||199||
children.translated_text: hear this, O mind fixed on me — a hidden treasure — and cherish it! ||199||

'Fixing your minds on me, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, liberated from all other activities, constantly remembering me, you shall quickly attain me.' ||197|| 'You who were established in this forest at <s>Vraja</s> when I was sporting at night — O blessed ones, those who did not obtain the <s>rāsa</s> [dance] attained [me] through contemplation of my power.' ||198||

children.text: vṛttir yad anyā nirmucya mayy āmucya manaḥ sthitāḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Having released all other activities and having fixed your minds on me, you remain [established];

children.text: mām āpsyatha drutaṃ tasmān mama nātra svatantratā ||200||
children.translated_text: you shall attain me quickly — therefore there is no independence on my part [in this matter].' ||200||

children.text: mayīty anena prāpte 'pi kṛṣṇe kṛṣṇapadaṃ bruvan |
children.translated_text: By [the word] 'on me' (<s>mayi</s>), even when <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> was present, [yet] using the word '<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>' [separately],

children.text: anyarūpaṃ manyamānān hanyamānān vyadhāt prabhuḥ ||201
children.translated_text: the Lord struck down those who thought [he was] of another form. ||201||

children.text: mayīty evaṃ mām iti ca procya mām ity avocata |
children.translated_text: Having said 'on me' (<s>mayi</s>) thus, and 'me' (<s>mām</s>), he [then again] said 'me' (<s>mām</s>);

children.text: tac cāvṛttyā dṛḍhīkṛtya mataṃ paridṛḍhīkṛtam ||202||
children.translated_text: and by repetition, having firmly established [this], the [established] view was further consolidated. ||202||

children.text: kṛṣṇa iti padaṃ labdhe mayīty asya viśeṣaṇe |
children.translated_text: The word '<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>' being obtained as a qualifier of 'on me' (<s>mayi</s>),

children.text: māṃ dvaye 'py upalabdhāsā tadviśeṣaṇatā svataḥ ||203||
children.translated_text: 'me' (<s>mām</s>) in both [instances] — the hope of attainment — its qualification [by <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>] is inherent. ||203||

children.text: mayi kṛṣṇe 'tra māṃ kṛṣṇaṃ māṃ kṛṣṇam iti sidhyati |
children.translated_text: 'On me, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>' here, [and] 'me, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>,' 'me, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>' — thus it is established.

children.text: kalyāṇya iti sambodhya prabodhyaṃ kṛtavān idam ||204||
children.translated_text: By addressing [them as] 'O blessed ones' (<s>kalyāṇyaḥ</s>), he made this the object of their awakening. ||204||

children.text: na tāsām iva matprāptir dehaṃ vaḥ param īhate |
children.translated_text: 'The attainment of me is not as for those [who renounced their bodies]; your [body] desires the supreme' —

children.text: ity evam anyad apy atra manyamānaṃ manaḥ kuru ||205||
children.translated_text: thus, 'make your mind consider this other [meaning] as well.' ||205||

children.text: pūrvavad pañcabhiḥ
children.translated_text: As before, with five (verses)

children.text: yaḥ śrīrāmeṇa sandiśya priyāsu nijahṛdgatam |
children.translated_text: He who, having sent a message through the blessed <s>Rāma</s> (Balarāma), to his beloveds,

children.text: yathāvad vyañjayāmāsa śrīparāśaragīr yathā ||206||
children.translated_text: expressed what was in his own heart, just as the blessed <s>Parāśara</s>'s words [convey truth]. ||206||

children.text: pūrvavad yugmakam
children.translated_text: A couplet as before

children.text: yaḥ kurukṣetrayātrāyā vyājān mātrādikān cirāt |
children.translated_text: He who, on the pretext of the pilgrimage to <s>Kurukṣetra</s>, having united with his mother and others after a long time,

children.text: saṃsajyāmūn visṛjyānyān sahavāsamudaṃ dadhe ||208||
children.translated_text: and having sent away the others, gave [the residents of Vraja] the joy of being together. ||208||
'With messages sweet and gentle, full of love, devoid of pride, exceedingly captivating — by <s>Rāma</s> (Balarāma) the <s>gopīs</s> of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> were consoled.' ||207||

children.text: yaḥ suraghnān vraje gantuṃ vighnān hantuṃ vrajeśituḥ |
children.translated_text: He who, [wishing] to go to <s>Vraja</s> and to destroy the obstacles posed by demon-slaying,

children.text: vraje gamanam ācarya dvārakāgatim ādade ||209||
