children.translated_text: performed the journey to <s>Vraja</s> [while ostensibly] taking up the return to <s>Dvārakā</s>. ||209||

children.text: yaḥ krāmadbhiḥ sudīrgheṇa suṣṭhu kraṣṭuṃ vrajaṃ prati |
children.translated_text: He who, by those proceeding along the very long [path], being well drawn toward <s>Vraja</s>,

children.text: āmuktaḥ pāśasaṅkāśamanasā vrajavāsibhiḥ ||210||
children.translated_text: was held by the residents of <s>Vraja</s> with minds like nooses. ||210||

children.text: yaḥ prakāśaṃ mahārājasampadaṃ dadhad īkṣitaḥ |
children.translated_text: He who, openly bearing the splendor of a great king, was seen [by them],

children.text: vrajāya vrajarājādyenāhūtaḥ pūrvavad girā ||211||
children.translated_text: [yet] was addressed by the king of <s>Vraja</s> (<s>Nanda</s>) and others with words as before [i.e., familiarly]. ||211||

children.text: yas teṣāṃ suṣṭhu nirninye yan manaḥ svāgatispṛhiḥ2 |
children.translated_text: He who thoroughly drew out their minds, himself longing for their arrival;

children.text: tenāntaḥkarṣaṇaṃ prāptaḥ karṣam anyena nārhati ||212||
children.translated_text: having been drawn inwardly by them, he cannot be drawn by any other. ||212||

children.text: yaḥ svīyasahitas teṣāṃ svīyakāmān apūrayat |
children.translated_text: He who, together with his own [people], fulfilled their own desires,

children.text: kṛṣṇe kamalapatrākṣe sannyastākhilarādhasā ||213||
children.translated_text: all whose afflictions were surrendered unto <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the lotus-eyed one. ||213||

children.text: āgamiṣyaty adhīrgheṇety3 āśālabdhaṃ yad īpsitam |
children.translated_text: 'He will come before long' — by this hope, the desired [goal] was obtained;

children.text: tad artham eva tān arthān ye svīcakruḥ parān api ||214||
children.translated_text: for that very purpose, those who had accepted even other objects [did so only for that end]. ||214||

children.text: pūrvavad yugmakam
children.translated_text: A couplet as before

children.text: yaḥ svāgamanamaryādāṃ preyasīṣu nijāṃ vyadhāt |
children.translated_text: He who established the proper limit of his own return among his beloveds —

children.text: dantavakrāntaśatrūṇāṃ māraṇaṃ sarvatāraṇam ||215||
children.translated_text: the slaying of enemies ending with <s>Dantavakra</s> [would be] the deliverance of all. ||215||

children.text:
api smaratha naḥ sakhyaḥ svānām arthaṃ4 cikīrṣayā |
gatāṃś cirāyitān śatrupakṣakṣapaṇacetasaḥ ||216|| 5
mayi bhaktir hi bhūtānām amṛtatvāya kalpate |
diṣṭyā yad āsīn matsneho bhavatīnāṃ madāpanaḥ ||217||6
yas tātkālikaśāntyarthe tathāpi jñānam ādiśat |
children.translated_text: He who, for the purpose of their immediate pacification, nevertheless imparted knowledge;

children.text: āhūś cety7ādike padye prārthitas tābhir anyathā ||218||
children.translated_text: in the verse beginning 'They said' and so forth, when entreated by them otherwise, ||218||

'Do you remember us, O friends? We who departed long ago with the intent of accomplishing the welfare of our own, our minds set on destroying the enemy's faction. ||216|| Devotion to me indeed leads beings to immortality. Fortunately, the love you have for me is that which removes [the intoxication of] my [separation from you]. ||217||'

children.text: tatrāṅghrismṛtiyācñā tu lakṣyam eva vinirmame |
children.translated_text: therein, their prayer for the remembrance of his feet was fashioned as the true aim;

children.text: tatpratyāgatitātparyā sā tu paryavasāyyate ||219||
children.translated_text: but their real intent is concluded as the desire for his return. ||219||

children.text: mayi tāḥ preyasām ity8 ādy uktaṃ tena svayaṃ yataḥ |
children.translated_text: Since the verse beginning 'Among my beloveds, they...' was spoken by him himself,

children.text: tasmāt taccintanāśaktyā vyaktyā taddarśanārthitā ||220||
children.translated_text: therefore, through the power of contemplating him, their desire for his direct vision is manifest. ||220||

children.text: tathānugṛhya bhagavān gopīnāṃ sa gurur gatiḥ |9
children.translated_text: 'Then, the Blessed Lord, having thus graced them, being the <s>guru</s> (teacher) and refuge of the <s>gopīs</s>' —

children.text: ity anena muniḥ procya tāsāṃ vāñchitapūraṇam ||221||
children.translated_text: by this [statement], the sage, having declared the fulfillment of their desire, ||221||

children.text: mayi bhaktir hīti kṛṣṇaproktam eva nyajīgamat |
children.translated_text: affirmed the very statement spoken by <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>: 'Devotion to me indeed...'

children.text: mayy āveśya manaḥ kṛṣṇa ity10 ādy api ca tadvacaḥ ||222||
children.translated_text: And also the verse 'Fixing your mind on <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>...' and so forth — that too is his word. ||222||

children.text: pūrvavad tribhiḥ
children.translated_text: As before, with three verses.

children.text:
1. vip v.24.20; 2. (b) svāgataspṛhi; 3. BhP x.65.6; 4. (b) arthao; 5. BhP x.82||.41; 6 BhP x.82||.44; 7. BhP x.82||.48; 8. BhP x.46.5; 9. BhP x.83.1; 10. BhP x.47.36.
yaḥ pṛthivyā guṇastome satyenādāv abhiṣṭutaḥ
satyaṃ vidhātuṃ satyaṃ tan nāvrajet kiṃ vraje bata ||223||
children.translated_text: in order to make true that truth, would he not come to <s>Vraja</s> indeed? ||223||
[Footnotes: references to Viṣṇu Purāṇa, Bhāgavata Purāṇa, etc.] He who, in the assemblage of the qualities of the earth, was first praised for his truthfulness —

children.text: sambhāvanā mamaiveyam iti nātra vicāryatām |
children.translated_text: 'This expectation is mine alone' — let this not be deliberated upon here;

children.text: vrajasthānāṃ vrajaprāṇavaryasyāpy avadhāryatām ||224||
children.translated_text: let it be ascertained even of the foremost life-breath of the residents of <s>Vraja</s>. ||224||

children.text: śrīmadvrajādhirājasya kṛṣṇakāntāgaṇasya ca |
children.translated_text: Of the glorious sovereign of <s>Vraja</s> and of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s host of beloveds —

children.text: uddhavaṃ prati gīr īdṛg dṛśyatāṃ daśamādiṣu ||225||
children.translated_text: let such words addressed to <s>Uddhava</s> be seen in the Tenth [Canto] and elsewhere. ||225||

children.text: yugmakam
children.translated_text: A pair of verses.

children.text: yas tu yarhy ambujākṣeti1 stuvadbhir dvārakājanaiḥ |
children.translated_text: He who, when the people of <s>Dvārakā</s> were praising him [with words] beginning 'O Lotus-eyed one' —

children.text: kadācid vrajam āgād ity abhyudhāyi kadācana ||226||
children.translated_text: once came to <s>Vraja</s>, so it was proclaimed somewhere. ||226||

children.text: yas tathā śrūyate pādmottarakhaṇḍād api sphuṭam |
children.translated_text: He who is likewise clearly heard of from the <s>Uttarakhaṇḍa</s> (latter section) of the <s>Padma Purāṇa</s>;

children.text: adād vrajāya svaprāptimaṅgalaṃ nityam ity api ||227||
children.translated_text: who gave to <s>Vraja</s> the auspiciousness of attaining him, eternally. ||227||

children.text: dattvā tatkṛtakṛtyaḥ san prādurbhāvāntaraṃ gataḥ |
children.translated_text: Having given that and become fulfilled, he entered another manifestation;

children.text: jagāma dvārakām ity apy aśrāvīty api yuktimat ||228||
children.translated_text: 'he went to <s>Dvārakā</s>' — that was also heard, and it is consistent. ||228||

children.text: āgamiṣyaty adīrgheṇety uddhavād buddham anyathā |
children.translated_text: 'He will return before long' — [the <s>gopīs</s>] understood from <s>Uddhava</s> otherwise;

children.text: yathā na syāt tathā bhāṣyaṃ2 kathānyā vitathā matā ||229||
children.translated_text: so that it should not be so, this statement [is reconciled]; the other narrative is considered not invalid. ||229||

children.text: yas tyajann api gām ākhyat tam uddhavakam utsukaḥ |
children.translated_text: He who, even while leaving the earth, eagerly told <s>Uddhava</s> about it;

children.text: rāmeṇa sārdham ity3ādyaṃ tāsāṃ kāmitalambhanam ||230||
children.translated_text: 'Together with <s>Rāma</s>...' and so forth — that is the attainment of what they desired. ||230||

children.text: rāmeṇeti dvayenāha viyukter yad vyatītatām |
children.translated_text: With 'together with <s>Rāma</s>,' he stated by means of a pair [of words] what had already passed regarding separation;

children.text: tena nāsti viyuktiḥ sā tadānīm iti bhāvyate ||231||
children.translated_text: thereby, that separation did not exist at that time — so it should be understood. ||231||

children.text: mayi tāḥ preyasāṃ preṣṭha iti4 prāktanavāgdvaye |
children.translated_text: 'Among my beloveds, they are the dearest' — in this pair of former statements,

children.text: viyukter vartamānatvaṃ dṛṣṭvā niṣṭaṅkatām idam ||232||
children.translated_text: seeing the present-tense nature of the separation, let this be firmly established. ||232||

children.text: svena tāsāṃ punaḥ saṅge yad vṛttaṃ prathame 'hani |
children.translated_text: What occurred on the first day when he personally reunited with them —

children.text: tadapy atītarīty āha prītyā samadadhad uddhavam ||233||
children.translated_text: even that he spoke of as past, affectionately pleasing <s>Uddhava</s>. ||233||

children.text: tā nāvidann iti5 proce yatra tāsāṃ madātmatām |
children.translated_text: 'They did not know' — in what he declared, wherein their identity with him

children.text: babhūva sa mahābhāvaḥ sarvāsāṃ parataḥ paraḥ ||234||
children.translated_text: became that great state (<s>mahābhāva</s>), the supreme beyond the supreme, of all of them. ||234||

children.text: tataś ca nāmarūpātmany udbhūte svīyavaibhave |
children.translated_text: And then, when their own glory, consisting of name and form, had arisen,

children.text: praviṣṭā iva na spaṣṭaṃ praviṣṭā gatyabhāvataḥ ||235
children.translated_text: they entered as it were, yet did not clearly enter, because there was nowhere to go. ||235||

children.text: dṛṣṭāntayugalaṃ tat tu nāvidann iti kevale |
children.translated_text: That pair of examples pertains only to '[they] did not know';

children.text: avedanaṃ nadīpakṣe py abdhyanyarasatāhatiḥ ||236
children.translated_text: the non-knowing — on the side of rivers too, the loss of separate taste in the ocean. ||236||

children.text: samādhāv iti dṛṣṭāntasyāṅgarūpatayor itam |
children.translated_text: 'In <s>samādhi</s> (absorption)' — of the example's limb-nature, this

children.text: dārṣṭāntikasyānuṣaṅgaṃ syād aṅgaṃ tadbhidādvayoḥ ||237
children.translated_text: would be the connection of the illustrated; the limb would be of the two that differ from it. ||237||

children.text: matkāmā ramaṇaṃ jāram asvarūpavido 'balāḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Desiring me, [having accepted me as their] lover — women who did not know [my] true nature;

children.text: brahma māṃ paramaṃ prāpur iti6 padye tu tatpare ||238||
children.translated_text: they attained me, the supreme <s>Brahman</s>' — in this verse, however, the meaning is: ||238||

children.text: pacyantāṃ vividhāḥ pākā7 itīvātrārthikaḥ kramaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Let various [fruits] ripen' — thus the sequence here pertains to the meaning;

children.text: tā brahma prāpur ity evaṃ tā ity asyātra cānvayaḥ ||239||
children.translated_text: 'they attained <s>Brahman</s>' — in this manner, the syntactic connection of 'they' applies here. ||239||

children.text: kīdṛg brahmeti bodhāya yat prāha paramaṃ padam |
children.translated_text: To indicate what kind of <s>Brahman</s>, [he said] 'the supreme abode';

children.text: tatrāpy ākāṅkṣayāvādīn mām iti svaṃ punaḥ prabhuḥ ||240||
children.translated_text: and therein too, out of the desire [to clarify], the Lord said 'me' — himself again. ||240||
[Footnotes: references to Bhāgavata Purāṇa, etc.]

children.text: mayi bhaktir hīti vākyād āha prāg etad eva hi |
children.translated_text: From the statement 'Devotion to me indeed...,' he had already stated this very thing;

children.text: dhārayanty atikṛcchreṇety uktyā vyānag idaṃ purā ||241||
children.translated_text: with the utterance 'sustaining [their lives] with the greatest difficulty,' he had expressed this before. ||241||

children.text: prāṇatyāgena matprāptir nānyavat tāsu manmatā |
children.translated_text: 'Attainment of me through giving up one's life — not like others' is not my opinion regarding them;

children.text: matkāmā iti pūrvārdhe cākhyat prāptivibhaktatām ||242||
children.translated_text: in the first half of 'desiring me,' he also stated the distinctness of their attainment. ||242||

children.text: asvarūpavidaḥ satyaḥ prāpur jāradhiyety avak |
children.translated_text: 'Not knowing the true nature' — true; 'they attained through the notion of a lover' — he said below;

children.text: nityatatpreyasīrūpasvarūpaṃ hi tadīyakam ||243||
children.translated_text: for their nature is indeed that of being his eternal beloveds. ||243||

children.text: yat pūrvaṃ bhāvayan bhāvaṃ bhāvinīnām amūdṛśām |
children.translated_text: He who, contemplating beforehand the sentiment of such women,

children.text: matkāmā iti niḥkṣipya jāratve sthairyam1 ākṣipat ||244||
children.translated_text: having placed 'desiring me' there, challenged the firmness of [his being merely] a paramour. ||244||

children.text: mayi kāmaḥ sadā yāsāṃ tā matkāmā itīritāḥ |
children.translated_text: Those who always have desire for me — they are called 'desiring me';

children.text: kāmaś ca ramaṇatvena spṛhātra pratipadyate ||245||
children.translated_text: and 'desire' here is understood as the longing for him to be their lover. ||245||

children.text: asminn api batety2ādi śrīrādhāgīr aliṃ prati |
children.translated_text: The words of the glorious <s>Rādhā</s> to a bee, beginning 'In this one, alas...' —

children.text: vivicyatāṃ tataḥ sarvam anyad anyad vivicyatām ||246||
children.translated_text: let them be examined; then let everything else, one by one, be examined. ||246||

children.text: atrāryaputra3 śabdaḥ syāt patyāv eva prasiddhibhāk |
children.translated_text: Here, the word '<s>āryaputra</s>' (noble husband) would apply only to a husband, by well-known usage;

children.text: tathāpi sveṣu kaiṅkaryaṃ dainyāt kanyāvad īritam ||247||
children.translated_text: yet service to one's own [lord] is expressed out of humility, as if by a maiden. ||247||

children.text: saṅk ptāpatitā tābhiḥ punar ittham udīritam |
children.translated_text: Having fallen down [at his feet], they spoke again in this manner;

children.text: śyāmasundara te dāsya iti4 yadvat tatheha ca ||248||
children.translated_text: 'O <s>Śyāmasundara</s> (beautiful dark one), [we are] your servants' — just as that was said, so here too. ||248||

children.text: āryaputraḥ kadāsmākaṃ kiṅkarīṇāṃ tu mūrdhani |
children.translated_text: 'When will the noble husband place his arm upon the heads of us, his maidservants?' —

children.text: bhujaṃ dhāsyaty evam āsāṃ tatpatnīpadakāmatā ||249||
children.translated_text: thus is their desire for the status of being his wives. ||249||

children.text: tatkāmatā hi siddhā cet tena taddānam avyayam |
children.translated_text: For if that desire [for wifehood] is already accomplished, then his gift [of himself] is imperishable;

children.text: ye yathā māṃ prapadyante iti5 yatvat6 pratiśravaḥ ||250||
children.translated_text: as per the promise: 'As they surrender unto me [so I reward them].' ||250||

children.text: vallavyo me madātmāna iti7 yat proktam ātmanā |
children.translated_text: The <s>gopīs</s> are my own, their selves [belong to] me' — what was spoken by the Lord himself,

children.text: sarveṣāṃ vacasām ūrdhvaṃ tad āstāṃ sarvamūrdhani ||251||
children.translated_text: let that stand above all other statements, at the crest of all. ||251||

children.text: yan matkāmā iti proce tāsāṃ prāptis tathā svayam |
children.translated_text: What he declared as 'desiring me' — their attainment is likewise by himself;

children.text: tan mayā sādhu tat proktaṃ tāsāṃ kāmitalambhanam ||252||
children.translated_text: that was well spoken by me — the attainment of what they desired. ||252||

children.text: matkāmā iti padyasya turyāṃśe tv idam ucyate |
children.translated_text: In the fourth quarter of the verse 'desiring me,' this is stated:

children.text: parāś ca saṅgatas tāsāṃ prāpuḥ śatasahasraśaḥ8 ||253||
children.translated_text: 'And others, along with them, attained [me] in hundreds of thousands.' ||253||

children.text: pūrvavad ekaviṃśatyā
children.translated_text: As before, with twenty-one verses.

children.text: yaḥ śrīgargavacaḥ pūrṇaṃ tūrṇaṃ cakre svayaṃ dvayam |
children.translated_text: He who swiftly made the complete words of the glorious <s>Garga</s> into a pair [of fulfillments];

children.text: eṣa vaḥ śreya ādhasyad ya etasmin maheti9 dik ||254||
children.translated_text: 'This one will bestow supreme good upon you, who...' — thus is the direction of the verse beginning 'great.' ||254||

children.text: nāśād vighnasya kaṃsādeḥ patyābhāsādijasya ca |
children.translated_text: Through the destruction of obstacles beginning with <s>Kaṃsa</s> and of those born from the semblance of a husband and the like,

children.text: 1. (b) 'sthairyam; 2. BhP x.47.21; 3. ibid.; 4. x.22.15; 5. gītā 4.11; 6. (a) yat tat; 7. BhP x.46.6; 8. BhP xi.12.13; 9. BhP x.8.16
children.translated_text: [Footnotes: textual variants and references.]

children.text: sadā svam adadād yasmād vraje kāntāvrajeṣv api ||255||
children.translated_text: he always gave himself — in <s>Vraja</s> and among the groups of beloveds of <s>Vraja</s> as well. ||255||

children.text: pūrvavad yugmakam
children.translated_text: As before, a pair of verses.

children.text: yaḥ prādād vrajavāsibhyaḥ pūrvarītyā nijāṃ gatim |
children.translated_text: He who gave to the residents of <s>Vraja</s>, in the former manner, his own abode —

children.text: vṛndāvanasthāṃ golokanāmnīṃ yāṃ prāg alokayat ||256||
children.translated_text: that which is situated in <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, named <s>Goloka</s>, which was formerly revealed. ||256||

children.text: yāṃ śrībṛhadgautamīye prāha vṛndāvanaṃ prati |
children.translated_text: That which is stated in the glorious <s>Bṛhadgautamīya</s> [Tantra] regarding <s>Vṛndāvana</s>:

children.text: sarvadevamayaś cāhaṃ na tyajāmi vanaṃ kvacit ||257||
children.translated_text: 'I am all the gods, and I never abandon this forest.'

children.text:
āvirbhāvas tirobhāvo bhaven me'tra yuge yuge |
tejomayam idaṃ ramyam adṛśyaṃ carmacakṣuṣā ||258||1
tad etad vistarād brahmasaṃhitāyāṃ nirūpitam |
children.translated_text: That very thing has been expounded in detail in the <s>Brahmasaṃhitā</s>;

children.text: golokanāmnā2 tanmadhye gokulākhyaṃ hareḥ padam ||259||
children.translated_text: in the midst of [the realm] called <s>Goloka</s>, the abode of <s>Hari</s> called <s>Gokula</s>. ||259||
'Manifestation and disappearance occur for me here in every age; this [abode] is effulgent, charming, and invisible to the mortal eye.' ||258||

children.text: na tyajāmīti yat tat tu dvidhābhiprāyakaṃ matam |
children.translated_text: 'I do not abandon [it]' — this is considered to have a twofold purport:

children.text: virahe 'pi vraje sphūrtyā pūrtyā śīghrāgater api ||260||
children.translated_text: even in separation, [he remains] in <s>Vraja</s> through manifestation, and through fulfillment — because of his swift return also. ||260||

children.text: pūrvavac caturbhiḥ
children.translated_text: As before, with four verses.

children.text:
yaḥ sva-puryor api sthairyaṃ yāti nityaṃ yathāha ca |
mathurā bhagavān yatra nityaṃ sannihito hariḥ ||261||3
dvārakāṃ hariṇā tyaktāṃ samudrotplāvayat kṣaṇāt |
varjayitvā mahārāja śrīmad-bhagavad-ālayam ||262||4
smṛtvāśeṣāśubha-haraṃ sarva-maṅgala-maṅgalaḥ |
nityaṃ sannihitas tatra bhagavān madhusūdanaḥ ||263||5
children.translated_text: He who eternally abides even in his two cities, as is also stated: '<s>Mathurā</s>, where the Blessed Lord <s>Hari</s> eternally resides.' ||261|| '<s>Dvārakā</s>, abandoned by <s>Hari</s>, was instantly engulfed by the ocean, except, O great king, for the blessed temple of the Lord.' ||262|| 'Remembering [him] who removes all inauspiciousness, the all-auspicious; the Blessed Lord <s>Madhusūdana</s> eternally resides there.' ||263||

children.text: pūrvavad tribhiḥ
children.translated_text: As before, with three verses.

children.text: yas tasmād ubhayatrāpi rājatīti śukena ca |
children.translated_text: He who therefore shines in both places — by <s>Śuka</s> too,

children.text: jayatīty6 ādi-vākyena varṇitaḥ kṣitipaṃ prati ||264||
children.translated_text: with the statement beginning 'He conquers...' he was described to the king. ||264||

children.text: yaś campū-yugala-prāntam īdṛk siddhāntam īritam |
children.translated_text: He who, at the conclusion of the pair of <s>campū</s> [compositions], proclaimed such a conclusion;

children.text: jīvāntaryāmitāṃ prāptas tūrṇaṃ pūrṇam acīkarat ||265||
children.translated_text: having attained the state of being the inner controller (<s>antaryāmin</s>) of <s>Jīva</s>, he swiftly made it complete. ||265||

children.text: sa tu harir adhivartma dantavakraṃ
children.translated_text: That <s>Hari</s>, having pacified <s>Dantavakra</s>

children.text: yudhi śamayan vraja-vāsam āsasāda |
children.translated_text: in battle on the road beyond, reached the dwelling of <s>Vraja</s>;

children.text: tam abhiyayur amī vrajeśa-mukhyāḥ
children.translated_text: the leaders of <s>Vraja</s>, headed by [<s>Nanda</s>], approached him

children.text: śaśinam iva kṣudhitāś cakora-vārāḥ ||266||
children.translated_text: as hungry <s>cakora</s> birds [approach] the moon. ||266||

children.text: ādim ārabhya mahā-kulakam
children.translated_text: Beginning from here, a great cluster of verses.

children.text: sa ca janaka-mukhān nirīkṣya
children.translated_text: And he, seeing <s>Janaka</s> (<s>Nanda</s>) and the others,

children.text: śuṣkān svadṛg-amṛtena siñcati sma |
children.translated_text: withered, sprinkled them with the nectar of his glance;

children.text: pulaka-kula-miṣād yathāṅkurāṇāṃ
children.translated_text: under the pretext of horripilation, those cowherd-trees

children.text: tatim adadhur bata te'pi gopavṛkṣāḥ ||267||
children.translated_text: put forth a row of sprouts, alas! ||267||

children.text: atha hari-hariṇīdṛśaś ca tarhi
children.translated_text: Then the doe-eyed beloveds of <s>Hari</s>, as if attaining

children.text: sphuraṇam iva pratipadya pūrva-tulyam |
children.translated_text: a stirring equal to the former [experience],

children.text: nayana-gatatayānyathā ca matvā
children.translated_text: yet considering it otherwise since it had entered their eyes,

children.text: muhur agaman bhramam abhramaṃ ca tatra ||268||
children.translated_text: repeatedly went back and forth between confusion and certainty there. ||268||
[Footnotes: references.]

children.text: vrajam atha viśataḥ sa-ratnam ārātrikam anulabdhavataś ca tasya lokaḥ |
children.translated_text: As he entered <s>Vraja</s>, the people, having received the jeweled <s>āratrika</s> (welcome lamp), performed for him

children.text: kusuma-kula-sahodaraṃ vitanvan jaya-jaya-ghoṣam uvāca bhadra-vācam ||269||
children.translated_text: a shower of flowers akin to kinsmen, uttering the auspicious cry of 'Victory! Victory!' ||269||

children.text: vrajam atha sukhayan vinīta-vācā
children.translated_text: Then, delighting <s>Vraja</s> with gentle words,

children.text: kramam anulabdha-tadīya-saṅgamaś ca |
children.translated_text: and having gradually obtained their company,

children.text: druta-gati jananīṃ sukhena sektuṃ
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇacandra</s> (Moon-like Kṛṣṇa), with swift steps, to drench his mother with joy,

children.text: gṛham adasīyam iyāya kṛṣṇa-candraḥ ||270||
children.translated_text: went to the house of his [mother <s>Yaśodā</s>]. ||270||

children.text: ciram api viracayya śarma tasyās tad-anumatiṃ pratilabhya tat-tanūjaḥ |
children.translated_text: Having produced joy in her for a long time, and having obtained her permission, her son,

children.text: saha-sakhi-nikareṇa divya-śayyāṃ sukham adhiśayya niśāvirāma-dṛṣṭaḥ ||271||
children.translated_text: together with the group of his friends, resting happily upon a divine bed, was seen at the close of the night. ||271||

children.text: punar api nija-vṛnda-saukhya-vṛndaṃ vidadhad uditya sa nitya-citra-mitraḥ |
children.translated_text: Again, arising, that ever-wonderful friend, producing heaps of joy for his own group,

children.text: nija-mukha-kamalaṃ vikāsya netra-bhramara-madhūtsavam ātatāna tatra ||272||
children.translated_text: opening his own lotus-face, extended there the festival of nectar for the bee-like eyes. ||272||

children.text: yugmakam
children.translated_text: A pair of verses.

children.text: aharahar idam eva tatra pūrva-1pratinava-bhāvam avāpa kevalaṃ na |
children.translated_text: Day after day, this very [experience] there took on a freshness as if experienced for the first time — not merely [that];

children.text: jana-samuditir apy adṛṣṭa-pūrvāṃ vapur anukāntim iyāya śaśvad eva ||273||
children.translated_text: even the assembly of people attained a beauty of form ever-unseen-before, perpetually. ||273||

children.text: divasa-katipaye tadātiyāte2 paśupati-pālakatāpta-tādṛg-icchuḥ |
children.translated_text: After a few days had passed, [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>], desiring to fulfill the wish obtained through the role of protector of the cowherds,

children.text: nija-ratha-tarasā nināya goṣṭhaṃ saha-jananī-kabalaṃ tam uddhavaṃ ca ||274||
children.translated_text: by the speed of his own chariot, brought to the cowshed, together with his mother as a morsel [of love], <s>Uddhava</s> as well. ||274||

children.text: agharipu-sudṛśāṃ dhavābhimāniṣv akṛta-tanu-pratimāḥ purā tu māyā |
children.translated_text: The <s>Māyā</s> (illusory power), which had previously not created bodily replicas among those who claimed to be husbands of <s>Hari</s>'s doe-eyed beloveds,

children.text: sarabhasam adhunā sma tā vibhajya prakṛta-tanūs tanute premāspadāni ||275||
children.translated_text: now eagerly divided them and fashioned their natural bodies as vessels of <s>prema</s> (love). ||275||

children.text: atha gatavati mūrti-bheda-rītyā yadu-puram atra ca rājamāna-dhāmni |
children.translated_text: Now, when [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>] had departed through the manner of division of forms to the city of the <s>Yadus</s>, and here too his splendor was resplendent —

children.text: vraja-bhava-jana-mātra-dṛśya-rūpe matir udiyāt tava citta gopa-kṛṣṇe ||276||
children.translated_text: may your mind, O heart, be directed toward the cowherd <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, whose form is visible only to the inhabitants of <s>Vraja</s>. ||276||

children.text:
iti janmādi-līlā
||1||
children.translated_text: Thus [ends] the <s>līlā</s> (divine sport) of birth and so forth. ||1||

children.text: 1. (b) pūrvaṃ; 2. (a) tadādio
children.translated_text: [Footnotes: textual variants.]

children.text: atha nityalīlā
children.translated_text: Now, the eternal <s>līlā</s> (<s>nityalīlā</s>).

children.text: prakaṭataravikāsabhāji vṛndāvana iha bhāti kim apy adṛśya-dhāma |
children.translated_text: In <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, an invisible abode shines here, resplendent with most manifest splendor;

children.text: vraja-jana-sahitaḥ sa yatra kṛṣṇaḥ sukha-vihṛtiṃ vidadhad vibhāti nityam ||1||
children.translated_text: where <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, together with the people of <s>Vraja</s>, eternally shines, performing blissful pastimes. ||1||

children.text: parilasati payaḥ-samudra-sīmā vraja-yuva-rāja-samāja-loka eṣaḥ |
children.translated_text: This realm of the young prince of <s>Vraja</s> shines, bordered by the milk-ocean;

children.text: amum anu caturasram atra vanyāgiri-sarid-añcita-cārutātidhanyā ||2||
children.translated_text: following it, square in shape, exceedingly blessed, adorned with forests, mountains, and rivers. ||2||

children.text: girisamuditir atra suṣṭhu govardhanavalitā paribhāti citratulyā |
children.translated_text: The host of mountains here shines beautifully, encircled by <s>Govardhana</s>, as if in a painting;

children.text: vilasati yamunādikānadīnāṃ tatir api mānasagaṅgayānuṣaktā ||3||
children.translated_text: the array of rivers beginning with <s>Yamunā</s> also glistens, joined with the celestial <s>Gaṅgā</s> of the mind. ||3||

children.text: abhirucidadaratnacitramitraṃ bhuvanam idaṃ paribhāti yatra vṛkṣāḥ |
children.translated_text: This world shines with beautiful gems and the sun as its friend; where the trees

children.text: tad anukṛtiparārucā samṛddhyā hariratidāyitayā ca ye vibhātāḥ ||4||
children.translated_text: are resplendent with a competing beauty that imitates it, and with the prosperity given by <s>Hari</s>'s intense love. ||4||

children.text: vilasati caturasradhāmni ghasrakṣitipatibimbamahaḥ sahasrapatram |
children.translated_text: In the four-cornered abode, the thousand-petaled [lotus] shines with the splendor of the sun-image, the lord of the earth by day.

children.text: upavanam adhipatram atra kṛṣṇapriyatama1dāravihārasāravāraḥ ||5||
children.translated_text: The garden is the supreme leaf here — a flood of the essence of the pastimes with the most beloved consorts of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>. ||5||

children.text: iha kamaladaladvayālimadhyasthitipathivṛndam atisphuṭaṃ vibhāti |
children.translated_text: Here, the group of pathways situated between two rows of lotus petals shines most brilliantly,

children.text: aparaparagatāv acākṣuṣāṇi śrutivihitāny ayanāni yat tu jetṛ ||6||
children.translated_text: surpassing the invisible paths ordained by the <s>Śrutis</s> (scriptures) that proceed to the far and near. ||6||

children.text: maṇijani2kamalasya tasya cāgrāvalivalayapratisandhilabdhasandhi |
children.translated_text: And from the tip of that jewel-born lotus, [there is] a joint obtained at the junction of the encircling ring of petals;

children.text: surabhigaṇavṛtāsudhābhadugdhāsurabhitatiḥ śrayate śubhaṃyugoṣṭham ||7||
children.translated_text: an expanse of fragrance, surrounded by herds of <s>Surabhi</s> cows, yielding nectar-like milk, graces the auspicious cowshed. ||7||

children.text: atha dalavalayasya madhyabhāgaṃ3 pratilasati vrajarājarājadhānī |
children.translated_text: Now, the capital of the king of <s>Vraja</s> gleams as the central portion of the petal-ring,

children.text: paridhivad4 abhitaḥ samastagopaprakaragṛhāvalir atra yatra bhāti ||8||
children.translated_text: where the row of houses of all the cowherds shines around it like a rampart. ||8||

children.text: rucilasadavarodhamadhyabhāgaṃ sapariṣadantimaṣaṣṭhabhāgapuṣṭam |
children.translated_text: The palace of the king of <s>Vraja</s>, with a beautifully shining inner quarter at its center, enriched by the sixth part at the ultimate perimeter with its assembly hall,

children.text: vrajanṛpabhavanaṃ tu tatra cāntar dinakaravad vidadhāti raśmisṛṣṭim ||9||
children.translated_text: within, like the sun, emanates a flood of rays. ||9||

children.text: yad api maṇimayaṃ tad eka-rūpaṃ tad api sad adbhuta-madhya-madhya-bhāgam |
children.translated_text: Though that [palace] is made of jewels, it is of a single form; yet it possesses a wonderfully varied inner center;

children.text: yadi bahu-vidham ūhituṃ samīhā smara mama mānasa gopa-campū-yugmam ||10||
children.translated_text: if there is a desire to imagine its manifold [beauty] — O my mind, remember the twin encampments of the cowherds. ||10||

children.text: iha sahacaratārakālipuṣṭaḥ svakaparicāricakoravārajuṣṭaḥ |
children.translated_text: Here, nurtured by the rows of companion stars, attended by the young ones among his own attendants,

children.text: smitam anuyaśa ity anudya kaumudy avataratīty uditātareḥ sutuṣṭaḥ ||11||
children.translated_text: having uttered 'following praise' as a smile, he descends like a moonrise and is exceedingly delighted. ||11||

children.text: vrajakulakumudāvalīmudāṃ yaḥ satatamahāmahakṛdvidhāv atandraḥ |
children.translated_text: He who is always tireless in the festival-making that brings joy to the cluster of night-lotuses that is the <s>Vraja</s> clan —

children.text: pitṛmukhasadasi priyāvalīnāṃ mahasi ca nandati gopakṛṣṇacandraḥ ||12||
children.translated_text: the cowherd <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>-moon rejoices in the assembly headed by his father and in the splendor of his rows of beloveds. ||12||

children.text: surapatimaṇimānitāṅgisaṅghapaṭapapaṭutākṛtahemaraṅgabhaṅgaḥ |
children.translated_text: He who shatters the golden stage by the brilliance of his company of women, adorned with jewels honored by the king of the gods —

children.text: guṇagaṇabhṛtabhāratīsamājaḥ sa jayati gokularājavaṃśarājaḥ ||13||
children.translated_text: that king of the dynasty of the king of <s>Gokula</s>, bearing a company of eloquence endowed with clusters of virtues, is triumphant! ||13||

children.text: tribhiḥ kulakam
children.translated_text: A <s>kulaka</s> of three verses.

children.text: iha harivihṛtīr atītarītyā śṛṇu kathayāmi sadāpi nātibhinnāḥ |
children.translated_text: Now hear — I shall narrate <s>Hari</s>'s pastimes in a manner that transcends ordinary style, ever undivided;

children.text: yad anṛtam api pūrvarīti cetaḥ praviśati nādyatanaṃ tathā yathārtham ||14||
children.translated_text: for a former account, even if fictitious, enters the mind — not a present one in the same way as the true. ||14||

children.text: 1. (b) priyatam udārao; 2. (b) cintāmaṇio; 3. obhāsaṃ; 4. (b) parividhad; 5.
children.translated_text: 1. (b) priyatam udārao; 2. (b) cintāmaṇio; 3. obhāsaṃ; 4. (b) parividhad; 5.

children.text: pratilavam api citram asya tat tat ka iva sudhīr avasānam ādadīta? ||15||
children.translated_text: Even at each moment, each wonder of his — what wise person could ever reach its end? ||15||

children.text: atha niśi rahasāgatāntarāyāṃ valajam ite stavavādyavidyaloke |
children.translated_text: Then, when night had come and obstacles had secretly departed, [when] the people of <s>Valaja</s> had gone to the city of praise, music, and learning,

children.text: vrajabhavanajanaḥ sahaiva jāgran manasi hariṃ dadhad āgataṃ nananda ||16||
children.translated_text: the people of <s>Vraja</s>'s homes, remaining awake together, holding <s>Hari</s> in their minds, rejoiced as he arrived. ||16||

children.text: sa mathananinadaṃ sagītanādaṃ sasurabhidoharavaṃ sagopavādam |
children.translated_text: With the sound of churning, accompanied by the melody of singing, with the fragrant milking sounds, with the discourse of cowherds,

children.text: amṛtamathanayuk payodhitulyaṃ vrajakulam ullasitaṃ didhinva kṛṣṇam ||17||
children.translated_text: the <s>Vraja</s> clan, jubilant, resembling the milky ocean churned for nectar, licked up <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> [with their eyes]. ||17||

children.text: vrajapatimithunaṃ tadātha putrapramadamadaślathitapradānasetu |
children.translated_text: The couple that is the lord and lady of <s>Vraja</s> — then their dam of generous giving, loosened by the intoxicating joy over their son —

children.text: tanayajaya1viruttatiṃ paṭhadbhyaḥ pracurataraṃ vitatāra vāravāram2 ||18||
children.translated_text: to those reciting the auspicious chants of their son's victory, they distributed [gifts] most abundantly, again and again. ||18||

children.text: iha lasati harer vilāsagehapratatir udārasudārasāravārā |
children.translated_text: Here shines forth the expanse of <s>Hari</s>'s pleasure-houses, with streams of generous, splendid essence;

children.text: śayanasukhamayī nikuñjavīthiḥ kvacana ca tādṛśatāṃ gatā vibhāti ||19||
children.translated_text: somewhere, the grove-lane, full of the bliss of rest, appears as having attained that very [beauty]. ||19||

children.text: nijanijaśayanaṃ gataṃ tam āliṅganavalitaṃ vidadhur vidhusutanvaḥ |
children.translated_text: Having gone to their respective beds, the moon-complexioned women embraced him, entwining him;

children.text: rajani viramaṇaṃ yathā yathāsīd aghaṭata dordraḍhimā tathā tathāsām ||20||
children.translated_text: as the cessation of the night proceeded, so proportionally grew the firmness of their arms [around him]. ||20||

children.text: iha paramaramā vibhāti rādhā saduḍugaṇe gagane yathendumūrtiḥ |
children.translated_text: Here the supreme <s>Ramā</s> (goddess of beauty), <s>Rādhā</s>, shines forth — like the form of the moon in the sky among beautiful stars;

children.text: tad iyam adhikayā girā sabhājyā tadanugatiṃ dadhatāṃ parāḥ sapatnyaḥ ||21||
children.translated_text: she is to be honored with exalted speech; the rival wives who follow her are subordinate. ||21||

children.text: vrajasukṛtavilāsasāraratnākaravṛṣabhānusujātaśātalakṣmīḥ |
children.translated_text: She is the foremost among the captivating jewels of <s>Hari</s>'s city — born from <s>Vṛṣabhānu</s>, the essence-jewel of <s>Vraja</s>'s meritorious beauty, of cool radiance,

children.text: agharipuramaṇīramāsu mukhyā svayam anurāgavihārahārimūrtiḥ ||22||
children.translated_text: her very form enchanting in the pastimes of love. ||22||

children.text: dayitaghanataḍidvilāsivarṇā priyatamavarṇasva3varṇaśastavastrā |
children.translated_text: Her complexion sports like lightning upon the beloved dark cloud; her garments are praised as matching the hue of her most beloved's color;

children.text: harimaṇitaralādidivyadīvyanmaṇimayabhūṣaṇabhūṣaṇāṅgabhaṅgiḥ ||23||
children.translated_text: her limbs are graced with ornaments of divine, sparkling jewels beginning with emeralds of <s>Hari</s>'s hue. ||23||

children.text: upamitipadavīṃ svam eva yāntīṃ suparimitivyatiśobhitāṅgasaṅghā |
children.translated_text: She who herself becomes the standard of comparison, her assemblage of limbs adorned beyond measure,

children.text: pratikakubhaśubhaṅkaraprathābhiḥ sahajavilakṣaṇāṅkitaśrīḥ ||24||
children.translated_text: marked with innate distinction by her fames that render inauspiciousness beautiful in every direction. ||24||

children.text: śaśikamalarucāṃ padāpi jetrī nijanakhakāntibhir ujjvalena tena |
children.translated_text: She who conquers even the radiance of the moon and lotus with the brilliance of her own nails — through that resplendent [beauty],

children.text: avayavakulam anyad4 anyad astu pratinavarocir upāttakāntacittam ||25||
children.translated_text: let each and every other group of limbs be [acknowledged as] captivating the mind with ever-new luster. ||25||

children.text: sukusumasukumāratāvatāras trijagati saurabhasaurabhākaraśrīḥ |
children.translated_text: An incarnation of delicacy softer than fine flowers, she is the source of the splendor of fragrance among the three worlds;

children.text: ṛtam itamadhurapriyārtharītipravalitavarṇanarītilabdhavarṇā ||26||
children.translated_text: she has obtained her hue through the graceful unfolding of her naturally sweet and beloved manner. ||26||

children.text: sumatim atiguruḥ samastavidyā sakalakalāvalitātinamracittā |
children.translated_text: Of surpassing weight of good sense, [endowed with] all learning, humble-hearted with all arts,

children.text: hriyam anu vinayaṃ nayaṃ samajñām api dadhatī svajanādi śarmadātrī ||27||
children.translated_text: bearing modesty, courtesy, good conduct, and propriety, she bestows happiness upon her own people. ||27||

children.text: nikhilagakaruṇādikair guṇais taṃ svadayitam eva tulāṃ sadāpi dhartrī |
children.translated_text: She who always holds her own beloved as the standard through qualities of compassion and the rest for all beings;

children.text: gurunikaradayāspadātibhaktiḥ sthiracarahārdasukhāmṛtābhiṣiktā ||28||
children.translated_text: whose devotion is supreme, being the object of grace of the multitude of elders — anointed with the nectar of heartfelt joy of all moving and non-moving beings. ||28||

children.text: priyapadanakhakāntileśanirmañchanaparacittadaśāvaśānuvelam |
children.translated_text: Her state of mind constantly absorbed in the polishing with rays of the luster of her beloved's toenails,

children.text: bhramaram api tadīyadūtabuddhyā praṇayajacitragirā vicitrayantī ||29||
children.translated_text: she entertains even a bee, thinking it his messenger, with variegated speech born of love. ||29||

children.text: marud api calati svabhāvataś cet kvacid anukūlatayā nijābhisāre |
children.translated_text: If even the wind naturally stirs, [she takes it as] somehow favorable to her own <s>abhisāra</s> (secret tryst);

children.text: navavidham api tatra bhaktabhāvaṃ vinidadhatī priyabhaktacittasaktā ||30||
children.translated_text: there she places ninefold devotional sentiment, her mind attached to devotion to her beloved. ||30||

children.text: bahir anumitidūrabhāvapūrasvacarita5cārutayā sadāvasantī |
children.translated_text: Outwardly manifesting the appearance of indifference, through the beauty of her own conduct she is ever in spring;

children.text: racayati rahasi priyājane sā svadayitam anv api narmakeliśarma ||31||
children.translated_text: in private, among her beloved's people, she creates even playful amorous joy for her beloved. ||31||

children.text: navabhiḥ
children.translated_text: Nine verses.

children.text: 1. (b) ojanao; 2. (a) vāraṃ vāram; 3. (b) osao; 4. (b) anyam; 5. (b) oracitao;
children.translated_text: 1. (b) saṅgibhaṅgi; 2. jīva has not made sandhi of ṛ. 3. (b) saiva saiva; 4. (b) hṛdaye; 5. (b) vibhāvam; 6. (b) sārdram;

children.text: bhrukuṭinayanabhaṅgisaṅgi1 kutrāpy ativinayaprathi cāṭu kutracic ca |
children.translated_text: Somewhere with a frown and a glance, somewhere with excessive humility, somewhere with flattery —

children.text: vaśayati dayitaṃ hariṃ priyā sā kim idam iti prathanāya nāham īśe ||32||
children.translated_text: the beloved <s>Rādhā</s> brings <s>Hari</s> under her sway — how this happens, I am not able to express. ||32||

children.text: harir api śuśubhe sa yābhir uccair anugatimāditayā sugānadhāmni |
children.translated_text: <s>Hari</s> too shone exceedingly with those [<s>gopīs</s>], in the abode of beautiful singing, in the manner of those who follow from the beginning;

children.text: praṇayaṛṇidaśām2 avāpa yāsāṃ prathatamā khalu tāsu saiva seva3 ||33||
children.translated_text: he attained the state of a debtor of love to them — truly the foremost among them is she alone, in service. ||33||

children.text: śṛṇu guṇam aparaṃ kṛpāvilāsaṃ vṛṣaravijām anu rāsakelinaktam |
children.translated_text: Hear another quality — a pastime of compassion: following the daughter of <s>Vṛṣabhānu</s>, on the night of <s>Rāsa</s> play,

children.text: mararipur amukāṃ nināya dūraṃ nijanayanaṃ bubudhe mudā tu neyam ||34||
children.translated_text: the enemy of <s>Mara</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) led her far away; he understood joyfully that she should be led. ||34||

children.text: tad api tad asahiṣṇavaḥ sapatnyaḥ kim api jajalpur amūr amūṃ vinindya |
children.translated_text: Yet the rival wives, unable to bear that, censuring her, muttered something;

children.text: iyam api tu murārimelanāya svayam upapattim adād amūṣu suṣṭhu ||35||
children.translated_text: but she herself offered the means of reunion with <s>Murāri</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) to them most excellently. ||35||

children.text: yugmakam
children.translated_text: A pair of verses.

children.text: guṇakulam aparaṃ kim aṅga varṇyaṃ harirativāridhibhaṅgasaṅgharūpam |
children.translated_text: What other cluster of virtues should be described, O dear one — having the form of the crashing waves of the ocean of love-play with <s>Hari</s>?

children.text: ayi śṛṇu hṛdaya4 prage ca tasyāś caritam idaṃ mṛdu tatpriyasya cātha ||36||
children.translated_text: O heart, hear now the gentle conduct of hers at dawn, and then of her beloved. ||36||

children.text: anumitam akarod yadālpakalpaṃ rajanivibhāgam5 iyaṃ tadā tu kāntam |
children.translated_text: When she realized that the division of the night was brief,

children.text: akuruta bhujapāśabaddham asrasnapitanibhaṃ kurute sma varṣma cāsya ||37||
children.translated_text: she then held her beloved bound in the noose of her arms — and she made his body as if bathed in tears. ||37||

children.text: atha bahuvinayaṃ dadhan murārinayanapayāṃsy apasārayan amuṣyāḥ |
children.translated_text: Then <s>Murāri</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), showing great tenderness, wiping away her tears,

children.text: svanayanasalilena sārdham6 aṅgaṃ nijam akarot idam iyam apy abhīkṣṇam ||38||
children.translated_text: moistened his own body with the water of his own eyes — and she did the same again and again. ||38||

children.text: tadanu ca lalitāviśākhike dve samavayasāv anayor upetya pārśvam |
children.translated_text: Thereupon the two friends <s>Lalitā</s> and <s>Viśākhā</s>, of equal age, approaching their side,

children.text: ahimakarahimarturaśmitulyāt kharavacanāt paṭu lumpataḥ sma jāḍyam ||39||
children.translated_text: skillfully dispelled the stupor [caused by] harsh words equal to the frost-rays of the cold-rayed [moon]. ||39||

children.text: hriyam iyam abalā tadā tu yātā dayitatanor upagūhanaṃ visṛjya |
children.translated_text: That tender woman, overcome by modesty, then released her embrace of her beloved's body,

children.text: svapanam iva gatā kṣaṇaṃ nirīhā punar iva jāgaraṇaṃ bhayād dadambha ||40||
children.translated_text: and for a moment became as if gone to sleep, motionless; then again she feigned wakefulness out of fear. ||40||

children.text: ahar uditanibhaṃ parāś ca yātā haridayitā harimātaraṃ bhaveyuḥ |
children.translated_text: And the other beloveds of <s>Hari</s>, having departed as if day had dawned — might they become <s>Hari</s>'s mothers [i.e., of proper behavior]?

children.text: iti taduditasambhramād ayāsīd aharudayānugakarmadharmadhāma ||41||
children.translated_text: In the flurry occasioned by his rising, she went to the abode of her duties following the daybreak. ||41||

children.text: rajanivilasitaprasaṅgivāsaḥ kulam ajahāt tad iyaṃ yad eva hṛdyam |
children.translated_text: She abandoned the garments associated with the night's pleasures — those very ones that were delightful —

children.text: aparam akurutāṅgasaṅgi yat skhalayitum7 iṣṭam aho balī tu diṣṭaḥ ||42||
children.translated_text: and put on others that covered her body, wishing to conceal [the signs]; alas, fate is powerful indeed! ||42||

children.text: padakaravadanaṃ muhuḥ punānā yad iha jalaṃ visasarja śubhrapātre |
children.translated_text: Repeatedly purifying her hands, feet, and face, when she here released the water into a bright vessel,

children.text: bhuvam api tad idaṃ bhuvaḥsvarādīny api bhuvanāni sadā punad vibhāti ||43||
children.translated_text: this [water] ever purifies even the earth, and even the heavens of the lord of the earth, and all the worlds. ||43||

children.text: akuruta na paraṃ bahiḥ snihaṃ sā haridayitā muhur antarasnihaṃ ca |
children.translated_text: That beloved of <s>Hari</s> did not apply the external oil often, nor the inner oil [ointment];

children.text: harivapurupayuktatailaśeṣaṃ vinidadhatī khalu yā tulāṃ siṣeve ||44||
children.translated_text: for she who applied the remaining oil used on <s>Hari</s>'s body indeed served as [its] equal. ||44||

children.text: surabhibhir atha mardanāni kṛtvāsnapayad amūm udakena tādṛśena |
children.translated_text: Then, having been massaged with fragrant [substances], she was bathed with water of the same kind;

children.text: sahajasurabhitā tatas tadaṅgād udayam itā vijitā diśaś cakāra ||45||
children.translated_text: the natural fragrance, having risen from her body, conquered all the directions. ||45||

children.text: yugmakam
children.translated_text: A pair of verses.

children.text: tanum anu vavase varāṃśukaṃ sā tadapi tanuś chavim ujjagāra tasyāḥ |
children.translated_text: She then put on an excellent garment upon her body, yet even that garment emitted the radiance of her complexion;

children.text: ghanatatipihite 'pi sūryabimbe diśi diśi rājati tasya raśmisaṅghaḥ ||46||
children.translated_text: even when the disc of the sun is covered by dense clouds, its cluster of rays shines forth in every direction. ||46||

children.text:
athavā,
hariratir atigupyate tayā sā tadapi ca tacchavir īkṣyate bahiś ca |
children.translated_text: Or alternatively: her love-play with <s>Hari</s> is kept most secret by her, yet even that [secret] radiance is visible externally;

children.text: vrajanṛpamithunasya cāṅghritīrthaṃ vrajanṛpates tanayasya ca prapīya |
children.translated_text: Having drunk the holy water from the feet of the couple who are the lord and lady of <s>Vraja</s>, and of the king of <s>Vraja</s>'s son,

children.text: japavidhivihitadvivarṇamantrā harijananīm avalokituṃ pratasthe ||48||
children.translated_text: with the <s>mantra</s> of two syllables performed according to the method of <s>japa</s>, she set out to behold <s>Hari</s>'s mother. ||48||

the diverse jewel-ornaments delight those companion friends of the beautiful-eyed one — thus this is so. And here, the joyous ornament of horripilation, ignited by the remembrance of <s>Hari</s>'s qualities — what shall I praise? ||47||

children.text: atha harijananīṃ prati prayātāpy abhimukham eti na sā sakhīvṛtāpi |
children.translated_text: Then, having proceeded toward <s>Hari</s>'s mother, she does not approach her directly, even though surrounded by her companions;

children.text: api tu kuṭilavartmanānugamya praṇamati tatpadayor nidhāya bhālam ||49||
children.translated_text: rather, following a winding path, she bows, placing her forehead at those [mother's] feet. ||49||

children.text: atha harijananī svayaṃ karābhyāṃ śirasi samunnamite sayatnam asyāḥ |
children.translated_text: Then <s>Hari</s>'s mother herself, with her own hands, with effort lifts her head;

children.text: parimalam upalabhya sāsram enāṃ pihitatanuṃ parirabhyanandati sma ||50||
children.translated_text: perceiving her fragrance, with tears she embraces this veiled one and rejoices. ||50||

children.text: tadanu tadupadeśataḥ samastāṃ guruvanitām avanamya ramyacittā |
children.translated_text: Thereupon, at her instruction, she bows to all the elder women, her mind charmed;

children.text: pṛthag upaviśatī samastadṛṣṭīr aharata candramukhī cakoratulyāḥ ||51||
children.translated_text: sitting separately, the moon-faced one drew all gazes to herself, like <s>cakora</s> birds [drawn to the moon]. ||51||

children.text: yadapi muhur iyaṃ sadānubhūtā tadapi tadā milatī pratisvam ārdram |
children.translated_text: Though she is ever experienced [in this], even so, meeting each one individually with tenderness,

children.text: rajani virahitā2 ca kāravarṣājanir iva gharmakanīyasī samastam ||52||
children.translated_text: separated [from <s>Hari</s>] during the night — like the junior season of rains after the hot season — she [refreshes] everything. ||52||

children.text: iti sati carite haripriyāyā haricaritaṃ śṛṇu citta varṇayāmi |
children.translated_text: Thus, in the conduct of <s>Hari</s>'s beloved, hear now, O mind — I shall describe <s>Hari</s>'s conduct;

children.text: gṛhagatavibhave suvarṇite syād gṛhapativarṇanam āśu saukhyadāyi ||53||
children.translated_text: when the glory of the house has been described, the description of the householder should quickly bring happiness. ||53||

children.text: haridayitatamā yadāśu talpād dinamukhakṛtyakṛte kṛteham āsīt3 |
children.translated_text: When the most beloved of <s>Hari</s> quickly rose from the bed and performed the morning duties, saying 'I have finished' —

children.text: harir api sa tadā tadartham ātmapriyasakhadāsagaṇena sevyate sma ||54||
children.translated_text: <s>Hari</s> too was then attended for the same purpose by his beloved friends and servant-groups. ||54||

children.text: sa rajanivasanaṃ sasarja tac ca sphuṭam iva sūcayati sma gūḍhavṛttam |
children.translated_text: He cast off the night garments, and those [garments] seemed to openly hint at the secret activities;

children.text: iha ca tad idam antaraṅgam itthaṃ piśunam itīva tadā smitaṃ suhṛdbhiḥ ||55||
children.translated_text: and here this innermost [garment], thus becoming a tell-tale — thereupon there was smiling by his friends. ||55||

children.text: mukhakaracaraṇaṃ hareḥ sudhautaṃ kamalavanāni jigāya tac ca paśya |
children.translated_text: The face, hands, and feet of <s>Hari</s>, well-washed, surpassed the lotus groves — and behold!

children.text: vrajam anu kamalālayāpi yasya śrayati rajaḥ padayor yathātra vandī ||56||
children.translated_text: even <s>Kamalālaya</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>, she who dwells on the lotus) resorts to the dust of his feet throughout <s>Vraja</s>, like a panegyrist. ||56||

children.text: bahuvidham api tailam iṣṭagandhaṃ dhṛtam abhitaḥ sa vidagdhatānidigdhaḥ |
children.translated_text: Various kinds of fragrant oil were applied all around him — he who is anointed with cleverness;

children.text: surabhitam iha rādhayā tu devyā svayam urarīkurute sma kṛṣṇacandraḥ ||57||
children.translated_text: but the one perfumed by the divine <s>Rādhā</s> herself — that <s>Kṛṣṇacandra</s> accepted upon his chest. ||57||

children.text: tad aghajiti sutailam ādadāne samajani pūṣitā na tat tu citram |
children.translated_text: When the conqueror of <s>Agha</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) accepted that oil, it became honored — that is not wonderful;

children.text: prathamam api sa tan mudābhijighrann agamad amūdṛśatāṃ tad eva citram ||58||
children.translated_text: but that he first joyfully smelled it and thereby attained such a state — that indeed is wonderful. ||58||

children.text: sa śucisurabhiṇā jalena siktaṃ svavapur akārayad īdṛśaṃ vidhātum |
children.translated_text: His body was sprinkled with pure, fragrant water — he caused it to be done in this manner;

children.text: ahaha śṛṇu manas tad eva tat tad guṇamahasā samabhūd atīvasāndram ||59||
children.translated_text: O listen, mind! That very [water] became extremely dense with the splendor of those qualities. ||59||

children.text: haritanum anu mārjanaṃ vidhitsan mṛdur iyam ity adhigatya kampate sma |
children.translated_text: Wishing to dry <s>Hari</s>'s body, understanding 'this is tender,' he [the attendant] trembled;

children.text: jalaguruvasanaṃ visarjayaṃs taddvayam aparaṃ sa dadhat4 praphullati sma ||60||
children.translated_text: removing the water-heavy garment and applying another pair, he bloomed with joy. ||60||

children.text: kanakanibhapaṭadvayaṃ paṭīyān paridadhad ambudarocir uptakeśaḥ |
children.translated_text: The more skillful one, placing a pair of golden-hued garments [on him], [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>] with cloud-like luster, with hair combed upward —

children.text: satilakalaghubhūṣaṇaḥ svakāntyā trijagati kāntidayā sakhīn didhinva ||61||
children.translated_text: wearing a <s>tilaka</s> mark, lightly ornamented, by his own radiance bestowed the gift of beauty upon his companions throughout the three worlds.

children.text: harir atha kanakāsane niviśya vyaracayad ācamanaṃ yathā nidiṣṭam |
children.translated_text: Then <s>Hari</s>, having seated himself upon a golden seat, performed <s>ācamana</s> (ritual sipping of water) as prescribed;

children.text: paridadhad upavītam anyad āsīj japam anu sandadhad apy adīpi tatra ||62||
children.translated_text: he put on another sacred thread, and after performing <s>japa</s> (mantra repetition), a lamp was also lit there.

children.text: yadupuram anu yat pradhānabhāvaṃ harir akaroj janake 'pi vidyamāne |
children.translated_text: That <s>Hari</s> assumed the principal role in <s>Yadupura</s> (the city of the Yadus) even while his father was present;

children.text: taducitam ucitaṃ tu nātra yasmāt pitṛsutatāgatatāratamyam asti ||63||
children.translated_text: that was fitting, for it is fitting here since there exists a gradation of superiority between father and son.

children.text: 1. this line not found in (b); 2. cirahitā; 3. (b) kṛtehayāsīt; 4. (a) dadatvraja-pati-mithune1 sadāpi bālyaṃ harim anucintayad evam āha nityam |
children.translated_text: [Textual notes] The royal couple of <s>Vraja</s> always contemplated <s>Hari</s> in his childhood, and would say this constantly:

children.text: vayam iha2 sukṛtāni yāni kurmaḥ pratinidhayas tava tatra na svatantrāḥ ||64||
children.translated_text: 'Whatever meritorious deeds we perform here — they are your representatives there, not independent.'

children.text: iti harir iha nātidharmakarmāṇy uṣasi karoti pituḥ pramodakārī |
children.translated_text: Thus <s>Hari</s>, performing here his rituals that go beyond mere duty, at dawn, causing delight to his father,

children.text: api tu tadanumodanānukūlāṃ bhavikakṛtiṃ vidadhāti mātur agre ||65||
children.translated_text: moreover, he performs before his mother a devotional act that is favorable to her approval.

children.text: harir atha calati sma mātṛpārśvam saha sakhibhir dhvanayan bhūṣaṇāni |
children.translated_text: Then <s>Hari</s> went toward his mother's side, together with his companions, making his ornaments jingle;

children.text: sa tad avakalayan vadhūnikāyaḥ sapadi sasāra rahasyapākadhāma ||66||
children.translated_text: perceiving that, the group of young brides immediately proceeded to the kitchen of secret preparations.

children.text:
atha harijananī hariṃ nirīkṣya vrajamahilābhir iyāya tasya pārśvam |
sutam anugamanaṃ vyaloki dhenoḥ samam anayā natarāṃ gavāṃ param āsām||67||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Hari's</s> mother, seeing <s>Hari</s>, went to his side with the women of <s>Vraja</s>; she saw her son's following like that of a cow, and even more so — she [regarded him] as the supreme among all the cows.

children.text:
padam anu patanaṃ bhaven na tasyāḥ savidhajuṣā hariṇā drutaṃ milantyāḥ
iti harir avanamya dūradeśāc ciram iva tadvad atiṣṭhad iṣṭabhaktiḥ3 ||68||
children.translated_text: Lest she stumble at every step as she rushed to meet <s>Hari</s> who was nearby — with this [concern], <s>Hari</s>, whose devotion was dear, bowed from a great distance and stood still for what seemed a long time.

children.text: drutam atha jananī tam etya putraṃ drutam udanīnayad4 āgrahaṃ dadhānā |
children.translated_text: Then the mother, coming swiftly to that son, swiftly drew him close, holding him firmly,

children.text: tadanu ca suciraṃ prasajya mūrdhni sravadudakākṣiyugaṃ tam āluloke ||69||
children.translated_text: and then, pressing him to her head for a long time, with eyes streaming with tears, she gazed upon him.

children.text: harir avakalayan sarohiṇīkā vrajamahilā jananīsamānabhāvāḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Hari</s>, perceiving that the women of <s>Vraja</s>, together with <s>Rohiṇī</s>, had the same feelings as his mother,

children.text: tadanuguṇakabhaktibhāg amūṣāṃ namanakṛdasrajalena sicyate sma ||70||
children.translated_text: partaking of their devotion in accord with their disposition, bowing, was sprinkled by them with tears.

children.text: atha balavalitāḥ pare sakhāyaḥ sahamadhumaṅgalakāḥ samāgatās te |
children.translated_text: Then the other companions, strong and spirited, along with <s>Madhumaṅgala</s>, arrived;

children.text: yad ajitam abhajaṃs tad ahni citraṃ vidhum anuṣajya subhagrahā virejuḥ ||71||
children.translated_text: that day when they worshipped the unconquerable one was wonderful — like stars following the moon, they shone as the fortunate ones.

children.text: atha punar upaveśam āgatās te haribalamātṛmukhāḥ sukhād aśeṣāḥ |
children.translated_text: Then, having come to sit down, all [the party] headed by the mothers of <s>Hari</s> and <s>Bala</s> (Balarāma), happily;

children.text: haribalavalitā yathāsvam āsann adhi vividhāsanam udyadasranetrāḥ ||72||
children.translated_text: accompanied by <s>Hari</s> and <s>Bala</s>, they took their respective seats, with eyes brimming with tears.

children.text: atha purugurudāralambhitāśīr baṭusahitāḥ pratipadya viprabhāryāḥ |
children.translated_text: Then the wives of the <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, having received blessings invoked by the revered elders, together with the young students;

children.text: valayitasakalaḥ sarāmakṛṣṇaḥ praṇamanasaṅgatam unnaman didhinva ||73||
children.translated_text: Śrī <s>Rāma</s> (Balarāma) and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, embraced by all, bowing with folded hands and rising, bestowed [their grace].

children.text: dvijakulamahilā baṭupradhānā dinadinam āśiṣam adbhutāṃ dadānāḥ |
children.translated_text: The women of the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> families, led by the young students, bestowing wondrous blessings day after day,

children.text: tadudayam api śaśvad īkṣamāṇā vidadhati sākṣatalājapuṣpavṛṣṭim ||74||
children.translated_text: ever gazing upon his rising, showered a rain of parched rice, <s>akṣata</s> (unbroken grains), and flowers.

children.text: harir atha kapilāḥ sanavyavatsā rajatakhuraprakarāḥ suvarṇaśṛṅgāḥ |
children.translated_text: Then <s>Hari</s>, having worshipped tawny cows with new calves, with hooves of silver and horns of gold,

children.text: vividhamaṇibhūṣaṇāḥ samarcya dvijabaṭusādakarod vidhānayuktam ||75||
children.translated_text: adorned with various gems, performed their offering to the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> students in the proper ritual manner.

children.text: dhṛtamaṇinavakaṃ suvarṇapātraṃ ghṛtaparipūritabhūrikāntimadhyam |
children.translated_text: A golden vessel set with nine gems, filled with ghee of great splendor in the middle,

children.text: paricitamukhabimbabimbam īśas tithigaṇakāya dideśa deśarūpam ||76||
children.translated_text: reflecting his face like a mirror — the Lord presented it to the astrologer as a suitable gift.

children.text: dvijakulajasatīr baṭūṃś ca kṛṣṇaḥ praṇamana5pūrvakam īpsayābhinandya |
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, having honored the virtuous women of <s>brāhmaṇa</s> families and the students with salutation first, with affectionate desire, and greeted them,

children.text: madhurataragirā visṛjya dhāmne nijajananīrucimaṅgalaṃ pupoṣa ||77||
children.translated_text: and sent them home with words sweeter still, he nourished the auspicious joy dear to his own mother.

children.text: janayitṛjananīsvasṛḥ pitṛvyādikavanitāś ca vadhūsutāvimiśrāḥ |
children.translated_text: The women — mother, father's sisters, aunts, and other women, mingled with brides and their children —

children.text: anunayavinayapraṇāmapūjādibhir upaveśatayā harir didhinva ||78||
children.translated_text: <s>Hari</s> honored them all, sitting together, with entreaty, propriety, salutation, and worship.

children.text: iti purukṛtamaṅgalaḥ sa kṛṣṇaḥ svakagṛhanirmitatatkṛtir balaś ca |
children.translated_text: Thus <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, having performed many auspicious [rites], having accomplished the duties created in his own home, and <s>Bala</s> (Balarāma) too,

children.text: sakhicitam ucitapradeśam añcann aśanavidhiṃ vidhinā vidhitsati sma ||79||
children.translated_text: going to a suitable place chosen by his friends, wished to commence the meal in the proper manner.

children.text: asitakuṭilakeśaveśabhaṅgījanajanalobhanaśobhayā manojñam |
children.translated_text: With charming dark curly hair, tresses, and locks that enchant all people with their beauty, his incomparable face,

children.text: nirupamavadanaṃ6 sanīlaśubhracchavi savilāsasaśoṇakoṇanetram ||81||
children.translated_text: with the radiance of blue and fair [complexion], with playful eyes whose corners are reddish —

children.text: 1. (b) omithunaṃ; 2. (b) api; 3. (a) obhakti; 4. (a) udanīnamamat; 5. (a) praṇamanaṃ; 6. (b) ovadanaḥ
children.translated_text: [Textual notes and variant readings]

children.text: alakavitatabhālamaṇḍitapuṇḍraṃ pṛthutaranīradamuktaṃ muktanāsam |
children.translated_text: his forehead covered by locks, adorned with the <s>puṇḍra</s> (tilaka mark), [his nose] like a pearl released from a vast cloud,

children.text: maṇigaṇamayakuṇḍalaprabhābhiḥ śavalitagaṇḍarucātirocituṇḍam ||82||
children.translated_text: his cheeks illuminated by the splendor of jeweled earrings, his face exceedingly resplendent —

children.text: galavalayavibhūṣaṇātiramyaṃ maṇisaramadhyanibaddharatnavaryam |
children.translated_text: exceedingly lovely with the ornament of a necklace around the throat, with the best of gems fastened in the middle of the gem-strand,

children.text: valayavilasadūrmikāṅgadānāṃ cchavicaladūrmibhujadvayāticāru ||83||
children.translated_text: with the beauty of arms [adorned with] bracelets, shining finger-rings, and armlets, with waves of radiance playing upon his two arms — extremely beautiful —

children.text: nṛharivadavalagnalagnakāñcīstavakacalāñcalacañcadaṃsujālam1 |
children.translated_text: with a waist-belt clinging as if to <s>Nṛhari</s> (the Man-Lion form), with tassels of the swinging girdle and the dancing network of garment-edges,

children.text: kanakaghanajidantarāṃśukāṃśaspṛśamaṇinūpurakāntipūrapūrṇam ||84||
children.translated_text: with anklets of gems touching the hem of the under-garment between [the legs], surpassing gold in density — filled with the flood of their radiance —

children.text: abhimukham upaviṣṭam iṣṭapārasparikanirīkṣaṇākṣiyugmam |
children.translated_text: seated facing [the viewer], his pair of eyes gazing with the glance of one cherished and cherishing,

children.text: navaghanaghanasārakāntipradavapurunnatadāsajuṣṭapṛṣṭam ||85||
children.translated_text: his body having the beauty of the essence of a fresh cloud, his back attended by exalted servants —

children.text: vividhavidhavicitramitrapaṅktidvayaracitadravatarṣimātṛharṣi |
children.translated_text: with two rows of varied and wondrous friends arranged on either side, creating delight for the overflowing sages and mothers,

children.text: nijanijavadhudṛśyadṛśyarūpaṃ rahasi vinirmitajālavantravṛndāt ||86||
children.translated_text: his form visible as their own to each of his own brides — from a privately constructed lattice screen —

children.text: svayam api samiṣaṃ nirīkṣamāṇaṃ tadanugavākṣakulaṃ kriyākulākṣam |
dinamukham adhikṛtya bhavyakṛtyaṃ smara sahajadvayam iṣṭamiṣṭabhukti |87||
children.translated_text: devoted to the auspicious duty at the beginning of the day, remember this innate pair [<s>Rāma</s> and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>], [partaking of] the desired, the cherished food.
he himself, gazing at the offerings with rice, his eyes busy looking through the window-lattice —

children.text: saptabhiḥ
children.translated_text: With seven verses

children.text: bahuṣu dinamukheṣu goṣu śīghraṃ vrajanam iti vrajabhūbhṛtā subhojyam |
children.translated_text: On many mornings, since the cows must go swiftly to <s>Vraja</s>, the fine food [is served];

children.text: svayam aśanakṛtā praheyam ity apy aśanam idaṃ laghu vaṣṭi kṛṣṇacandraḥ ||88||
children.translated_text: though the self-prepared meal is to be offered first — this modest meal <s>Kṛṣṇacandra</s> (Moon-like Kṛṣṇa) relishes.

children.text: atha maricasitāsitāṃśumiśraṃ ghṛtaparamānnam adann asāv amībhiḥ |
children.translated_text: Then, eating the supreme rice pudding mixed with pepper and white and dark seasonings, he with these [companions],

children.text: nijarucim iyatā nicāyayaṃś ca pratikavalaṃ praśaśaṃsa kaṃsaśatruḥ ||89||
children.translated_text: spreading his own luster by that measure, praised each morsel — the enemy of <s>Kaṃsa</s>.

children.text: navavadhūnihitaṃ balasya mātrā svayam upanīya dhṛtaṃ vrajādhirājñyām |
children.translated_text: That [food] placed by the new brides, brought personally by <s>Bala's</s> (Balarāma's) mother, and held by the queen of <s>Vraja</s> —

children.text: akuruta pariveṣaṇaṃ tathā sā lavam api nātra yathā sa hātum aiṣṭa ||90||
children.translated_text: she served it in such a way that he did not wish to abandon even a morsel.

children.text: saparimalajalaṃ tathā jananyor mṛdu mṛdu jalpavikāsimandahāsam |
children.translated_text: With fragrant water, and with the two mothers, gently and gently, with conversation, blooming and soft laughter,

children.text: anubhavad iha rāmakṛṣṇayugmaṃ kramam anu bhojanatṛṣṇatām ahāsīt ||91||
children.translated_text: the pair <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> experienced [the meal] here; step by step, the thirst for eating subsided.

children.text: punar api jananīdvayī śiśūnām aśanarasaṃ vyatihāsanāt pupoṣa |
children.translated_text: Again, the two mothers nourished the relish for eating of the boys through mutual jest;

children.text: harir atha ca gavāvanāya khelāvanagamanāya ca taṃ kramāt tatāra ||92||
children.translated_text: then <s>Hari</s> gradually crossed over [from the meal] toward tending the cows, and toward play and going to the forest.

children.text: parimalajaladhautavaktrabimbā navaharicandanacārucarcitāṅgāḥ |
children.translated_text: With face-mirrors washed with fragrant water, their beautiful limbs anointed with fresh <s>haricandana</s> (sandalwood),

children.text: khapuraphanidalīpuṭībhir ete surabhitarañjitam ūhur āsyamadhyam ||93||
children.translated_text: these [boys], with cups of camphor and betel-leaf, bore the most fragrant and delightful [substances] in the center of their mouths.

children.text: vrajanṛpatibhṛtibhuk2kumāravṛndārpitamaharābharaṇāñcikañcukādi |
children.translated_text: The group of boys, servants of the king of <s>Vraja</s>, offered great ornaments, jacket-garments, and the like;

children.text: sutatanum anu sā virājayantī jananayanāny akarod virājitāni ||94||
children.translated_text: she, adorning [<s>Kṛṣṇa's</s>] slender body, made the eyes of all people adorned [with delight].

children.text: tam asitamaṇikāntidehakāntisnapitasuvarṇajavarṇakāntavastram |
children.translated_text: Seeing him — his body-luster of dark sapphire hue bathing the golden-hued, splendid garment —

children.text: svaviracitavibhūṣaṇaṃ nirīkṣya stananayanād amṛtāny avoḍha mātā ||95||
children.translated_text: adorned with self-fashioned ornaments, the mother drew nectar from her breast-eyes.

children.text: maṇirucimuralīsuvaṛnayaṣṭipravaraśikhaṇḍakaśobhayā tu3 kṛṣṇaḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, with the beauty of a gem-bright flute, a golden staff, and an excellent peacock feather,

children.text: asukhayad avarodhalokadṛṣṭiṃ sukhayitum ittham iyeṣa sabhyadṛṣṭim4 ||96||
children.translated_text: saddened the eyes of the inner quarters' women, [yet] wished thus to gladden the eyes of the courtiers.

children.text: harim anukathanīyam atra yad yad balam anu tat tad avehi kintu yogyam |
children.translated_text: Whatever is to be narrated about <s>Hari</s> here, know all of that as equally applicable to <s>Bala</s> (Balarāma), but [each] as fitting;

children.text: haribalajananīyugaṃ ca tulyaṃ parikalaya priyatā hi tatra tulyā ||97||
children.translated_text: and consider the pair of mothers of <s>Hari</s> and <s>Bala</s> as equal, for the dearness [of each son to his mother] is indeed equal.

children.text: dinadinam anu sāvanāya gantuṃ kṛtamanasas tanayasya maṅgalāya |
children.translated_text: Day after day, for the sake of the auspicious departure of her son who has set his mind on going to the forest,

children.text: sajalakalasadīpasāram ārātrikamukhamaṅgalavastu visṛṇoti ||98||
children.translated_text: she sends forth auspicious items beginning with <s>āratrika</s> (waving of lamps), with water-filled vessels and lamps as the essence.

children.text: 1. (b) jaladāṃśujālam; 2. (b) obhṛtibhṛto; 3. (b) ca; 4. (a) osṛṣṭim;
children.translated_text: [Textual notes and variant readings]

children.text: atha calitamanāḥ svamātur ārād aracayad añjalim acyutaḥ praṇamya |
children.translated_text: Then <s>Acyuta</s> (the Unfailing One), his mind stirring, departing from his mother's side, offered a salutation with folded hands,

children.text: iyam avamṛśatī kareṇa cāmūṃ stananayanāmṛtasārdham āha cedam ||99||
children.translated_text: and she, stroking him with her hand, together with the nectar of her breast-eyes, spoke thus:

children.text: "vayam api bhavatā samaṃ prayāmaḥ kṛtapacanaṃ drutam uṣṇam arpayāmaḥ |
children.translated_text: "We too shall go along with you; we shall quickly offer the freshly cooked hot [food];

children.text: pariṇatavayasaś cirād abhūma prathayasi lajjitam atra kiṃ nu vatsa ||100||
children.translated_text: we have grown old with the passing of time — why do you put us to shame in this matter, O child?

children.text: yadi vadati bhavān svadhāmni kā syād avasaram āvakayos tadā vidadhyām |
children.translated_text: If you say [we should remain] in our own home, then who would create the opportunity for us two?

children.text: gṛham aham ahani kvacādhivatsyāmy atha balasūr api vatsyati kva cāpi ||101||
children.translated_text: I shall stay at home on some day, and <s>Bala's</s> mother too will stay on some other day.

children.text: katham iva vadasi tvam etad evaṃ gṛhakṛtir uddhatim āpsyatīti vatsa |
children.translated_text: How can you say it thus — that the household work will become agitated, O child?

children.text: tava vanagamane punas tad etat kim api na sidhyati pṛcchyatām idaṃ ca ||102||
children.translated_text: When you go to the forest, this [household work] simply does not get accomplished — let this also be asked about.

children.text: aharahar ayatāṃ vanāni vatsaḥ svasadanavāsasukhaṃ tyajāva nāvām |
children.translated_text: Day after day the child goes to the forests — let him abandon the happiness of dwelling in his own home for us two;

children.text: itimati pitarāv amū na śaṅkāṃ na ca hriyam atra labhāvahe tanūja ||"103||
children.translated_text: in this way, [thinking about] the two parents, we harbor neither apprehension nor shame, O son."

children.text: iti sa tu jananīritaṃ niśamya smitavalitaṃ dhṛtabāṣpam ālalāpa |
children.translated_text: He, hearing what his mother said, spoke with a smile and restrained tears:

children.text: "dvividaripur api praṇamramūrdhnā1 mṛdu tadanūditam antarā cacāra ||104||
children.translated_text: "Even <s>Dvividāri</s> (the demon Dvivida), with bowed head, gently enacted what she said, in between.

children.text: janani yadi pitā tathā ca mātā pariṇamati sma śiśur babhūva yogyaḥ |
children.translated_text: O mother, if the father and mother have matured thus, then the child has become worthy;

children.text: śiśur ayam ubhayatra tatra rājanyati yadi tarhi vibhāti suṣṭhu yogyaḥ ||105||
children.translated_text: this child, [residing] in both places — if he so reigns, then he truly shines as fully worthy.

children.text: vanam anu dhavalāvanāya mādṛk yad aṭati tanmiṣasiddhim amba viddhi | sukhaviharaṇam eva tatra sārdhaṃ sakhibhir amībhir anukṣaṇaṃ bibharti ||106||
children.translated_text: O mother, know this — that the attainment accomplished under the pretext of my going to the forest for the tending of the white [cows] and such, [consists of] happy sport there with these companions at every moment.

children.text: vipinam anu vihāpitaṃ bhavatyo janani caturvidham annajātam admaḥ |
children.translated_text: O mother, the four kinds of food prepared and sent by you to the forest — we eat [it];

children.text: amṛtajayiphalāni yena vanyāny abhirucim attum ayāma2 tatra bhūri ||107||
children.translated_text: through that, the forest fruits that conquer nectar — we go there with great relish to eat them abundantly.

children.text: vrajaripukulamūlam āśu hantuṃ punar agamaṃ3 punar āgamaṃ vrajaṃ ca |
children.translated_text: Moreover, I went again to swiftly slay the root of the enemies of <s>Vraja</s>, and I came back to <s>Vraja</s>;

children.text: ajani ca jagatām adṛśya eṣa sphuratu kathaṃ bata mātar atha bhītiḥ ||108||
children.translated_text: and though I became invisible to the worlds — how, alas, O mother, can fear arise?

children.text: ahaha bata gavāṃ kulaṃ samastaṃ mama pathi tiṣṭhati madgatiṃ pratīkṣya |
children.translated_text: Alas! The entire herd of cows stands on my path, awaiting my movement;

children.text: mayi gatavati śaṣpam atti caivaṃ hṛdi mama dhīradaśām aśāśyate sma ||"109||
children.translated_text: when I have gone, they eat the grass — and thus they cause a state of steadfast courage to shine in my heart."

children.text: atha harijananīṃ purandhri4mānyātatir avadad dhṛtanīravṛṣṭidṛṣṭi |
"bhavikam anu manuṣva nityakṛtyaṃ bhavati tad eva gatiḥ parāvarā ca |"110||
children.translated_text: "Follow the devotional daily duty with propriety — that itself is the goal, both higher and lower."
Then the assembly of honored matrons addressed <s>Hari's</s> mother, with eyes holding a rain of tears:

children.text: tanujam anu purandhribhiḥ śubhāśīrvratatir akāri tataḥ svayaṃ tu mātā |
children.translated_text: After the son, the assembly of matrons performed the rite of auspicious blessings; then the mother herself,

children.text: vidhṛtakaratayāṅganāya sāsrāpy amum avatārayati sma mandamandam ||111||
children.translated_text: holding his hand, weeping, slowly, slowly escorted him down [to the doorway].

children.text: spṛśati diśati vāñchati prayāti praṇayati mandati nandati bravīti |
children.translated_text: She touches, she gives, she yearns, she goes forward, she shows affection, she slows down, she rejoices, she speaks —

children.text: iti bahuvidhalālanāṃ dadhānā sutam anu sā jananī na tṛptim āpa ||112||
children.translated_text: thus performing many kinds of caressing, that mother toward her son did not attain satisfaction.

children.text: atha guruvanitāgaṇena mātrāpy anusaraṇād avarodha5setum āptaḥ |
children.translated_text: Then, having reached the boundary of the inner quarters through the following of the group of elder women and the mother,

children.text: praṇayaviṣarabandhatas tu dāmodarapadavīṃ punar eṣa śaśvad āpa ||113||
children.translated_text: <s>Dāmodara</s> (Kṛṣṇa, bound by the rope of love), from the binding of the rope of affection, again and again attained the path of being bound.

children.text: atha harigamane krameṇa siddhe harijananī nijageham eva gatvā |
children.translated_text: Then, as <s>Hari's</s> departure was gradually accomplished, <s>Hari's</s> mother, going only to her own home,

children.text: gṛhakṛtikalanān nināya kālaṃ vṛṣaravijā caritāni tu smarāmi ||114||
children.translated_text: spent the time in the arrangement of household duties — and I remember the exploits of the son of <s>Vṛṣabhānu</s> (i.e., <s>Rādhā</s>).

children.text: yadavadhi harir eti mātṛpārśvaṃ tadavadhi sā ca parāś ca jālarandhrāt |
children.translated_text: From the moment <s>Hari</s> reaches his mother's side, from that moment she and the others, through the lattice window,

children.text: harim avakalayanti yatra sarvā muhur api moham ayanti saṃharanti ||115||
children.translated_text: keep watching <s>Hari</s>, where all of them repeatedly become faint and then recover.

children.text: 1. (a) mūrdhā; 2. (b) uttamayāma; 3. (a) puragamaṃ; 4. (a) puredhrio; 5. (b) avarodhio
children.translated_text: [Textual notes and variant readings]

children.text: yad anupadam iyaṃ tadāryapatnyāṃ dayitakṛte vinidhāya divyam annam |
children.translated_text: What she [does] at every step then — having placed divine food [in trust] with the noble wife for the sake of her beloved one,

children.text: sukham anubhavati sma tat tu māṃ ca kṣipati sudhājaladhāv aho kva yāmi ||116||
children.translated_text: she experiences happiness in that; but that also casts me into the ocean of nectar — alas, where shall I go?

children.text: tadaśanam anu yad vihāsajalpaṃ harikṛtam anvadhita svakarṇayugmam |
children.translated_text: And then, after the meal, the jesting and laughter that <s>Hari</s> performed — my two ears have absorbed [it];

children.text: smitanayanayugaṃ tathā nijālīḥ prati tad idaṃ mama cittam āvṛṇoti ||117||
children.translated_text: with smiling pair of eyes, thus toward his own companions — that [memory] envelops my mind.

children.text: harir ahaha tadā vanaṃ prayātuṃ nijatanum āstṛta divyavastralakṣmyā |
children.translated_text: <s>Hari</s>, ah!, then preparing to go to the forest, adorned his own body with the splendor of divine garments;

children.text: iyam asahanamānasā sapatnyām iva nidadhe sakaṭākṣam akṣi tasyām ||118||
children.translated_text: she, unable to bear [it], as if [glancing] at a co-wife, cast a sidelong glance upon that [garment]. ||118||
