children.text: sa vipinagataye yadāpy udasthād adhita dhṛtiṃ nahi tarhi khañjanākṣī |
children.translated_text: When he rose to go to the forest, the wagtail-eyed one could not maintain composure;

children.text: vapur iva jahatā svacetasā taṃ prasajati sā sma vanāya nirgamāya ||119||
children.translated_text: as if her consciousness were leaving her body, she followed him as he went forth to the forest. ||119||

children.text: sarasijadṛg athāṅgane 'vatīrṇaḥ smitam amṛtaṃ vicakāra yarhi dikṣu |
children.translated_text: Then, when the lotus-eyed one descended into the courtyard and cast his nectarine smile in all directions,

children.text: iyam atularuciḥ sakhīṣu guptā svanayanam añjalim ācacāra tarhi ||120||
children.translated_text: she, of incomparable beauty, hidden among her companions, offered the cupped offering of her eyes. ||120||

children.text: murajiti nirite varāvarodhād guruvanitāsu nivṛtya cāgatāsu |
children.translated_text: When the slayer of <s>Mura</s> departed from the excellent inner quarters and the elder ladies returned after turning back,

children.text: iyam atha lalitādibhiḥ svagehaṃ prati gamitāgamayat klamena kālam ||121||
children.translated_text: she was then led home by <s>Lalitā</s> and the others, and passed the time in languor. ||121||

children.text: prathamam ajitam īkṣate gavākṣāt tad anu ca varṇayati priyābhir eṣā |
children.translated_text: First she beholds the unconquered one from the window, then describes [him] to her dear friends;

children.text: iha muhur api tarṣadharṣam asyāḥ puru dadhad akṣiyugaṃ na śāntim eti ||122||
children.translated_text: her pair of eyes, repeatedly bearing the agitation of thirst for him, does not attain peace. ||122||

children.text: sṛjati harikṛte sahāramālyādy atulam iyaṃ nijasaṅginīsahāyā |
children.translated_text: She fashions garlands and the like, incomparable, for <s>Hari</s>'s sake, assisted by her companions;

children.text: hariguṇagaṇagānaṃ apy apūrvaṃ mṛdu vidadhāti tathāpi naiti śāntim ||123||
children.translated_text: she also composes extraordinary, gentle songs about the multitude of <s>Hari</s>'s virtues — yet even so, she does not attain peace. ||123||

children.text: mṛgamadatilakā sa1nīlaratnaśrutiyugalābharaṇā ghanābhavastrā |
children.translated_text: Adorned with a musk-dot mark on the forehead, earrings of blue gems on both ears, wearing garments dark as a cloud,

children.text: harivasanasanābhikāntir eṣā svakaratidīpanatāṃ svayaṃ jagāma ||123
children.translated_text: she, of beauty resembling the garments of <s>Hari</s>, herself became a lamp illuminating her own [arts of love]. ||123||

children.text: jagur iha harirāgi rādhikāyāś caritam anūtanam ālayaḥ prasajya |
children.translated_text: The women of the household sang the unprecedented love-story of <s>Rādhikā</s>, devoted to <s>Hari</s>;

children.text: svayam iyam api tatra tāsu kasyāścid api jagāv anurāgipūrvarāgam ||1242
children.translated_text: she herself, among them, sang the <s>pūrvarāga</s> (first awakening of love) of some [unnamed] lover. ||124||

children.text: murajiti jananīgṛhāt prayāte vanam anu varṣavarān susakhyadigdhān |
children.translated_text: When the slayer of <s>Mura</s> departed from his mother's house to the forest, the fair-browed one assigned

children.text: avasaram anu veṣabhaṅgibhāṣādiṣu vadhupuṃstulitān dideśa subhrūḥ ||125
children.translated_text: the best of year-companions, anointed with [the marks of] good friendship, matching brides and men in attire, gesture, speech, and the like, according to the occasion. ||125||

children.text: "pratinidhitanavaḥ stha yūyam asmākam iti nijaprabhunā samaṃ prayāta |
children.translated_text: "You are our representatives — go together with your master;

children.text: prabhum api tam upetya madvidhārhaṃ paricaraṇaṃ kuruta vyatiprasajya ||
children.translated_text: and approaching that master, perform the service worthy of one such as me, with devoted attachment.

children.text: muhur atha ca bhavādṛg eka ekaḥ sucaritam asya nirīkṣya naḥ sametu |"
iti tad anumataḥ sa sakramāt taṃ muhur anubhūya jagāda tām upetya ||127||
children.translated_text: Thus instructed, they, having experienced him step by step, came and reported to her upon return. ||127||
And then, one by one, each of you resembling him, having observed his good conduct, come back to us."

children.text: atha harir agamat pituḥ sabhāyāṃ divijagaṇastutabhāvabhāvitāyām |
children.translated_text: Then <s>Hari</s> went to his father's assembly hall, which was sanctified by the praises of the host of divine beings,

children.text: paśupatiparipūjyapāśupatyavrajajanabhāskārabhāsitāmbarāyām ||128||
children.translated_text: which was adorned by the veneration of <s>Paśupati</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) and the bright-robed <s>Vraja</s> folk illuminated like the sun. ||128||

children.text: dvijakalakalapoṣavedaghoṣaprakarajamaṅgalasaṅgatiṃ vrajantyām |
children.translated_text: Which was filled with auspicious gatherings born from the multitude of Vedic chants and the warbling of birds,

children.text: diśi diśi kavisūtamāgadhādiprakararavastavavistaraṃ bhajantyām ||
children.translated_text: which hosted the elaborate panegyrics of bards, poets, and <s>māgadha</s> (eulogists) on all sides,

children.text: bharatavivṛtagītavādyanṛtyapracayabhidādividāṃ mudāṃ3 dharaṇyām |
children.translated_text: which bore the joys of witnessing the abundance of songs, music, and dance, unfolded in the <s>Bharata</s> style,

children.text: nijapitṛkulamātṛvaṃśatattadvivahanapuṇyayujāṃ pramodakhanyām ||130||
children.translated_text: and which was a mine of delight for those endowed with the merit of marriages on both the paternal and maternal sides of his family. ||130||

children.text: bala4sakhisahitaḥ sa sarvacakṣustatiṣu vavarṣa sudhām ivāṅgakāntim |
children.translated_text: He, accompanied by <s>Bala</s> (Balarāma) and friends, showered upon the gazes of all the radiance of his limbs like nectar;

children.text: jayajayajayakāravārasāraḥ samajani yena tadānaśe jagac ca ||131||
children.translated_text: whereby a flood of cries of 'Victory! Victory! Victory!' arose, and the world was filled. ||131||

children.text: caturbhiḥ
children.translated_text: With four (verses)

children.text: 1. (b) suo; 2. this verse missing from (b); 3. (b) mudā; 4. (a) margin: svakao
children.translated_text: 1. (b) suo; 2. this verse missing from (b); 3. (b) mudā; 4. (a) margin: svakao [variant readings]

children.text: api varaguravas tam āśu dṛṣṭvā nijanijapīṭhavarā upetavantaḥ |
children.translated_text: Even the venerable elders, upon seeing him swiftly, rose from their own excellent seats;

children.text: jalanidhim iva rāgitānadī tān prasabham amuṃ vahatīti tac ca yuktam ||132||
children.translated_text: just as rivers charged with passion flow forcefully into the ocean — and that was fitting. ||132||

children.text:
kramamanu sa gurūn varān anaṃsīd yugapad atha praṇanāma kāṃścid anyān
samagamad aparān natān bhujābhyāṃ karakamalena tathā dṛśā parāṃs tu ||
children.translated_text: In order, he honored the venerable elders, simultaneously bowed to some others, embraced yet others who were bowing with his arms, and acknowledged the rest with a lotus-hand and a glance.

children.text: vrajam anu paramā varādibhedā davaratayā yad api sphuranti lokāḥ |
children.translated_text: Even though in <s>Vraja</s>, distinctions of rank and the like shine forth among people with lightning speed,

children.text: tadapi vidhir ajalpad atra mitraṃ padam iti hārdam amuṣya vakti suṣṭhu1 ||
children.translated_text: nevertheless the Creator here has declared 'friendship' as the principle — and this declares the heartfelt [nature] of his [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s conduct] excellently.

children.text: harir asitamaṇipravekamūrtir lasati balaḥ pṛthupūrtihīramūrtiḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Hari</s>, shining as the foremost dark gem in form, and <s>Bala</s> (Balarāma), a great white diamond in form —

children.text: nijanidhir iti puṇyajātalabdhaḥ svayam iti sakramam ākali vrajena ||135
children.translated_text: were perceived in succession by [the people of] <s>Vraja</s> as their own treasure, obtained through accumulated merit, and as self-manifest. ||135||

children.text: vrajanṛpatir atha svabāṣpanīrasthagitagalaḥ kṣamate sma nāpi vaktum |
children.translated_text: Then the king of <s>Vraja</s> (<s>Nanda</s>), his throat choked by his own tears, was unable even to speak;

children.text: tadapi harir avetya tasya hṛdyaṃ smitanayanāmbuvṛtām uvāca vācam ||136
children.translated_text: yet <s>Hari</s>, understanding his heart, spoke words [accompanied] by a rain of smiles and tears from his eyes. ||136||

children.text: "ayi pitṛcaraṇā na cāsti kiñcid vrajavipine bhayadaṃ purāvad atra |
children.translated_text: "O father, there is nothing fearsome here in the forest of <s>Vraja</s>, as there was before;

children.text: svayam api dhavalā vanād upeyus tadapi vayaṃ khalu khelituṃ vrajāmaḥ ||"
children.translated_text: even the white [cows] have come from the forest of their own accord — yet we certainly go to play!"

children.text: tam avadad upanandamukhyavṛndaṃ
children.translated_text: The group headed by <s>Upananda</s> said to him:

children.text: "vrajasadasām asavaḥ pitā tavāyam |
children.translated_text: "Of the assembly of <s>Vraja</s>, your father here is the very life-breath;

children.text: tvam asi tad asavas tad atra vācyaṃ
children.translated_text: you are that life-breath. Therefore what is to be said here?

children.text: kim iva bhaven nikhilaṃ tvam eva vetsi ||138
children.translated_text: What could there be? You know everything." ||138||

children.text: vrajapatir atha yācakān samīkṣya svasutasukhāya punar dade bahūni |
children.translated_text: Then the lord of <s>Vraja</s>, seeing the supplicants, gave many [gifts] again for the happiness of his son;

children.text: vrajapatisutam aṇv amī yad āśīstatim adadur na sa tatra sāmyam āpa ||139
children.translated_text: when those [supplicants] offered blessings, however slight, for the lord of <s>Vraja</s>'s son — he did not find [anything] equal to that. ||139||

children.text: atha vanagataye 'ñjaliṃ dadhāne murajiti tadgatitarṣam ūhamānāḥ |
children.translated_text: Then, when the slayer of <s>Mura</s> bowed with joined palms for departing to the forest, perceiving his eagerness to go,

children.text: śrutibhaṇitaśubhān dvijān anuprāggati tam amī dhavalāntikāya ninyuḥ ||140
children.translated_text: those [people], having made the auspicious twice-born (<s>brāhmaṇas</s>) who recited Vedic blessings precede him, escorted him to the edge of the white [cows' grazing ground]. ||140||

children.text: svayam asavidhataḥ samīkṣya dhenūr2
children.translated_text: The [people] themselves, seeing the cows without [proper] arrangement,

children.text: na yayur amī prayayus tu kṛṣṇamukhyāḥ |
children.translated_text: did not go [further], but those led by <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> proceeded.

children.text: rabhasavaśam amūr amūṃs tu vīkṣyā-
children.translated_text: The cows, seeing them depart in haste,

children.text: tmajasadṛśānu samaṃ samaṃ praṇeduḥ ||141
children.translated_text: bellowed, following after each [boy] as if [he were] their own calf. ||141||

children.text: atha jihi jihi kārataḥ samastā vidadhur amī dhavalā vanāya nunnāḥ |
children.translated_text: Then all the white [cows], urged toward the forest, made [sounds of] 'jihi jihi';

children.text: harisurabhim amūs tu vindamānā harim anugamya muhur nivṛttim āpuḥ ||
children.translated_text: but catching <s>Hari</s>'s fragrance, those [cows] followed <s>Hari</s> and repeatedly turned back.

children.text: tadapi gurugaṇe sthite haris tu vigatamanaḥsthitisūcanāṃ cakāra |
children.translated_text: Even so, while the group of elders stood [watching], <s>Hari</s> gave signs that his composure of mind had departed;

children.text: harimatim avabudhya bāṣpakaṇṭhaḥ sa ca katham apy apasaryaṇaṃ babhāja |
children.translated_text: and he [<s>Nanda</s>], understanding <s>Hari</s>'s feelings, with a choked throat, somehow managed to depart.

children.text: vacanavadanamārjanānuśikṣādyanugatim ujjahad apy amuṣyatātaḥ |
children.translated_text: Though his father abandoned the following [of his son] in speech, face-wiping, instruction, and the like,

children.text: amum anunayanānuvṛtticaryāṃ na tu śithilām iva kartum īśitāsīt ||144
children.translated_text: he was unable to make slack the practice of following through loving conciliation. ||144||

children.text: katham api vinivṛtya sadma yāti vrajadharaṇīśitari vraje ca kṛtsne |
children.translated_text: When the lord of the earth of <s>Vraja</s> somehow turned back and went home, throughout all of <s>Vraja</s>,

children.text: harim anu vinivṛtya dṛṣṭir asmān na vighaṭituṃ ghaṭate sma tasya tasya ||
children.translated_text: the gaze of each and every one, having turned back following <s>Hari</s>, could not be detached from him.

children.text: murajid atha viśan vanāntarālaṃ gurukulasannatikṛd vidūrato 'pi |
children.translated_text: Then the slayer of <s>Mura</s>, entering the forest interior, bowing to the elder kinsmen even from afar,

children.text: gurubhir atitarāṃ tadāśīstatibhir apuṣyata tuṣyad akṣilakṣmi ||146
children.translated_text: was nourished by the elders' blessings exceedingly, delighting the beauty of his eyes. ||146||

children.text: atha harir aṭavīm aṭan suhṛdbhiḥ sahajavareṇa ca gāḥ sthirīvibhāvya |
children.translated_text: Then <s>Hari</s>, roaming the forest with his dear friends and the foremost among companions, having steadied the cows,

children.text: abhirucitapathaḥ prayāṇayuktā samavalayan mṛdugānarītihūti ||147
children.translated_text: set out on the path of his liking, encircling [the forest] with gentle singing, customs, and calls. ||147||

children.text: 1. (a) sa sma [?]; 2. (b) gāvaḥ;
children.translated_text: 1. (a) olatālio; 2. (b) gāvaḥ [variant readings]

children.text: atha vanam agamad balādisaṅgaṃ paramasukhapradam eṣa manyamānaḥ |
children.translated_text: Then he entered the forest, considering the company of <s>Bala</s> (Balarāma) and the others to bestow supreme bliss,

children.text: vividhatarulatāsu1 kokilādidvijamṛgasaṅgītam āviśat parantu ||148
children.translated_text: resounding with the songs of cuckoos and other birds and animals among the various trees and creepers. ||148||

children.text: madhupapikaśikhipradhānapakṣiplavagarurupriyakādijantubhedān |
children.translated_text: The different creatures — bees, parrots, peacocks, and the foremost among winged, aquatic, owl, and other beings —

children.text: dhvanitanaṭakalābhir anvakurvann ajitabalādi2mudām udārabālyāḥ2 ||149
children.translated_text: he imitated through sounds, dance, and skill — those of noble boyhood, <s>Ajita</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), <s>Bala</s> (Balarāma), and the others, in their delight. ||149||

children.text: iti bahuvidhakhelayā mukundaṃ sukhayati bāndhavavṛndam etam eva |
children.translated_text: Thus, with manifold play, <s>Mukunda</s> delights this very group of kinsmen;

children.text: nijanijavividhasvabhāvataś ca pramadayati pratidiṣṭam iṣṭamiṣṭam ||149
children.translated_text: and by the various distinctive natures of each one, he gives delight to each desired [person] in the desired [way]. ||149||

children.text: sthirataravarabuddhayaḥ sakhāyaḥ sacivacaritratayā hariṃ bhajanti |
children.translated_text: Those friends of steadfast and excellent intellect serve <s>Hari</s> with the conduct of ministers;

children.text: capalamatimiladvidūṣakārhaprahasana3kāvyagiraḥ prahāsayanti ||150
children.translated_text: others, deserving the role of jesters with restless wit, make him laugh with comedic and poetic words. ||150||

children.text: ṛjutamacaritaprayuktayuktasthitigatirītisamāḥ sabhājayanti |
children.translated_text: Those whose bearing, gait, and manner are suited to righteous and proper conduct honor him;

children.text: pratimuhur api vāmatāyamānasvacaracitajalpakalāvikalpayanti ||1514
children.translated_text: and those who repeatedly devise the arts of teasing speech with feigned contrariness, entertain him. ||151||

children.text: atulakulajaśīlamīladugraprakṛtikagīrmṛdulāḥ sadārdrayanti |
children.translated_text: Those of unmatched noble birth and character, endowed with gentle speech and fierce disposition, always soften [his heart];

children.text: girigiri ca vitaṇḍayāticaṇḍaprabharacanaprabhavo vicitrayanti ||152
children.translated_text: and those who excel in composing arguments with thunderous 'giri giri' and extreme vehemence, amuse him with variety. ||152||

children.text: iti nikhilagaṇā vicitratattadguṇaguṇitapraṇayaprakarṣacittāḥ |
children.translated_text: Thus all the groups, their hearts enriched by the excellence of love multiplied by each one's distinctive qualities,

children.text: bahuvidhavidhayaḥ pare pare te sukhadam amuṃ satataṃ sukhāyayanti ||153
children.translated_text: in manifold ways, those supreme ones constantly bring happiness to this one who is the giver of happiness. ||153||

children.text: kvacid api divase samitya govardhanam iha mānasasañjñitāṃ ca gaṅgām |
children.translated_text: On some days, having gathered at <s>Govardhana</s> and at the <s>Gaṅgā</s> called <s>Mānasa</s>,

children.text: raviduhitaram atra cāhni līlāḥ sthalagalagā vidadhe tvadīyakāntaḥ ||154
children.translated_text: and at the daughter of the sun (<s>Yamunā</s>) — your beloved performs pastimes on land and in water during the day. ||154||

children.text: kvacana ca sakhībhiḥ sameti bhāṇḍīrakam adhiyojanam asti yaḥ prasajya |
children.translated_text: Sometimes, with his friends, he goes to <s>Bhāṇḍīraka</s>, which extends for a <s>yojana</s> and beyond,

children.text: sthalavanayamunādi kelim asmin vividhavidhaṃ vidadhāti kṛṣṇacandraḥ ||155
children.translated_text: and <s>Kṛṣṇacandra</s> performs pastimes of various kinds on land, in the forest, and at the <s>Yamunā</s>. ||155||

children.text: ayi tava dayitaḥ kalena veṇoś calayati devagaṇāṃs tathā pataṅgān |
children.translated_text: O friend, your beloved, with the art of the flute, moves the hosts of gods and even the sun;

children.text: idam api ghaṭatāṃ parantu citraṃ sa hi dhunute nirasūn acetanāṃś ca |156
children.translated_text: yet this is even more wondrous — for he stirs even the lifeless and the unconscious! ||156||

children.text: hvayati ca dhavalājanāya yarhi tvadadhipatir madhureṇa śabditena |
children.translated_text: When your lord calls the white cows with his sweet sound,

children.text: jalam api karakāyamāṇam āsāṃ mṛdu mṛdu carvaṇayā5 rasaṃ bibharti ||157
children.translated_text: even the water that is being chewed in their mouths gently, gently bears [its] flavor. ||157||

children.text: nirudakagirisānugāḥ kadācid bahudhavalāḥ śavalās tṛṣā nirīkṣya |
children.translated_text: Sometimes, seeing the many white and dappled [cows] following the waterless mountains, thirsty,

children.text: dhvanayati muralīṃ patis tavāsmāddharaṇidharadravatā hi tāḥ piparti6 ||158
children.translated_text: your lord plays the <s>muralī</s> (flute), and the mountains flow with water, sustaining those [cows]. ||158||

children.text: kalayati yamunādisañjñayā tāḥ śuṣirakalāśritayā sa eṣa dhenūḥ |
children.translated_text: He draws those cows by the names '<s>Yamunā</s>' and the like through the art of the wind instrument;

children.text: iha nijanijanāmabuddhinadyaḥ kim ayur amuṃ kim u vā kalāntakṛṣṭi ||159
children.translated_text: here, those rivers of understanding bearing the names of each [cow] — is it their lifespan or the attraction of his art? ||159||

children.text: kvacana ca divase nidāghamādhyāhnikasamaye vigatā vṛṣṭi7pradeśe |
children.translated_text: On some days, at the hot midday time of summer, in a place without rain,

children.text: dadhad atha muralīkalaṃ payodāṃś cyutasalilān vidadhāti goṣu goṣu ||160
children.translated_text: then, producing the art of the flute, he makes the clouds release water upon the cows, upon the cows. ||160||

children.text: kvacana ca divase samārdracittaḥ kalayati veṇukalaṃ tathā yathānu |
children.translated_text: On some days, with moistened heart, he plays the art of the flute such that

children.text: dravati girigaṇe padāṅkamudrā jahati śilā na kadāpi tatra teṣām ||161
children.translated_text: the mountains melt with footprint-impressions, yet the rocks never [truly] leave their place. ||161||

children.text: racayati muralīṃ kadāpi nāvaṃ sariti paśūn paśupāṃś ca tārayan saḥ |
children.translated_text: Sometimes he makes the flute into a boat, ferrying the cattle and cowherds across the river;

children.text: madhurakalatayā yadā tu tasyā ghaṭayati tāṃ kaṭhināṃ kutūhalena ||162
children.translated_text: when he combines the sweetness of its art, he makes even that hard [river] [yield] with wonder. ||162||

children.text: kvacid api kavayaḥ śilādravādyaṃ bata kavayanti kavipracāravṛttyā |
children.translated_text: Sometimes even the poets poeticize the melting of stones and the like, in the manner of poetic convention;

children.text: 1. (a) olatālio; 2. (a) margin: mude mudā vayasyāḥ; 3. (b) prahasanaṃ; 4. this verse absent from (b); 5. (a) ca varṇayā; 6. (a) piparttiḥ; 7. (b) vigatāvṛtio
children.translated_text: 1. (a) olatālio; 2. (a) margin: mude mudā vayasyāḥ; 3. (b) prahasanaṃ; 4. this verse absent from (b); 5. (a) ca varṇayā; 6. (a) piparttiḥ; 7. (b) vigatāvṛtio [variant readings]

children.text: dadhati sarasatāṃ ca tatra vijñā harim anu tat tu nijaṃ kim atra varṇyam ||163||
children.translated_text: but those wise ones also invest these [events] with truth following <s>Hari</s> — what need is there to describe their own [poetic skill]? ||163||

children.text: sakhivṛṣamahiṣān mudā yudhā tān valayati saṃvalate ca tatra tatra |
children.translated_text: He joyfully wrestles with his friends' bulls and buffaloes, and is encircled [by them] here and there;

children.text: kva ca vijayaparājayāv abhīkṣya prahasitam añcati yuṣmadīyakāntaḥ ||164||
children.translated_text: somewhere, observing victory and defeat, your beloved flashes a smile. ||164||

children.text: kvacana ca racanāñcivastrayugmaṃ kvaca satirīṭam1 akuñcakāntarīyam |
children.translated_text: Sometimes he desires a pair of colorfully patterned garments, sometimes a fine-bordered upper cloth with a simple lower garment,

children.text: kvaca naṭarucibhṛtpaṭaṃ kvacāpi pravalitamallatulaṃ sa vaṣṭi veṣam ||165||
children.translated_text: sometimes a cloth bearing the beauty of a dancer, and sometimes the attire of a swaying wrestler. ||165||

children.text: kvacid api vidadhāti mallalīlāṃ kvacid api nṛtyakalāṃ suhṛdbhir eṣaḥ |
children.translated_text: Sometimes he performs the sport of wrestling, sometimes the art of dance with his friends;

children.text: dvayam api bhidayā mṛśāmi nedaṃ gatir aticitratamā samā dvaye 'pi ||166||
children.translated_text: I perceive both with distinction — this is the most wonderfully varied, yet equal in both. ||166||

children.text: hariṇaviharaṇaṃ satuṇḍayuddhaṃ nayananimīlanśālinarmagāliḥ |
children.translated_text: Play with deer, fights between beaks, games involving the closing of eyes and wit —

children.text: iti bahuvidhakhelanāptavelaṃ svam aśanam apy aniśaṃ visasmarus te ||167||
children.translated_text: thus, having reached the time for manifold play, they constantly forgot even their own food. ||167||

children.text: atha bahuvihṛtiṃ vicitracaryāṃ sa racitavān sakhibhiḥ sukhaṃ niṣaṇṇaḥ |
children.translated_text: Then, having performed many sports and varied activities, seated happily with his friends,

children.text: śayanam anugataś ca vījanādyaiḥ paricaritaḥ sukham eti tad dadāti ||168||
children.translated_text: resting and being served with fanning and the like, he attains happiness and bestows it. ||168||

children.text: iti haricarite tu tena tena śravasi cite muralīninādaramye |
children.translated_text: Thus, when those various pastimes of <s>Hari</s>, beautiful with the sound of the <s>muralī</s> (flute), were recounted to their ears,

children.text: sapadi tadavadhānam ādadhānā muhur abhajanta daśām amūm amūś ca ||169||
children.translated_text: immediately fixing their attention upon that, they repeatedly assumed this state and those [states]. ||169||

children.text: adhi harimuralisvapūrvarāgasphuraṇadaśāvaśāpurāvadīhaḥ2 |
children.translated_text: Regarding the conditions of the flute's manifestation of their former love (<s>pūrvarāga</s>) for <s>Hari</s>, and the efforts of their former state,

children.text: vṛṣaravitanayāmukhāḥ suduḥkhās tadamilanān mumuhur muhurmuhuś ca ||170||
children.translated_text: those beginning with <s>Vṛṣabha</s>, the daughter of the sun (<s>Yamunā</s>), and others, deeply distressed, were bewildered again and again. ||170||

children.text: iti sati sacivāyamānarāmā jagadur "aho katham atra vihvalāḥ stha? |
children.translated_text: When such was the case, <s>Rāmā</s> (<s>Rādhā</s>), being served by her attendants, said: "Alas! How are you distraught here?

children.text: vrajanṛpagṛhiṇīnideśavaryaṃ katham atha vismṛtam ārtibhiḥ kurudhve ||171
children.translated_text: How have you, in your afflictions, forgotten the foremost command of the queen of the lord of <s>Vraja</s>?" ||171||

children.text: adiśata sadayā hareḥ prasūr yad dvividaripor api sā vidhāya yuktim |
children.translated_text: The compassionate mother of <s>Hari</s> had given instructions, and she too, [even regarding] the enemy of the <s>Dvivida</s> [demon], made proper arrangements.

children.text: tad anusarata kāntarāgaśāntasmṛtitatayas tad upāyam ātanudhvam ||172
children.translated_text: Therefore follow the memory of the beloved's love-stilled [heart]; prepare the means for that. ||172||

children.text: prathamam aśanam īśituḥ prabhāte sphuṭam aparaṃ pratibhāti sārdhayāme |
children.translated_text: The first meal of the Lord is clearly at dawn; the second appears at the half-watch [mid-morning];

children.text: avaram api turīyayāmālambhe param atha rātrimukhe vyatītamātre ||173
children.translated_text: the lesser one at the commencement of the fourth watch; and the last one just after the onset of night. ||173||

children.text: prathamam aśanam arpyate jananyā tadaparam āvriyate suhṛdgaṇena |
children.translated_text: The first meal is offered by the mother; then the second is arranged by the group of friends;

children.text: pitṛmukhagurubhir vriyeta turyaṃ bhavadupayuktam atas tṛtīyam eva ||174
children.translated_text: the fourth is chosen by the father, the <s>guru</s>, and elders; therefore the third alone is appropriate for you [<s>gopīs</s>]. ||174||

children.text: vrajataṭam aṭataḥ murāriśatror abhigamanaṃ bhavatībhir atra yuktam |
children.translated_text: When the enemy of <s>Mura</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) wanders along the banks of <s>Vraja</s>, the approach by you [women] is fitting here;

children.text: sa hi miṣam upadhāya yuṣmadīyaṃ parisaram eṣyati dhāsyate ca śarma ||175
children.translated_text: for he, making your vicinity a pretext, will come and will bestow delight. ||175||

children.text: tvaritam iha tu kāntabhojyavaryaṃ kuruta kim apy adhunā tu tāḥ prayānti
vrajanarapatinā samaśnatā yā vyadhiśata dāpayituṃ sutāya bhojyam" ||176
children.translated_text: the ones whom the king of <s>Vraja</s> (<s>Nanda</s>), as he was eating, ordered to send food to [his] son. ||176||

children.text: iti harivanitāsu susthitāsu vrajapatigīrvaśataḥ purandhrimukhyāḥ |
children.translated_text: Thus, when the women of <s>Hari</s> were well-established, the chief matrons, obedient to the words of the lord of <s>Vraja</s>,

children.text: bahuvidham aśanaṃ vidhāya śīrṣṇi pramadabharaṃ manasi vrajāntam īyuḥ ||
children.translated_text: having prepared food of many kinds, with great delight in their hearts, went with it on their heads to the outskirts of <s>Vraja</s>. ||177||
Quickly prepare the finest food worthy of the beloved! For now those [<s>gopīs</s>] are departing —

children.text: atha nijanijakulyabālasaṅghā kutukaparītatayā dravann amūbhiḥ |
kvacid api purataḥ kvacic ca paścāt kvacid api dakṣiṇavāmataḥ prasajya |8
children.translated_text: clung to them — sometimes in front, sometimes behind, sometimes to the right and left. ||178||

children.text: vanalasadaśanapradhānakhelākutukakulaṃ bata citta tasya paśya |
children.translated_text: Behold, O mind, the flood of curiosity in his play-sport of eating in the forest's radiance!

children.text: tvam asi kila kiyan munīndravaryān api yad idaṃ nijavandinaḥ karoti ||179||
children.translated_text: How great you are, that even the greatest sages — even they he makes his own worshippers! ||179||
Then the groups of children from their respective families, running about with excited curiosity,

children.text: ka iha bata bhavanti te munīndrāḥ svayam api yacchravaṇe 'pi rādhikā sā |
children.translated_text: Who indeed are those great sages here? — when even she, <s>Rādhikā</s> herself,

children.text: 1.(b) sakirīṭam; 2. (b) oīhāḥ
children.translated_text: 1. (b) sakirīṭam; 2. (b) oīhāḥ [variant readings]

children.text: ajitam api guṇena mohayantī muhur api moham upaiti tatra kas tvam? |180||
children.translated_text: who enchants even the unconquered one with her qualities, is herself repeatedly bewildered — who then are you? ||180||

children.text: hariharisuhṛdaḥ sphuradvihārā dadṛśur amūr amukān amūś ca tatra |
tadapi tad ubhayaṃ kulaṃ na bhogaṃ prati viviveca vihāramagnabuddhi |181||
children.translated_text: yet even so, that whole group, their minds absorbed in play, did not distinguish with regard to enjoyment [between the two groups]. ||181||
The dear companions of <s>Hari</s>, their sports ablaze, saw these [<s>gopīs</s>] and those [cowherds] there;

children.text: katham api madhumaṅgalas tu paśyann atha viviveca javād uvāca tatra |
children.translated_text: <s>Madhumaṅgala</s>, somehow observing [this], then swiftly perceived [the situation] and spoke there:

children.text: "dhṛtavihṛtimadā na cet puras tātkṛtam api paśyatha kā kṣudhā varākī?" ||
children.translated_text: 'If you do not look at what has been prepared before [you] by those carrying the delights of sport, what is this miserable hunger?' ||182||

children.text: jagadur atha dhṛtasmitaṃ sakhāyaḥ "kvacid api cen na bhavet prayojanāya |
children.translated_text: Then the companions said with a smile: 'Even if it were of no use anywhere,

children.text: prakaṭataram ajāgalastanasya pratimadaśāṃ dvija eṣa saṃvaleta ||183
children.translated_text: this <s>brāhmaṇa</s> would assume the state of one intoxicated by a goat's udder!' ||183||

children.text: iti bahuhasitaṃ vidhāya tasmin sthalavalaye viniviśya kṛṣṇamukhyāḥ |
children.translated_text: Thus, having created much laughter, the group led by <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, settling in that clearing,

children.text: caraṇakaramukhaṃ viśadya vārbhiḥ samaśanaśarmakṛte dhṛteham āsan ||184||
children.translated_text: washed their feet, hands, and faces with water, and were ready for the happiness of eating together. ||184||

children.text: bahurucirucirāṃśukaṃ dukūlādikam adhikṛtya śubhaḥ śubhaṃyuveśaḥ |
children.translated_text: With splendid garments of many fine colors, silk cloth and the like, in auspicious youthful attire,

children.text: sahasakhinikaraḥ sa eṣa kṛṣṇaḥ sarabhasabhojanatṛṣṇatāṃ babhāja ||185||
children.translated_text: this <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, together with the multitude of his companions, shared in the eagerness for spirited feasting. ||185||

children.text: vidhum anu kamalaṃ baliṃ pradatte hasati cakorayugaṃ tad eva vīkṣya |
children.translated_text: As the lotus offers tribute following the moon, and the pair of <s>cakora</s> birds laugh seeing that very [moon] —

children.text: iti harim avalokya tatra tasthur vrajamahilā bata citratāṃ bhajantyaḥ ||186||
children.translated_text: thus, seeing <s>Hari</s> there, the women of <s>Vraja</s> stood, adopting a state of wonder! ||186||

children.text: pṛthakad upaviśan1 vilokayantyaḥ sa ca madhumaṅgalakaḥ sanarmajalpaḥ |
children.translated_text: Sitting separately [yet] watching [him] — and that <s>Madhumaṅgala</s>, with humorous talk,

children.text: pṛthag iva pariveṣayan prahāsaṃ rasam itavān surasān ṣaḍ apy amuṣṇāt ||
children.translated_text: serving separately as it were, distributing laughter, relished the six flavors and stole [everyone's hearts]. ||187||

children.text: samam aśanasamarpiṇībhir āptān vrajapṛthukān savidhe vidhāya sāsraḥ |
children.translated_text: Together with those who offered food, having placed the little ones of <s>Vraja</s> nearby, tearfully,

children.text: murajid adanabhājanād amībhyaḥ pratikavalaṃ kavalaṃ dadan nananda ||188||
children.translated_text: the slayer of <s>Mura</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), from his eating vessel, giving morsel for morsel to them, rejoiced. ||188||

children.text: surabhighṛtapariṣkṛtān samastān2 ṣaḍapi rasān praticarvaṇaṃ ruciprān |
children.translated_text: All six flavors, perfected with fragrant ghee, appetizing with each chewing,

children.text: pratilavarucibhoktṛṣu pradāya pratilavam āpa ruciṃ purandhrivargaḥ ||189||
children.translated_text: having offered them to those who savored each morsel, the group of matrons obtained delight with each serving. ||189||

children.text: iha bahuvidhasandhitāni nimbūprabhṛtiphalāni rucārpitāni rejuḥ |
children.translated_text: Here, various preserves of lime and other fruits, offered with flavor, shone forth,

children.text: nikaṭavinihitāni yāni cāsan pratimuhur eva ca sarvarocanāni ||190||
children.translated_text: placed nearby, which were appetizing again and again, stimulating all tastes. ||190||

children.text: abhinavaparipakvanārikeladravavalitaṃ maricādicārugandham |
children.translated_text: Freshly ripened coconut milk stirred in, with the lovely fragrance of pepper and the like,

children.text: lavalavaṇarasapriyaṃ kaduṣṇaṃ samucitapātrabhṛtaṃ ca mudgayūṣam ||191||
children.translated_text: delicious with a touch of salt, slightly warm, held in proper vessels — <s>mudga</s> (mung bean) broth. ||191||

children.text: surabhisurabhijātajātasarpiḥplutam atha pītanapītamiṣṭagandham |
children.translated_text: Fragrant, bathed in fresh butter of the finest kind, of undrunk and drunk pleasant fragrance,

children.text: api parimalaśālidivyaśāliprabhavasukomalaśubhraśocir annam ||192||
children.translated_text: and rice of aromatic, divine <s>śāli</s> (paddy), of supremely soft, bright, and radiant origin. ||192||

children.text: śṛtaghṛtamuhuruddhṛtapramṛṣṭa-dvidalavaṭīvividhaprakāravāram |
children.translated_text: Cooked in ghee, repeatedly refined and clarified — varieties of split-pulse <s>vaṭī</s> (fritters) in many styles,

children.text: harir abhijalasiktaniktatikta-svarasaviviktavicitrapākabhedam ||193||
children.translated_text: <s>Hari</s> [enjoyed these], sprinkled with water and purified of bitter taste, of distinctive and wondrous cooking-varieties. ||193||

children.text: navacaṇakakalāyamāṣamudga-pravarajayuktakaṭuprasaktasūpam |
children.translated_text: Soup made pungent with excellent fresh chickpeas, <s>kalāya</s> (peas), <s>māṣa</s> (black gram), and <s>mudga</s> (mung beans),

children.text: phaladalakusumatvagaṣṭikanda-prasavakṛtaprathayuktipaṅktibhedam ||194||
children.translated_text: with varieties of preparations made from fruits, leaves, flowers, bark, seeds, roots, and sprouts. ||194||

children.text: śṛtaghṛtadhṛtajīrakāñcidhātrī-phalarasapākakaṣāyaramyacukram3 |
children.translated_text: Delightful <s>cukra</s> (tamarind sauce) cooked with ghee, infused with cumin, <s>āñci</s> (mortar spice), and the juice of <s>dhātrī</s> (gooseberry) fruit, of pleasant astringency,

children.text: bahuvidharacanācaṇāmlasaṅghaṃ ghanadadhimaṇḍakaroṭikājyapakvam ||195||
children.translated_text: with varied preparations of sour condiments, cooked in thick yogurt, <s>maṇḍaka</s> (whey), <s>karoṭikā</s>, and ghee. ||195||

children.text: śrapitapayasi bāṣpapaṅkapiṣṭapravalitaśarkaramugdhadugdhasāram |
children.translated_text: In heated milk, steamed flour-paste rolled with sugar, rich with fresh cream —

children.text: amṛtajayirasaprasāraśālā-nibhavibhavaprasarāgraṇīrasānām ||196||
children.translated_text: the foremost of flavors, having the splendor of a hall spreading the taste that conquers nectar. ||196||

children.text: saparimalaṃ jalaṃ tathāmbadhātrī4 praṇayajakopavilāsavalguvācam |
children.translated_text: Fragrant water and also <s>ambā</s>-<s>dhātrī</s> [gooseberry drink], with charming words born of love's playful pique,

children.text: 1. (b) pṛthak samupaviśan; 2. (b) samāptān; 3. (a) ocukruḥ; 4. (b) osvadhātrīḥkulavarapariveṣikātatīnāṃ sakhivalayena vivādaśarmajātam ||197||
children.translated_text: 1. (b) pṛthak samupaviśan; 2. (b) samāptān; 3. (a) ocukruḥ; 4. (b) osvadhātrīḥ — joy born of the loving disputes between the serving women of the finest families and the circle of friends. ||197||

children.text: anubhavad iha rāmakṛṣṇayugmaṃ muhur api bhojanatṛṣṇatām avāpa |
children.translated_text: The pair <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> experienced [all this] here, and again and again the eagerness for eating arose;

children.text: tadapi ca nijasevakeṣu phalāvitaraṇakāmatayā tato vyaraṃsīt ||198||
children.translated_text: yet even so, desiring to distribute fruits among their own servants, they took delight in that. ||198||

children.text: aṣṭabhiḥ
children.translated_text: With eight (verses)

children.text: arasayad iha temanāni ṣaṣṭiṃ sahasakhisaṅghatayā svayaṃ murāriḥ |
children.translated_text: Here, the enemy of <s>Mura</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) himself, together with the company of friends, relished sixty preparations,

children.text: muhur atisarasāni yāni tatra spṛhijanabhāvabhidāṃ vidhunvate sma ||199||
children.translated_text: which were exceedingly flavorful and which would dispel the state of distinction-consciousness in those who desired [them]. ||199||

children.text: saparimalajalena vaktraśuddhiṃ vidadhur amī bata tādṛśena yat tu |
children.translated_text: They performed the cleansing of the mouth with fragrant water; and indeed with such [water]

children.text: aśanajasukhapūri suṣṭhu cakre hṛdayagataṃ kim api prasādaśātam ||200||
children.translated_text: he fully accomplished a certain tranquil satisfaction pervading the heart, born of the happiness of eating. ||200||

children.text: himajalahimabālukāsitābhir viracitapānakapāyakāḥ sakhāyaḥ |
children.translated_text: The companions, having made drinks and beverages from cold water, fine white sand-cooled [waters],

children.text: himakaravaragandhavīṭikābhiḥ kṛtamukhavāsatayā sukhaṃ virejuḥ ||201||
children.translated_text: and with betel-leaves of the fragrance of the finest moonbeam, having perfumed their mouths, shone forth happily. ||201||

children.text: iti harim upalabhya tṛptim etā
children.translated_text: Thus, having found <s>Hari</s> satisfied, these [<s>gopīs</s>]

children.text: harijananīm upalambhayāmbabhhūvuḥ |
children.translated_text: made the mother of <s>Hari</s> (<s>Yaśodā</s>) realize [his satisfaction].

children.text: tadaśanam amṛtaṃ vibhāti tasmin
children.translated_text: That food shines as nectar in his [presence] —

children.text: katham atha tatkathanaṃ tathā na tasyām ||202||
children.translated_text: how then should its telling not be so in hers? ||202||

children.text: tadanu tadanugā tu kāpi kāpi vrajakamalāḥ sajatī tadekaśarmā |
children.translated_text: Thereafter, certain lotus-women of <s>Vraja</s>, following after him, each finding their sole delight in him,

children.text: haricaritakathāsu lambhitāśā harim api lambhayituṃ drutaṃ vavāñcha2 ||203||
children.translated_text: having been given hope in the narrations of <s>Hari's</s> deeds, quickly desired to reach <s>Hari</s> himself. ||203||

children.text: atha paśupakulakṣitīśapatnyāḥ svam aśanakālam adhītya tatra yātāḥ |
children.translated_text: Then the wives of the chief of the cowherds, having learned their own mealtime there, departed;

children.text: tadaśanam anu tāṃ niṣevya tadgīrvaśam aśanaṃ rahasā carantv amūś ca ||204||
children.translated_text: and after that meal, having served her [<s>Yaśodā</s>], let those [other <s>gopīs</s>] secretly proceed, obedient to her words, to eat. ||204||

children.text: atha muhur upalabdhagoparājñīvacanabalāḥ svayam icchamānasāś ca |
children.translated_text: Then, repeatedly emboldened by the words of the queen of the cowherds, and themselves desiring

children.text: nijanijakarasādhitaṃ vitartuṃ nijaramaṇāya ramā babhūvur utkāḥ ||205||
children.translated_text: to offer what was prepared by their own hands to their own beloved — those beauties became eager. ||205||

children.text: dayitam abhisarantu taṃ tu dhanyāḥ śataśatayūtham itāḥ sa eva cāsu |
children.translated_text: Let those blessed ones go forth to meet their beloved, proceeding in hundreds and hundreds of groups! And may he

children.text: viracayatu gatiṃ kayāpi śaktyā smara mama citta mudā sadāpi rādhām ||206||
children.translated_text: fashion the path by some power — O mind, remember <s>Rādhā</s> always with joy! ||206||

children.text: śṛṇu hṛdaya diśāmi rādhikāyāṃ harim abhisāraya tatra tāṃ kadāpi |
children.translated_text: Listen, O heart! I show you [the way] toward <s>Rādhikā</s>; lead <s>Hari</s> to meet her at some time.

children.text: dvayam idam anu pūjanaṃ tad eva dvayam anu yat purutoṣapoṣakāri ||207||
children.translated_text: The worship of that pair is itself [the goal]; following that pair is what produces the nourishment and satisfaction of the Supreme. ||207||

children.text: atha saha dhavalābhir āvrajantaṃ vrajataṭam ahni turīyayāmabhāge |
children.translated_text: Then, as he was coming to the banks of <s>Vraja</s> in the afternoon, at the fourth watch of the day, with the white [cows],

children.text: puruyugavirahād ivātikhinnā vyatikṛtasatvaratāvidhāyijalpāḥ ||208||
children.translated_text: as if distressed by separation lasting many ages, [the <s>gopīs</s>] uttered words of haste surpassing [their composure]. ||208||

children.text: ghṛtaracitapacaṃ sumiṣṭam iṣṭaṃ tad anu ca ṣāḍavasaṅginīṃ rasālām |
children.translated_text: Cooked with ghee, very sweet and desirable, and then <s>rasālā</s> (sweet sauce) mixed with <s>ṣāḍava</s> (a confection) —

children.text: drutataragamanā vṛṣārkajātā vrajad abhigṛhya sakhībhir ātmakāntam ||209||
children.translated_text: the daughter of <s>Vṛṣabhānu</s> (<s>Rādhā</s>), going very swiftly, proceeded with her companions to meet her beloved, bringing [these offerings]. ||209||

children.text: yugmakam
children.translated_text: A couplet

children.text: nijavanagamanārhasūkṣmarandhraṃ drutam atigamya vanaṃ praviśya sarvāḥ |
children.translated_text: Having quickly passed through the subtle opening fit for entering their own forest, all of them, entering the forest,

children.text: praṇayi savidhadūratas tu tasthur jaḍahṛdayāḥ spṛhayā ca lajjayā ca ||210||
children.translated_text: stood lovingly at a distance, with stunned hearts, with both longing and shyness. ||210||

children.text: harir idam avagamya ramyacetāś chalam akaron nikhileṣu vacmi tac ca |
children.translated_text: <s>Hari</s>, perceiving this, his mind delighted, made a ruse — and I shall tell that too:

children.text: dinadinam anu kāpi devatā māṃ kalayitum eti rahas tataḥ prayāmi ||211||
children.translated_text: 'Day after day, some deity comes secretly to worship me; therefore I shall go [to investigate].' ||211||

children.text: tvaritam iha tu yūyam āvrajantaṃ kalayata mām iti dūratām upetya |
children.translated_text: 'But quickly come, you all, and find me as I arrive here!' — having gone to a distance [he said this];

children.text: atha kim ucitam ittham ūhamānas tricaturavālakasaṅgi tiṣṭhati sma ||212||
children.translated_text: and then, pondering what would be fitting, he stood [there] accompanied by three or four young boys. ||212||

children.text: 1. (b) adds kulakam; 2. (a) margin: gataṃ rasāñci;
children.translated_text: 1. (b) adds kulakam; 2. (a) margin: gataṃ rasāñci [variant readings]

children.text: atha kathitacarāḥ sakhīsadṛkṣā navanavavarṣavarā hariṃ parītya |
children.translated_text: Then, those girls of ever-fresh youth, resembling her companions, having been told [what to do], surrounded <s>Hari</s>,

children.text: svagatam uta tadīyam iṣṭam arthaṃ samaghaṭayan saha sā babhāṣire ca ||213
children.translated_text: and, fulfilling their welcome and his desired purpose, together with her [<s>Rādhā</s>], they spoke. ||213||

children.text: "vrajanṛpasuta tāḥ sadā bhajante navanavatāṃ tad amūḥ sadā kumāryaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'O son of the king of <s>Vraja</s>! Those [<s>gopīs</s>] who always worship you with ever-fresh [devotion] — they are ever-youthful maidens;

children.text: api dhṛtasubṛhadvratās tadāsāṃ tava muralī kṣipati vrataṃ muhuś ca ||"214||
children.translated_text: and though they have undertaken great vows, your flute repeatedly breaks their vows.' ||214||

children.text: harir idam avabudhya sudhyadhīśaḥ sahasitam āha "kathaṃ kva vātra doṣaḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Hari</s>, understanding this, the lord of pure intelligence, said with a smile: 'How and where is the fault here?

children.text: aham api sa kumāra eva tasmād abhigamanaṃ mayi yuktam eva tāsām ||215||
children.translated_text: I too am that very boy; therefore their approach to me is entirely fitting. ||215||

children.text: tadapi ca bata tā vratena khinnāḥ punar iyad āgamanaṃ na tāsu yuktam |
children.translated_text: Yet alas, they are wearied by their vow; such a visit again would not be fitting for them.

children.text: iti yad abhigataṃ tad eva tāsāṃ vayam anuyāma tathā sadāśrayāma ||"216||
children.translated_text: Therefore, what they have approached — that very [place] — we shall follow and always take shelter of.' ||216||

children.text: iti sa parihasann amūn amūṣāṃ hṛdi muralījanimohanaṃ tu jānan |
children.translated_text: Thus he, jesting with them, knowing in his heart the enchantment born of his flute,

children.text: sakaruṇadṛg amūṃ samīpam añcan pracurasakhīmilitāṃ dadarśa rādhām ||217||
children.translated_text: with compassionate glance, approaching near, beheld <s>Rādhā</s> surrounded by a multitude of companions. ||217||

children.text: harimilanavidūrabhāvanātaḥ kvacana ca dṛṣṭivisṛṣṭiyuktaṃ netrāḥ |
children.translated_text: From the contemplation of being far from meeting <s>Hari</s>, and with eyes fit for casting glances in some direction,

children.text: haritanum avalokcya tās tu sākṣāt kucitavapur laghu lilyire latāsu ||218||
children.translated_text: seeing [<s>Hari's</s>] dark body, those [<s>gopīs</s>], with bodies contracted, quickly hid behind the creepers. ||218||

children.text: atha harir anunīya tāḥ purastāt parivalayann upahāram ādadānaḥ |
children.translated_text: Then <s>Hari</s>, having conciliated them, encircling [them] before him, receiving their offerings,

children.text: svahṛdi sukhasukhaṃ prasajya tābhiḥ pratataparasparaśarmatāṃ dadhāra ||219||
children.translated_text: securing supreme happiness in his heart, together with them, maintained a state of mutual delight. ||219||

children.text: yadapi samayabhedataḥ samagrā dadhati tadāspadatāṃ bhuvaḥ kramasthāḥ |
children.translated_text: Even though all [sacred places] in their proper order assume that status [of holiness] according to different times,

children.text: tadapi digavalokanāya yogyaṃ niśamaya citta tad etad adya dhāma ||220||
children.translated_text: yet, O mind, hear of that abode which is worthy of beholding in all directions, even today. ||220||

children.text: purumaṇicayacāruśobhagovardhanaśivadiggatasāṇuni praśaste |
children.translated_text: At the glorious <s>Govardhana</s>, beautified with collections of fine jewels, on the auspicious ridge facing the blessed direction,

children.text: suratarujayibhūruhāliśāliprasavasamuccayamaṇḍikuṇḍayugmam ||221||
children.translated_text: a pair of pools adorned with groves of trees surpassing the wish-granting trees, full of abundant blossoms of <s>śāli</s> (rice). ||221||

children.text: anupamititadantarālavāle mṛdumṛdumārutabhāji kelidhāmni |
children.translated_text: In the incomparable intermediate area of the pool, a pleasure-garden kissed by gentle, gentle breezes,

children.text: parimalavanakṛṣṭadhṛṣṭahṛṣṭabhramararavakramajātajātasāmni ||222||
children.translated_text: where the humming of bold, delighted bees drawn by the fragrance of the forest creates successive harmonies. ||222||

children.text: murajidupaviśan smitārpitāśīr asitamaṇipraṇidhānahāribhāsī |
children.translated_text: The slayer of <s>Mura</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), sitting down, bestowing blessings with a smile, shining with the beauty of dark gem-like meditation,

children.text: kanakagaṇamanaḥprakāmamānapravasaśanakṛdvasanaśriyāṃ nivāsī ||223||
children.translated_text: dwelling in the splendor of garments that would captivate the minds of golden hosts at will. ||223||

children.text: nijavararamaṇīsuvarṇavarṇavratatitatismitapārijātajātim |
children.translated_text: Bringing to the path of experience the golden hue of the smiling <s>pārijāta</s> (coral tree) blooming upon the row of beautiful vows of his own supreme beloved,

children.text: anubhavapadavīṃ nayann ayaṃ pramadamadasthaganāya nāpa sātim ||224||
children.translated_text: intoxicated with joy, he did not reach satiety even for concealing [his delight]. ||224||

children.text: caturbhiḥ
children.translated_text: With four (verses)

children.text: kva ca yadi gaṇanātigāḥ sahāyāḥ sthalam apurupratham ekakaś ca kṛṣṇaḥ |
children.translated_text: Though the companions are beyond counting in some place, and the ground is not widely known, and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> is alone —

children.text: tadapi bhavati sāvakāśarītitrayam api citta vicitram atra paśya ||225||
children.translated_text: yet even so, O mind, behold the wondrous threefold occasion [for sport] that arises here! ||225||

children.text: yadapi subahavas tadīyakāntā nijanijagarvadharādharād abandhyāḥ |
children.translated_text: Even though his beloved ladies are very many, unfailing in their respective proud self-bearing —

children.text: tadapi kalaya citta sā tu rādhā nikhilapuraḥsaratāṃ gatā vibhāti ||226||
children.translated_text: yet know, O mind, that <s>Rādhā</s> shines forth as the foremost of all. ||226||

children.text: harim anu rasanīyam etayā yat paripariveṣitam atra tat tu bhāvyam |
children.translated_text: Whatever was served to <s>Hari</s> by her, the one worthy of relishing — that should be contemplated;

children.text: rasatatir iha paryaveṣi yānyā katham atha sā pariceyatāṃ prayātu ||227||
children.translated_text: the current of <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic rapture) that was investigated here by that other [<s>gopī</s>] — how then should she [<s>Rādhā</s>] become the object of familiarity? ||227||

children.text: nayanavalayayānvasūci kiñcin niṭilakacālanayā tathānyad atra |
children.translated_text: Something indicated by the movement of the eye-garland, and something else by the motion of the forehead's locks,

children.text: mṛdutaravacasā tathā paraṃ ca priyatamapṛṣṭatamaṃ tayā ramaṇyā ||228||
children.translated_text: and yet another thing by the softest words — the most intimate things asked by him of that charming one. ||228||

children.text: harir atha vividhaṃ vibhajya bhojyaṃ
children.translated_text: Then <s>Hari</s>, having distributed the various foods,

children.text: pṛthu-pṛthukān api tān mudopayojya |
children.translated_text: and having joyfully employed those abundant flattened rice portions —

children.text: mukham anu sarasaṃ jagāma yaṃ yaṃ1
children.translated_text: Whatever delicious [morsel] his mouth pursued,

children.text: nahi mukhataḥ prathanāya tasya śeke ||229||
children.translated_text: it could not succeed in spreading its taste from [merely reaching] the mouth. ||229||

children.text: aśanarasanayā jagām tṛptiṃ na tu dṛśi rocanayā murārir asyāḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Murāri</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) attained satisfaction through the taste-sense of eating, but not through the sight's delight of hers;

children.text: tadapi muraripur2 gāvāṃ vrajāya vrajanam anuvrajituṃ tato vyaraṃsīt ||230||
children.translated_text: yet even so, <s>Murāri</s> resolved to follow the cows to the pasture of <s>Vraja</s>. ||230||

children.text: atha mukha3karaśodhanāya tasmin surabhijalādikam arpitaṃ sakhībhiḥ |
children.translated_text: Then, for the cleansing of his mouth and hands, fragrant water and the like were offered by the <s>sakhīs</s> (friends);

children.text: yadanu surabhitā na cāsya mātraṃ surabhitam ācarad apy amuṣya cittam ||231||
children.translated_text: thereafter, the fragrance [of the water] did not merely perfume him — it also perfumed her heart. ||231||

children.text: aśanapadam idaṃ visṛjya kṛṣṇaḥ subhagam anu4 purataḥ sthalaṃ samitya |
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, leaving this place of eating, proceeded to a lovely spot before [the house];

children.text: sukhamanumukhavāsanaṃ priyābhiḥ saha rasayan mukhavāsanaṃ jagāma ||232||
children.translated_text: happily savoring mouth-freshener (<s>mukhavāsana</s>) with his beloveds, whose faces were turned toward him. ||232||

children.text: tadanu ca paritaḥ sakhīsakhībhir nijanijaśilpavilāsahāramālyam |
children.translated_text: Then, on all sides, the garlands, ornaments, and artistic displays fashioned by the friends of the <s>sakhīs</s>

children.text: upahṛtipadatām anāyi tac ca pratirucibhiś citam ullālasa tasya ||233||
children.translated_text: were brought as offerings; and those, arranged with competing beauties, delighted him. ||233||

children.text: asitamaṇisuvarṇavarṇam āgād abhimukhatāṃ mithunaṃ mithas tadagre |
children.translated_text: A couple of dark-sapphire-and-gold complexion came before him face to face;

children.text: pratiphalitatayā vilokya yat tu vyatiṣajyamānam iva smitaṃ sakhībhiḥ ||234||
children.translated_text: seeing them reflected [in each other], the <s>sakhīs</s> smiled, as if they were intertwined. ||234||

children.text: atha vidadhad amūṣu narmavācaṃ svayam anusandadhad apy amūm amūṣām |
children.translated_text: Then, while exchanging playful words with them, and himself also surveying this one and those —

children.text: amṛtasariti sekakelim ābhiḥ samam amata sphuṭam acyutaś cirāya ||235||
children.translated_text: <s>Acyuta</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) clearly delighted in the sport of sprinkling in the river of nectar with them for a long time. ||235||

children.text: atha harir avadad gavāvanāya tvarigahanāntar ahaṃ rahaḥ prayāmi |
children.translated_text: Then <s>Hari</s> said: 'I go alone into the deep forest interior to bring back the cows;

children.text: puru mama jananī nideśatuṣṭiprathanakṛte tvam api vrajaṃ prayāhi ||236||
children.translated_text: and you — for the sake of fulfilling my mother's command with great joy — go too to <s>Vraja</s>.' ||236||

children.text: atha varasudṛśāṃ śrutis tad etat pravaṇatayā niradhārayad yathārtham |
children.translated_text: Then the hearing of the beautiful-eyed ones grasped those very words as true, because of its inclination;

children.text: nijagṛhagamahākṣamā tu dṛṣṭiḥ śrutipatharodhanakṛd vighūrṇati sma ||237||
children.translated_text: but their sight, incapable of accepting the departure to their own homes, obstructing the path of hearing, began to whirl. ||237||

children.text: nayanayugalam aśnute sadāmbhaḥ kva nu nivased bata durlabhaḥ sa eṣaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'The pair of eyes is always flooded with water — alas, where will this rare one dwell?'

children.text: iti harivanitā hariṃ nirīkṣya dhruvam ajahur nayanāmbhasāṃ kulāni5 ||238||
children.translated_text: Thus the consorts of <s>Hari</s>, gazing at <s>Hari</s>, surely released streams of tears from their eyes. ||238||

children.text: murajid ucitacārucāturībhir muhur api netravinodanakriyābhiḥ |
children.translated_text: The slayer of <s>Mura</s>, with fitting, beautiful, and charming acts of delighting the eyes again and again,

children.text: svasadanavadanaṃ vidhātum āsāṃ nikaram aśakyata na svamagnam antaḥ ||239||
children.translated_text: was unable to make their host's faces resemble his own blissful countenance, [for they were] inwardly submerged [in sorrow]. ||239||

children.text: yadapi muraripuḥ priyāvad eva pravasanakātaratām avāpa tatra |
children.translated_text: Although <s>Muraripu</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) himself experienced the anguish of separation just as his beloveds did,

children.text: tadapi tam anu pauruṣaṃ babhūva sphuṭam abalāvalayāvalambanāya ||240||
children.translated_text: yet even so, manliness arose in him clearly, for the support of the circle of delicate women. ||240||

children.text: divijaphalajayīni tarhi vṛndāvanajaphalāni balīn priyāvalīśām |
children.translated_text: Then the fruits of the <s>Vṛndāvana</s> trees, conquering the fruits of the divine wish-fulfilling trees — he gathered abundant ones

children.text: sukhayitum ayam ālisādakarṣīt parimalasātkṛtavanti tāni tāś ca ||241||
children.translated_text: to delight the beloveds — those [fruits] made fragrant, and those [women] as well [were made fragrant]. ||241||

children.text: atha kiyad api dūravartma yātā vanavalayaṃ jalatīragaṃ nirīkṣya |
children.translated_text: Then, having gone some distance along the path, seeing the forest-belt bordered by water,

children.text: śramaviratikṛte murārirāmā niviviśire vṛṣabhānujāpradhānāḥ ||242||
children.translated_text: <s>Murāri</s> and the women, led by the daughter of <s>Vṛṣabhānu</s> (<s>Rādhā</s>), entered [the grove] for the sake of relieving their fatigue. ||242||

children.text: atha vṛṣaravidehajā sakhībhir vyatihasitaprathayā mudāñcitābhiḥ |
children.translated_text: Then the daughter of <s>Vṛṣabhānu</s>, with her <s>sakhīs</s> who displayed shared laughter and were adorned with joy,

children.text: muravijidaśanāviśeṣam ādat tadaśanaśarmakalām abhāvayac ca ||243||
children.translated_text: received the food specially prepared by the conqueror of <s>Mura</s>, and experienced the bliss of that food's sweetness. ||243||

children.text: samaguṇaparicārikābhir etāḥ surabhijalavyajanādidhāriṇībhiḥ |
children.translated_text: Attended eagerly on all sides by serving maids of equal qualities,

children.text: sarabhasam upasevitāḥ samantāj jitakamalādiguṇād virejuḥ ||244||
children.translated_text: bearing fragrant water, fans, and the like, they shone, surpassing the qualities of lotuses and the like. ||244||

children.text: atha sakhi-gaṇa-veṣam āśrayantyaḥ paṭu-gati-varṣa-varā murāri-pārśvam |
children.translated_text: Then, assuming the guise of the <s>sakhī</s> group, the beloveds of <s>Hari</s>, of excellent age and swift gait,

children.text: prati sapadi gatās tadā ca goṣṭhaṃ hari-dayitā nija-sadma-padmam āpa ||245||
children.translated_text: instantly went to <s>Murāri</s>'s side; and then to the cowshed — each beloved of <s>Hari</s> reached the lotus of her own home. ||245||

children.text: 1. (b) yat tan; 2. (b) madhuripur; 3. (a) margin: sukhao; 4. (a) ataḥ; 5. (b) kulāli;
children.translated_text: [Footnotes: textual variants.]

children.text: vrajapadam anugamya goparājñīm1 api tadanujñapitā svadhāma gatvā |
children.translated_text: Following the queen of the cowherds back to the abode of <s>Vraja</s>, having been given leave by her and having gone to her own home,

children.text: svadayitam upasevituṃ rajanyāṃ bahuvidhaśilpavikalpam ācacāra ||246||
children.translated_text: she practiced various arts and crafts in order to attend upon her beloved in the night. ||246||

children.text: iha mṛdu mṛdu kṛṣṇagānakartrī vṛṣaravijā lalitādibhiḥ sakhībhiḥ |
children.translated_text: Here, softly, softly, the daughter of <s>Vṛṣabhānu</s>, composing songs of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, with her <s>sakhīs</s> <s>Lalitā</s> and the others,

children.text: muhur api samasāntvikṛṣṇavṛttān mudam anu varṣavareṇa tena tena ||247||
children.translated_text: repeatedly consoled by the accounts of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, followed the joy [bestowed by] that best of the rainy seasons. ||247||

children.text: śṛṇu sakhi murajid yadā tu yuṣmad vyavahitim āpa tadā jagāma dhenuḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Listen, O friend! When the slayer of <s>Mura</s> became separated from you, then the cow departed;

children.text: madhumadhurakalān na dhenumātraṃ param aparaṃ ca cakarṣa jīvamātram ||248||
children.translated_text: the honey-sweet melodies [of his flute] attracted not merely the cows, but also every other living being.' ||248||

children.text: murajid atha samastajīvajātivyatikaravīkṣaṇataḥ kṣamām avindan |
children.translated_text: Then the slayer of <s>Mura</s>, finding the earth incapable [of holding still] from the sight of the mingling of all species of living beings,

children.text: akuruta muralīkalīviśeṣaṃ yad ajani sarvakam eva tatra bhinnam ||249||
children.translated_text: produced a particular melody of the flute that caused everything there to become distinct. ||249||

children.text: vayam akhilasakhiprasaktanānā haricaritākalanāya yarhi yātāḥ |
children.translated_text: When we, all the <s>sakhīs</s>, had gone to learn the various pastimes of <s>Hari</s>,

children.text: aparahariramābhir anyad ārād2 bahuvidhabhojyam adāyi tarhi guptam ||250||
children.translated_text: then secretly, by the other consorts of <s>Hari</s>, diverse foods were given from afar. ||250||

children.text: danujaripur aśeṣam eva sarvān prati vibabhāja ca bhājanāvalīṣu |
children.translated_text: The enemy of the demons distributed absolutely everything among all, into rows of vessels;

children.text: atigaṇitatayā nayād viviktaṃ samupahṛtaṃ tad idaṃ kayā kayeti ||251||
children.translated_text: because the offerings were uncountable, [they wondered] judiciously: 'This was brought by whom?' ||251||

children.text: harir atha jalapāyanāya dhenūr hvayati yadā sma tadā sravatpadāṅkāḥ3 |
children.translated_text: <s>Hari</s>, when he called the cows to drink water — then [the cows], with hoofprints streaming [with milk],

children.text: api nikhilam amūs tṛṣā vihīnaṃ vidadhur amūṣu tathā kathāstu4 dūre ||252||
children.translated_text: rendered everything around them free from thirst; and as for their own thirst — let that tale be [set aside as] far distant. ||252||

children.text: tadapi ca salilāni pāyayitvā nijakarasaṅkaratāsudhāyitāni |
children.translated_text: Even so, having made the cows drink waters

children.text: bahūni kaṭamukhīś cakāra dhenūr nijamukhatām api bibhratīḥ prayatya5 ||253||
children.translated_text: made nectarean by the touch of his own hands, he turned many cows [back],

children.text: na bhavati vinivartanādyupāyaḥ pratigatiyaṣṭivicālanādirūpaḥ |
children.translated_text: [cows] who bore even his own face [in reflection], with effort. ||253||

children.text: api tu harigavīṣu dṛṣṭiveṇū sapadi hareḥ sphurataḥ sma tatra tatra ||254||
children.translated_text: No means of turning back — such as waving a stick or the like — works

children.text: abhigṛham ajitasya yā nivṛtya pratigatir atra ca kautukaṃ vibhāti |
children.translated_text: for <s>Hari</s>'s cows; rather, the flute of [<s>Hari</s>'s] glance manifests here and there before them instantly. ||254||

children.text: upasurasurajātayaḥ samantān naṭanakalāghaṭanaprathām aṭanti ||255||
children.translated_text: And the unconquered one's return to each house — herein too wonder shines forth;

children.text: atha ca yadi tadā samastahṛdbhir bharatakalām anuvindate mukundaḥ |
children.translated_text: the celestial and semi-divine beings, from every direction, display the splendor of arranging the art of dance. ||255||

children.text: divi phalakarave tadā divīśā diśi diśi citranibhāni bhālayati ||"256||
children.translated_text: And if at that time <s>Mukunda</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) performs the art of <s>Bharata</s> (dramatic performance) with the hearts of all,

children.text: iti bhaṇati tadā tadīyavarge kalakalabhāg ajani prarmodigoṣṭham |
children.translated_text: then the lords of heaven in every direction gaze upon the wondrous painting-like [spectacles] in the sky beneath the fruit-bearing sun. ||256||

children.text: iha sati vṛṣabhānujādivargas tvarigati candraniveśam āruroha ||257||
children.translated_text: When [news of his return] was announced, then in his retinue arose a joyful commotion, filling the cowshed with delight;

children.text: uparigṛhagataḥ sa tatra tatra
children.translated_text: thereupon, the group led by the daughter of <s>Vṛṣabhānu</s> (<s>Rādhā</s>) swiftly ascended to the moon-terrace. ||257||

children.text: dravad iva gopakuladravād dadarśa |
children.translated_text: He, having gone above each house,

children.text: dṛśam atha bhṛśam agrataḥ prayacchan
children.translated_text: saw the cowherd families as if melting [with love];

children.text: nabhasi gatāṃ rajasāṃ nadīm apaśyat ||258||
children.translated_text: then, casting his gaze far ahead,

children.text: sphurad atha khurarambhaṇādiśabdaprasaraṇam āvṛtasarvam eṣa6 śṛṇvan |
children.translated_text: he saw in the sky a river of dust. ||258||

children.text: avadad api parasparaṃ tad itthaṃ svahṛdayaraṅgataraṅganṛtyatulyam ||259||
children.translated_text: Hearing the spreading sound of clattering hooves and the like, covering everything around,

children.text: kalaya sakhi puraḥ surabhyanīkaṃ tadanu ca yuktaniyuktalokasaṅghaḥ |
children.translated_text: he also spoke to one another thus — [it was] like a dance of waves in the arena of his own heart. ||259||

children.text: tam anu sakhisuhṛtkumāravṛndaṃ vilasati tatra ca śubhrakṛṣṇayugmam ||260||
children.translated_text: 'Behold, O friend, the host of fragrant cows before us; and then the crowd of appointed and commissioned people;

children.text: kvacid api paśunāma bhāṣamāṇaḥ kvacid api rakṣakanāma veṇupāṇiḥ |
children.translated_text: after them, the troop of friends, dear ones, and boys — and there shines the pair of dark and fair [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s> and <s>Balarāma</s>].' ||260||

children.text: kvacid api sakhināma miṣṭavaṃśīsvarakalayākhilamoham ātanoti ||261||
children.translated_text: Somewhere calling the names of the cows, somewhere the names of the guardians, flute in hand;

children.text: 1. (a) orājīm;; 2. (b) anyadāvad; 3. (a) padyoskāḥ (?); 4. (b) tathāstu; 5. (b) prayattaḥ; 6. (b) eva;
children.translated_text: somewhere calling the names of friends — with the melody of his sweet flute-sound, he spreads enchantment over all. ||261||

children.text: upariracitapuṣpavṛṣṭisṛṣṭiḥ stavakṛtasaṃstava eva divyalokaḥ |
children.translated_text: [Footnotes: textual variants.]

children.text: sukhayati sakhi gokulasya lokān priyam anu sapriyatāṃ hi suṣṭhu dhatte ||262||
children.translated_text: The divine realm, having created a shower of flowers from above and composed hymns of praise,

children.text: harim atha dhavalānivāsam āptaṃ svam anu ca sannatam agrajena sārdham |
children.translated_text: delights the people of <s>Gokula</s>, O friend; for it holds affection toward the beloved and his beloveds. ||262||

children.text: vrajapatir upalabhya tacchramāpaṃ muhur apamṛjya ciraṃ dadarśa sāsram ||263||
children.translated_text: The king of <s>Vraja</s> (<s>Nanda</s>), receiving <s>Hari</s> clad in white garments, who had arrived and bowed before him together with the elder brother,

children.text: svayam atha janakaḥ samastayuktaḥ paśukulam ākulam ālayāya nītvā |
children.translated_text: wiping away the [dust from the] fatigue repeatedly, gazed [at him] for a long time with tears. ||263||

children.text: sakalam aghaharaṃ śramāpanuttiṃ pratinidideśa yataḥ sa eṣa eti ||264||
children.translated_text: Then the father (<s>Nanda</s>) himself, together with all [attendants], having led the agitated herd of cows to the stable,

children.text: iti vadati sakhījane samantād vṛṣaravijāṃ vadati sma kācid etya |
children.translated_text: directed all the removal of fatigue and purification — [announcing] 'because this is he [who has arrived].' ||264||

children.text: "vrajanṛpadayitā samaṃ vadhūbhiś calati sutaṃ prati maṅgalānusaṅgi ||265||
children.translated_text: As the group of friends was speaking thus all around the daughter of <s>Vṛṣabhānu</s>, a certain one came and said:

children.text: idam avakalayan sakhīsamūhas tvarinikhilādhikarādhikaṃ pratasthe |
children.translated_text: 'The beloved of the king of <s>Vraja</s> (<s>Yaśodā</s>), together with the daughters-in-law, proceeds toward her son, accompanied by auspicious [rites].' ||265||

children.text: vrajanṛpavanitānuṣaṅgaḥ kāmaḥ karam anu cāsajati sma maṅgalāni ||266||
children.translated_text: Understanding this, the group of <s>sakhīs</s> swiftly set forth, surpassing all [in their] authority;

children.text: agharipujananī tu sarvayuktā svapatham abhīkṣṇam asāv abhīkṣamāṇā |
children.translated_text: the attendants of the queen of <s>Vraja</s> placed auspicious items in their hands. ||266||

children.text: vṛṣaravitanujādibhiḥ snuṣābhiḥ samanugatā svasukhā cakāra1 ||267||
children.translated_text: The mother of the enemy of <s>Agha</s> (<s>Yaśodā</s>), fully accompanied, constantly gazing at her own path,

children.text: atha jayajayaśabdabhavyagītastavaghṛtadīpakapūrṇakumbhalājān |
children.translated_text: followed by her daughters-in-law headed by the daughter of <s>Vṛṣabhānu</s> (<s>Rādhā</s>), performed her own joy. ||267||

children.text: vacasi śirasi hastayoḥ śrayantī harijananīprabhṛtis tatiḥ pratasthe ||268||
children.translated_text: Then, bearing upon their lips the words 'Victory! Victory!', auspicious songs and hymns, lighted lamps of camphor, full water-pots, and puffed rice —

children.text: samagamad avarodhaniṣkramadvāravadhim iyaṃ sa tadā tu kṛṣṇacandraḥ |
children.translated_text: upon their heads and in their hands — the procession led by <s>Hari</s>'s mother set forth. ||268||

children.text: sahabalam abhiyan puraḥ pradeśaṃ śramajarucāpy abhitaḥ sukhaṃ vavarṣa ||269||
children.translated_text: This [procession] met him at the boundary of the outer courtyard gate; and then <s>Kṛṣṇacandra</s>,

children.text: atha sakusumalājavṛṣṭinīrājanasukham anv anu mātur aṅghrilagnaḥ |
children.translated_text: advancing with <s>Bala</s> (<s>Balarāma</s>) ahead to that spot, even with the glow born of his exertion, rained happiness all around. ||269||

children.text: aparagurujaneṣu2 cānvatiṣṭhat tad atha yathā yugapad balaś ca tadvat ||270||
children.translated_text: Then, after the <s>nīrājana</s> (waving of lamps) with a shower of flowers and puffed rice, clinging to his mother's feet,

children.text: tadanu ca jananī hṛdāsadāśīstatim adadād vacasā tu neti sarvā |
children.translated_text: he also paid obeisance to the other elders; and simultaneously <s>Bala</s> (<s>Balarāma</s>) did likewise. ||270||

children.text: sanayanajalagadgadaṃ gadantī kalakalavalgugirāśiṣaḥ śaśaṃsa ||271||
children.translated_text: Then the mother, from the depths of her heart, bestowed blessings abundantly — but with words, she could not [complete them];

children.text: atha balajananīyutā yaśodā sutayugalaṃ dadhatī kareṇa doṣṇi |
children.translated_text: speaking falteringly with tears in her eyes and a choked voice, she uttered sweet, melodious blessings. ||271||

children.text: svasadanam upanīya khedariktaṃ karaṇalaghuvyajanaṃ vidhūnute sma ||272||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Yaśodā</s>, together with <s>Bala</s>'s mother (<s>Rohiṇī</s>), holding the pair of sons by the hand and in her arms,

children.text: kṣaṇakatipayamātṛlālanāyāṃ jaḍavad upeyatur asmṛtiṃ sahotthau |
children.translated_text: having led them to her own home, freed from fatigue, gently fanned them with a light fan. ||272||

children.text: tadanu ca tanusevakāḥ samūcuḥ snapanajalapramukhaṃ samastam asti ||273||
children.translated_text: After a few moments of the mother's fondling, having risen as if from a stupor, they came to awareness;

children.text: harir atha haricandanena raktaṃ mṛgajamadena balas tu vastrayugmam |
children.translated_text: then the body-servants announced: 'Everything is ready, beginning with the bathing water.' ||273||

children.text: dadhad anudadhad aṅgarāgam evaṃ bhūṣaṇam āpa mātṛpārśvam ||274||
children.translated_text: <s>Hari</s>, [anointed] with <s>haricandana</s> (sandalwood) — reddish; and <s>Bala</s> with <s>mṛgamada</s> (musk); each wearing a pair of garments,

children.text: sakalam avayavaṃ nijaṃ saveśaṃ surabhitam apy atulaṃ karoti kṛṣṇaḥ |
children.translated_text: thus having applied bodily unguents and [received] ornaments, they went to their mother's side. ||274||

children.text: niṭilam atitamāṃ3 yad asya paśyaty api purujighṛtitātamātṛyugmam ||275||
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> makes each of his own limbs, adorned and fragrant, incomparable;

children.text: sutayugam atha mātṛyugmam āptaṃ taducitacitrakacitram āśu kṛtvā |
children.translated_text: when [the mothers] see the <s>tilaka</s> mark on his forehead — behold! — the pair of mothers are seized with the desire to kiss it. ||275||

children.text: amṛtarucidhareṇa pānakena kramukapuṭena ca nandayāñcakāra ||276||
children.translated_text: Then, having quickly adorned the pair of sons and the pair of mothers with their appropriate colorful ornaments,

children.text: sphurad iha jananīyugaṃ prasūtyor yugam api citratayā vibhāti nityam |
children.translated_text: he delighted them with a nectar-like drink (<s>pānaka</s>) and with <s>kramuka</s> (betel nut) packets. ||276||

children.text: yugayugam anutarkyate na śīlāt kva nu jananī jananīyatāvibhāgaḥ ||277||
children.translated_text: The pair of mothers shining here alongside the pair of sons — this always appears wondrous in its diversity;

children.text: śirasi dadhad apūrvapaṭṭapāśaṃ karam anu ratnajacitramitrayaṣṭim |
children.translated_text: pair after pair, [their relationship] is beyond reasoning — where indeed lies the distinction of motherliness? ||277||

children.text: balasahitatayācalaj jananyoś caraṇanatiṃ vidadhat payāṃsi dogdhum ||278||
children.translated_text: Wearing an unprecedented silk turban upon his head, holding in his hand a gem-studded, beautiful staff,

children.text: 1. (b) sukhīcakāra; 2. (a) ojanīsucānvatiṣṭhat; 3. (b) atitamaṃ
children.translated_text: together with <s>Bala</s>, he set out from his mothers, offering prostrations at their feet, to milk the cows. ||278||

children.text: atha kanakaja-dohanādi-pātrāṇy anuga-janāḥ samam eva te gṛhītvā |
children.translated_text: [Footnotes: textual variants.]

children.text: vyatijaya-manasā dravaṃ dadhānā drava-gamanāḥ samayus tadīya-padyām ||279||
children.translated_text: Then the attendants, taking golden milking vessels and the like all together,

children.text: punar atha vṛṣabhānujādi-vargaḥ sadana-śiro-gṛha-jāla-randhra-lagnaḥ |
children.translated_text: with minds overflowing with joy and carrying the liquid [vessels], with fluid steps they reached his trail. ||279||

children.text: upadiśati parasparaṃ sma vīkṣya priya-caritaṃ gavi-dohanāya jātam ||280||
children.translated_text: Again, the group headed by the daughter of <s>Vṛṣabhānu</s> (<s>Rādhā</s>), clinging to the lattice-windows of the upper chambers of their homes,

children.text: kalaya sakhi hariḥ pitṛ-nideśaṃ svayam anu yācanayā prapadyamānaḥ |
children.translated_text: looking on, pointed out to one another the beloved's activity of going forth to milk the cows. ||280||

children.text: paśupa-janani-yojanānupūrvyā saha-balam ācarati sma goṣu doham ||281||
children.translated_text: 'Behold, O friend! <s>Hari</s>, himself soliciting his father's command,

children.text: yadapi ca harihūtimādhurībhiḥ sa nadati sarvaka eva dhenusaṅghaiḥ |
children.translated_text: by the arrangement of the cowherd mothers, together with <s>Bala</s>, performs the milking among the cows.' ||281||

children.text: tadapi ca bata kāpi tasya śikṣāvaśāgatayā tam iyarti tena hūtā ||282||
children.translated_text: 'Even though by the sweetness of <s>Hari</s>'s call, every single herd of cows bellows [in response],

children.text: atha parihitam uttarīyabaddhaṃ draḍhayati gāḍhatayā gavām adhīndraḥ |
children.translated_text: yet alas! a certain [cow], through the mastery of his training, comes to him — called by that [particular call].' ||282||

children.text: tad anu ca mṛdupāśanaddhavatsaṃ navadhavalācaraṇena saṃyunakti ||283||
children.translated_text: Then the lord of bulls (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), having tightened the upper garment tied around [him], firmly secures [the cow];

children.text: kṣitim anu caraṇāgradattabhāraḥ
children.translated_text: then, tying the calf with a soft rope, he joins it with a newly whitened [cow]. ||283||

children.text: praṇamitajānuyugāntarasthapātraḥ |
children.translated_text: Placing his weight on the tips of his feet upon the ground,

children.text: muhur api kalayan sagostanāgraṃ
children.translated_text: with a vessel placed between his lowered knees,

children.text: smitam api dugdham api sma dogdhi kṛṣṇaḥ ||284||
children.translated_text: repeatedly touching the tip of the udder,

children.text: kalaya harir amūm adugdha dhenuṃ katham aparā duhate svayaṃ vilokya |
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> milks both smiles and milk. ||284|| 'Behold! <s>Hari</s> milked that cow which was unmilked — how is it that another [cow] is being milked by herself, just upon seeing [him]?'

children.text: ahaha tadavalokya paśya dūrād anukurute jaradaṅganāgaṇaś ca ||285||
children.translated_text: Ah! Seeing that from afar, behold — even the groups of old women imitate [their dancing]! ||285||

children.text: drutam atha payasāṃ nipān prahṛtya prayayur amī vrajarānmukhā gṛhāya |
children.translated_text: Then swiftly, having delivered the vessels of milk, these [cowherds], facing <s>Vraja</s>, proceeded homeward;

children.text: harir atha sakalaḥ suhṛdvṛtiśrīḥ kavikavitaḥ sa sasāra rājasadma ||286||
children.translated_text: and <s>Hari</s>, complete, the beauty of the circle of friends, celebrated in the songs of poets, went to the royal residence. ||286||

children.text: balam anu sakhibhiḥ sahāsajalpaḥ karakaratāḍanayā mithaḥ pramodī |
children.translated_text: Following <s>Bala</s> (<s>Balarāma</s>), with his companions, with jesting talk, delighting mutually in playful clapping,

children.text: samadagajagatir vicitravetraḥ parisaram eti saran sarojanetraḥ ||287||
children.translated_text: walking with the gait of a lordly elephant, with a variegated staff, the lotus-eyed one goes about the precinct. ||287||

children.text: saraṇim anusarann amuṃ pradeśaṃ punar amum apy amum apy amuṃ viveśa
murajid adhiruroha karṇikāgraṃ nijanijasevanasiddhaye prayāmaḥ ||288||
children.translated_text: the slayer of <s>Mura</s> ascended the summit of the pericarp — going forth for the accomplishment of his own personal service. ||288||
Following the path, he entered this area, then this one too, and then this one and that one;

children.text: iti vividhatayānuvarṇyamānaḥ savidhasametatayāvakarṇyamānaḥ |
children.translated_text: Thus, being described in various ways, being heard about as one who approaches closely,

children.text: upajananaisa etya tannideśāt klamam apanetum iyāya vāsasadma ||289||
children.translated_text: having come from that place with birth-joy, to remove fatigue, he went to his resting chamber. ||289||

children.text: drutam atha vṛṣabhānujādivargaḥ priyam upasevitum āvṛtīyamānaḥ |
children.translated_text: Then swiftly, the group beginning with the daughter of <s>Vṛṣabhānu</s> (<s>Rādhā</s>), returning to serve their beloved,

children.text: akuruta jalatālavṛntacarcādyupakaraṇaṃ kalayaṃs tadīyaśarma ||290||
children.translated_text: made ready the articles of service — water, fan, betel-leaf, ointment, and so forth — contemplating his happiness. ||290||

children.text: ruciramṛdulatūlikāñcikhaṭṭām upari niveśam amuṃ niṣevyamāṇāḥ |
children.translated_text: Attending upon him seated above upon a beautiful, soft, fine couch,
