children.text: yad iha sukham amuṣya tan nijātmapratiphalitaṃ nijam eva tā viduḥ sma ||291||
children.translated_text: whatever happiness was his — they knew it as their own, reflected in their own selves. ||291||

children.text: yadapi tam anusevate samastā tatir iyam uttamakalpam alpakaṃ na |
children.translated_text: Although all of them attend upon him — this ministration, even of the highest order, is not slight;

children.text: tadapi ca vṛṣabhānujā yadā yat kalayati tan navatāṃ sadā prayāti ||292||
children.translated_text: yet whatever the daughter of <s>Vṛṣabhānu</s> (<s>Rādhā</s>) does — that always attains newness. ||292||

children.text: navam iva mithunaṃ mithaḥ sthitaṃ yan
children.translated_text: That this couple, standing together, is ever new;

children.text: navam iva rāgajanuś ca yasya nityam |
children.translated_text: that the passion born between them is ever new;

children.text: katham iva navatāṃ na tasya vinded
children.translated_text: how could the sharing of that which is known as

children.text: vyatibhajanaṃ harirādhikābhidhasya ||293||
children.translated_text: <s>Hari-Rādhikā</s> not attain newness? ||293||

children.text: iti rajanimukhe gate sukhena prahitacaraḥ śiśur āgataḥ sma vakti |
children.translated_text: Thus, when the evening came, a servant sent [ahead] happily came and announced:

children.text: vrajapatir adhunā svabhogadhāma praviśati tena samaṃ balādayaś ca ||294||
children.translated_text: 'The lord of <s>Vraja</s> is now entering his palace of enjoyment' — and along with him, <s>Bala</s> (<s>Balarāma</s>) and the others too. ||294||

children.text: atha muravijayī cacāla tasmāt pitṛsavidhaṃ pidadhan nijasmitādi |
children.translated_text: Then the conqueror of <s>Mura</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) departed from that place toward his father, bestowing his own smile and the rest;

children.text: sudṛg iyam api tarhi goparājñīnikaṭam atiprakaṭaṃ vihāya vartma ||295||
children.translated_text: and this beautiful-eyed one (<s>Rādhā</s>) too then, leaving behind the conspicuous path, [went] near the queen of the cowherds. ||295||

children.text: murajiti savidhaṃ gate vrajejyā nṛpasahitā muditā balādayaś ca |
children.translated_text: When the slayer of <s>Mura</s> went near, the queen of <s>Vraja</s>, together with the king, joyful, and <s>Bala</s> and others,

children.text: sajalajalamucīva cātakādyāḥ kalakalavalgu yayus tadābhimukhyam ||296||
children.translated_text: like <s>cātaka</s> birds [rushing] toward a rain-cloud bearing water, went toward him with sweet, melodious [cries]. ||296||

children.text: yadapi ravisamaḥ śaśī vibhāti vrajabhuvi tarhy api kāntibhedarītyā |
children.translated_text: Though the moon, equal to the sun, shines in the land of <s>Vraja</s>, yet by the different manner of radiance,

children.text: rajanidinavibhāgam īkṣamāṇā vyavahṛtibhedam amī sadā bhajanti ||297||
children.translated_text: observing the division of night and day, these [residents] always observe the differences of activity. ||297||

children.text: atha niviviśire vrajeśvarādyā danujaripupramukhāś ca bhinnapaṅkti |
children.translated_text: Then the lord of <s>Vraja</s> and others entered, and those headed by the enemy of demons (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), in separate rows;

children.text: iti1 hi hasarasaḥ samastabhojyaṃ svadanavidhiṃ nayate tad anyathā na ||298||
children.translated_text: thus, with the flavor of laughter, the complete meal was conducted through the rite of tasting — and not otherwise. ||298||

children.text: dinamukham anu tatra pākavṛnde dinajaṭharaprasaraṃ dināṅghripūrtim |
children.translated_text: Following the morning, regarding the cooking preparation — the expanse of the day's appetite, the fulfillment of the day's measure,

children.text: ṛtuvalayanideśadeśabhedaṃ vividhavidhānagatīḥ svayaṃ tu viddhi ||299||
children.translated_text: the differences of region and season and their cycles — know for yourself the various procedures and arrangements. ||299||

children.text: prathamam iha phulaṃ vanād upāttaṃ bakaripunā svadanāya suṣṭhu jātam |
children.translated_text: First, here, a flower taken from the forest by the enemy of <s>Baka</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), perfectly suited for savoring;

children.text: punar iha havir2ādigorasāntaṃ śatavidhatemanajemanaṃ babhūva ||300||
children.translated_text: then here, beginning with oblation-foods and ending with cow-products, there arose a feast of a hundred kinds to be enjoyed. ||300||

children.text: atha surabhijalena suṣṭhu tāmbūlajapuṭakena ca śodhitāsyapadmāḥ |
children.translated_text: Then, having thoroughly cleansed their lotus-mouths with fragrant water and betel-leaf packets,

children.text: vrajanṛpatitadīyanandanādyā bahir upaveśasabhām abhāsayanta ||301||
children.translated_text: the king of <s>Vraja</s>, his son, and others illuminated the outer assembly hall. ||301||

children.text: atha punar adhiruhya candraśālā3-
children.translated_text: Then again, ascending to the terrace

children.text: mukham amṛtāṃśu4mukhīgaṇāḥ svakāntam |
children.translated_text: of the moonlit upper chamber, the groups of nectar-faced women [saw] their beloved;

children.text: abhimukhasadasi sphūranniveśaṃ
children.translated_text: as he appeared in the assembly before them,

children.text: dadṛśur amuṃ nibhṛtaṃ mitho 'py anūcuḥ ||302||
children.translated_text: they beheld him and privately also spoke to one another. ||302||

children.text: iha viviṣakalākalāpavijñāḥ samuditatāṃ samavāpur utkacittāḥ |
children.translated_text: Here, those expert in the assemblage of all various arts, with minds eager, attained a state of excited joy;

children.text: amum uditām itāḥ kalānidhānaṃ svakulakalāṃ vinivedya bhartum aicchan ||303||
children.translated_text: having approached him — that treasury of arts — having displayed their own family arts, they wished to offer [them]. ||303||

children.text: yadapi harir asau kalānivijñas tadapi tadalpakalāsu toṣam eti |
children.translated_text: Though <s>Hari</s> is himself the supreme knower of all arts, yet he delights even in their modest arts;

children.text: yadapi kṛtamukhāḥ kalāsu sabhyās tadapi harer mukhavīkṣayā ramante ||304||
children.translated_text: and though the courtiers are accomplished in arts, yet they delight in beholding <s>Hari</s>'s face. ||304||

children.text: na bhajati sakalaṃ sadā sabhāyāḥ samavasaraṃ bata kāvyanāṭakādi |
children.translated_text: The complete assembly does not always attend to poetry, drama, and such;

children.text: iti niśi niśi bhinnatānumatyā vrajapatir iṣṭatamaṃ tadātaniṣṭa ||305||
children.translated_text: thus, night after night, with differently approved [programs], the lord of <s>Vraja</s> arranged the most desired [entertainment]. ||305||

children.text: kvaca niśi nṛpatiḥ sa vaṣṭi kāvyaṃ kvacid api nāṭyakalāṃ kvacāpi citram |
children.translated_text: On some night the king desires poetry, on some other the art of drama, on yet another, painting;

children.text: pṛthag api na pṛthag vibhāti sarvaṃ hariracitāni paraṃ puraḥ karoti ||306||
children.translated_text: though separately [considered], everything shines as inseparable — [for] the compositions of <s>Hari</s> bring the supreme to the fore. ||306||

children.text: iti purukutuke gate tu yāme haribalasaṃvalitāḥ samastalokāḥ |
children.translated_text: Thus, when the watch [of the night] had passed with great curiosity, all the people, accompanied by <s>Hari</s> and <s>Bala</s>,

children.text: vrajanarapatim utthitaṃ vilokya prati tadavasthiti tasthur ādareṇa ||307||
children.translated_text: seeing the lord of <s>Vraja</s> risen, stood in their respective positions with respect. ||307||

children.text: murajiti gadituṃ kim apy anīśe pitari ca bāṣpaniruddhakaṇṭhadeśe |
children.translated_text: When the slayer of <s>Mura</s> was unable to speak anything, and when the father's throat was choked with tears,

children.text: sthaviragurujanā dvayaṃ nivedya pratividhaye samanaskam ācaran sma ||308||
children.translated_text: the venerable elders, presenting both [father and son] with [blessings], performed the appropriate rites with a unified mind. ||308||

children.text: avanatapitṛkaḥ parān yathārhaṃ nativinayādibhṛtān vidhāya kṛṣṇaḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, having bowed to his father, performed due salutations, humility, and the rest toward the elders as befitting;

children.text: sahabalam anugatya mātṛyugmaṃ taducitalālitatāṃ ciraṃ jagāma ||309||
children.translated_text: then, along with <s>Bala</s> (<s>Balarāma</s>), following the pair of mothers, he long enjoyed their befitting caresses. ||309||

children.text: anumatim atha mātṛyugmadattām avakalayan praṇaman sanamradṛṣṭiḥ |
children.translated_text: Then, discerning the permission given by the pair of mothers, bowing with lowered eyes,

children.text: haladharam anugamya taṃ praṇamya śritanavavarṣavaraḥ svavāsam āpa ||310||
children.translated_text: following <s>Haladhara</s> (<s>Balarāma</s>, the Plough-bearer) and bowing to him — the best of fresh adolescents attained his own dwelling. ||310||

children.text: 1. (b) iha; 2. (a) harir ādio; 3. (b) candraśālīo ; 4. (a) amṛtāśuo
children.translated_text: 1. (b) iha; 2. (a) harir ādio; 3. (b) candraśālīo; 4. (a) amṛtāśuo

children.text: iti muraharavarṇanāṃ sa kurvan muraharam apy avalokya sadmasīmni |
children.translated_text: Thus, describing the slayer of <s>Mura</s>, and seeing the slayer of <s>Mura</s> at the boundary of the residence,

children.text: drutataram avaruhya rādhikādir nijatadapahṇavam ācacāra vargaḥ ||311||
children.translated_text: swiftly descending, the group beginning with <s>Rādhikā</s> performed their own concealment [of the secret meeting]. ||311||

children.text: iha matam apareṇa sarvakāntāsv anuniśam añcati so 'yam ittham astu |
children.translated_text: Here, another opinion holds that he goes to all his beloveds every night in this way — let that be so;

children.text: hṛdaya kalaya kintu cāru rādhāharicaritaṃ paritaḥ smara tvam atra ||312||
children.translated_text: but O heart, contemplate the beautiful pastimes of <s>Rādhā</s> and <s>Hari</s> all around — remember that here. ||312||

children.text: vṛṣaravitanayādibhis tadā drāk samagami hāri hariḥ suveśa eṣaḥ |
children.translated_text: Then, the daughter of <s>Vṛṣabhānu</s> and the others swiftly met <s>Hari</s> — this enchanting, beautifully dressed one;

children.text: navaghana iva vidyutāvalībhir yad amṛtavṛṣṭimayī babhūva dṛṣṭiḥ ||313||
children.translated_text: like a fresh rain-cloud with rows of lightning — for his glance had become a shower of nectar. ||313||

children.text: vratatimaṇivivekakhaṇḍiśobhā
children.translated_text: The beauty that shatters the discernment of the group of observers,

children.text: parimalabhāg iha sadma kintu kuñjam |
children.translated_text: a share of fragrance — here the dwelling is not [merely] a house, but a bower;

children.text: iha kim u kusumaṃ kim aṃśukaṃ vā
children.translated_text: what here is a flower, what is a garment?

children.text: śayanaṃ idaṃ mithunam yad adhyaśete ||314||
children.translated_text: This is the bed upon which the couple reclined. ||314||

children.text:
iti nityalīlā
 ||2 ||
children.translated_text: Thus [ends] the Eternal Pastimes (<s>Nitya-līlā</s>). ||2||

children.text: śrīgopālāya namaḥ,1
children.translated_text: Salutation to <s>Śrī Gopāla</s>!

children.text: sā ca janmādikā sā ca nityalīlā śrutiritā |
children.translated_text: That birth-pastime and that eternal pastime (<s>nitya-līlā</s>) are described in the <s>Śrutis</s>;

children.text: mithaḥ pūrvā parā ca syād bījavṛkṣapravāhavat ||o ||
children.translated_text: mutually, the former and the latter are like seed and tree in a stream. ||o||

children.text: atha nityāntarvartisarvartulīlā
children.translated_text: Now, all the seasonal pastimes within the eternal [pastimes].

children.text: atha hṛdi kuru vallavīsutasya stavam anu-gautama-tantra-labdham asya |
children.translated_text: Now, hold in your heart the hymn of the son of the cowherd woman (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), obtained from the <s>Gautama Tantra</s>,

children.text: bahu-vidha-samayāgamād vicitraṃ śubha-caritam racita-sva-bhakta-bhakti ||1||
children.translated_text: his variegated auspicious conduct [performed] at the arrival of many various seasons, which creates devotion in his own devotees. ||1||

children.text: januṣi madhu-ṛtoḥ kumāra-bhāve taruṇimani pravayastayā ca yoge |
children.translated_text: In birth, in boyhood of the spring season, in youth, in maturity, and in union —

children.text: dayita-dayitayor vasanta-rāga-prabhṛti-kalā lasati sma śāmyati sma ||2||
children.translated_text: the art of the spring <s>rāga</s> (passionate melody) and the like shone forth between the beloved and his beloved, and also subsided. ||2||

children.text: tad idam ṛtuṣu ṣaṭsu rucyabhedāt pṛthag anuvarṇanam iṣyate tathā hi |
children.translated_text: This [description], differing according to beauty in each of the six seasons, is desired to be described separately; for thus —

children.text: harir iha vihṛtipracāracaryāṃ vidadhad avarṇayad eṣa tarhi tarhi ||3||
children.translated_text: <s>Hari</s>, performing the conduct of the course of his pastimes here, described it then and then. ||3||

children.text: prathamam iha śṛṇuṣva citta vākyaṃ
children.translated_text: First, hear here, O mind, the word

children.text: kvaca niśi yat prabhum āha hāri rādhā |
children.translated_text: which the enchanting <s>Rādhā</s> spoke to the Lord at some night;

children.text: atha kalaya harer vacaś ca tasyām
children.translated_text: then contemplate <s>Hari</s>'s speech to her,

children.text: amṛtavad antaraśantamasya dātṛ ||4||
children.translated_text: bestowing what is like nectar, dispelling inner darkness. ||4||

children.text: "ahaha vanavanaṃ nidāghadagdhasthalam aṭasi svavapuḥ prapīdya rukṣaḥ2 |
children.translated_text: "Alas! You wander through forest after forest, on ground scorched by summer, pressing your own body, dry and harsh;

children.text: murahara tava cintanena jīrṇān katham avitāsi janān idaṃ na jāne ||"5||
children.translated_text: O slayer of <s>Mura</s>, how you have protected the wasted people through contemplation of you — this I do not know." ||5||

children.text: idam abhihitam ākalayya kṛṣṇaḥ smitavadanaḥ svayam āha yat tu rādhām |
children.translated_text: Having understood what was thus spoken, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, with a smiling face, himself said this to <s>Rādhā</s>;

children.text: tad avakalaya citta vittam etat tava bahuvṛttipadaṃ bhavisyad asti ||6||
children.translated_text: contemplate that, O mind — this is [your] treasure, a seat of many modes [of understanding] that is to come. ||6||

children.text: "ahaha sumukhi nedam anyad ūhyaṃ tapaṛtum anv api tatra citratāsti |
children.translated_text: "Alas, O beautiful-faced one, this is not to be imagined otherwise — even in the summer season, there is wonder there;

children.text: kvaca sa hi madhuvat kvacāpi varṣāvad anubhavaṃ dadate svayaṃ kvacāpi ||7||
children.translated_text: for somewhere it is like [the sweetness of] honey, somewhere like the rainy season — they bestow experience by themselves, and somewhere [otherwise]. ||7||

children.text: vanam iha yad anūpam asti tasmin madhur iva bhāti nidāghakāla eṣaḥ |
children.translated_text: This forest here is rich in water — within it, this summer season shines as if sweet;

children.text: nirudakataruṇi svayaṃ nidāghaḥ kṣitidharanirjharabhājivārṣikaśrīḥ ||8||
children.translated_text: summer itself, [though normally] waterless and harsh, [here] has the beauty of the rainy season with mountain-streams. ||8||

children.text: mama samam amarībhir atra vṛndā nikhilavanaṃ paritaḥ pariṣkaroti |
children.translated_text: Along with me, <s>Vṛndā</s> (the forest goddess), together with the celestial women, adorns the entire forest all around;

children.text: yad aharahar ahaṃ bhavatyā saha sahacāribhir apy alaṃ bhajāmi ||9||
children.translated_text: for day after day, I, together with you and with [our] companions, fully enjoy [it]. ||9||

children.text: sumadhuranavanārikelanīraṃ tadupamatālaphalāmbu cāsya3 majja |
children.translated_text: The very sweet, fresh coconut water, and the water from the palmyra fruit comparable to it — O thirsty one, plunge in;

children.text: upahṛtam iha vṛndayā satṛṣṇe sakhisahite mayi tṛptim ādadhīta ||10||
children.translated_text: brought here by <s>Vṛndā</s>, together with your companions, may it bring satisfaction to me. ||10||

children.text: sa panasasahakāragostanīnāṃ
children.translated_text: From the jackfruit, mango, and <s>gostanī</s> fruits,

children.text: rasavasanaṃ racayāmy ahaṃ samitraḥ |
children.translated_text: I, together with my friends, shall prepare a drink of their essence;

children.text: tvadadharamadhu māṃ tu tatra citraṃ
children.translated_text: but the honey of your lips, O beautiful-browed one — wonder! —

children.text: smarayati sāndratayā svam eva subhru ||11||
children.translated_text: reminds me there of its own [sweetness] by its density. ||11||

children.text: atha vayam api tāṃ vihārabhūmiṃ tava kalayāma yadi tvadīyam iṣṭam |"
children.translated_text: Then we too shall visit that playground of yours, if it is your wish."

children.text: 1. (b) not found; the following verse is placed after atha etc.; 2. (a) rukṣaḥ; 3.. (a) margin: cālpa;iti vṛṣaravijādibhiḥ pradiṣṭas tvaritam amūbhir amūṃ hariḥ pratasthe ||12||
children.translated_text: Thus directed by the daughter of <s>Vṛṣabhānu</s> and others, <s>Hari</s> swiftly set out with them. ||12||

children.text: prathamam abhiyayau vasantavantaṃ vipinaviśeṣam atha pradeśam anyam |
children.translated_text: First he went to a particular grove rich in the spring season, then to another area;

children.text: anubhavatulayānubhāvayaṃś ca pravadati sa sma sanarmasuṣṭhu vācam ||13||
children.translated_text: and experiencing and causing others to experience by [mutual] comparison, he spoke many a well-crafted, playful word. ||13||

children.text: ahani vayam amūṃ nirīkṣya subhru varasaritaṃ purataḥ samaṃ sajantaḥ |
children.translated_text: "During the day, O beautiful-browed one, having beheld that excellent river before us, together [with you],

children.text: nijanijadhavalās tu pāyayitvā viharaṇam atra suhṛdbhir ācarāma ||14||
children.translated_text: having given our own white [cows] to drink, we shall here sport with [our] friends. ||14||

children.text: śaśimukhi śucimāsi madhyamadhyaṃ dinam anu mandiratulyaśailagarbhe |
children.translated_text: O moon-faced one, in the middle of the pure month, day after day, in the interior of the mountain resembling a temple,

children.text: jharanikaraparītapārśvadeśe saha bhavatīkam ahaṃ mudā śayiṣye ||15||
children.translated_text: at the sides surrounded by clusters of waterfalls, I shall joyfully rest together with you. ||15||

children.text: savitṛduhitṛtuṅgatīragarbhe śaśimaṇidhāmani kuñjapuñjarāji |
children.translated_text: In the interior of the high bank of the daughter of the Sun (<s>Yamunā</s>), in the moonstone-jeweled abode, the rows of bower-clusters —

children.text: anurahasam ahar vrajāntarantaḥ saha bhavatīkam ahaṃ mudāśrayiṣye ||16||
children.translated_text: in secret, during the day, within the inner part of <s>Vraja</s>, I shall joyfully resort [there] together with you. ||16||

children.text: vayam iha sariti draveṇa gatvā viharaṇaṃ narmasaśarmatāṃ nayāma |
children.translated_text: Let us go here to the river in a boat and make our sport attain the state of joy and play."

children.text: iti vṛṣaravijāṃ vidhṛtya bāhāv aparasakhīsahitāṃ ca calann uvāca ||17||
children.translated_text: Thus holding the daughter of <s>Vṛṣabhānu</s> (<s>Rādhā</s>) on his arm, along with other companions, he walked and spoke. ||17||

children.text: nikaṭanikaṭatāṃ calaṃs taṭinyā
children.translated_text: Moving ever closer to the river,

children.text: nirudakamātrapadaṃ kramāt tyajaṃś ca |
children.translated_text: gradually leaving behind the ground that was merely waterless:

children.text: "tapamadhunṛparāṣṭrayugmamadhyaṃ
children.translated_text: "O moon-faced one, see here, as if gone

children.text: gatam iva candramukhi svam atra paśya ||18||
children.translated_text: to the middle of the twin kingdoms of the summer and honey season. ||18||

children.text: iha kamalavanāni tāpaśīrṇāny api kamalāni kiyanti dhārayanti |
children.translated_text: Here, the lotus groves, though withered by the heat, still bear some lotuses;

children.text: tata iha sariti praviśya yūyaṃ vayam api tāni vicitya cāru cinmaḥ ||19||
children.translated_text: therefore, entering the river here, you [gather them], and we too, having searched for those beautiful ones, shall collect them. ||19||

children.text: muhur iha paritaḥ samāvrajantaḥ sariti rasaprasaraṃ gaveṣayantaḥ |
children.translated_text: Here, the bees, going about again and again, seeking the flow of nectar in the river,

children.text: navanavatanayāya padminīnāṃ stanam iva vāriruhaṃ duhanti bhṛṅgāḥ ||"20||
children.translated_text: milk the water-born [lotuses] as if [they were] the breasts of the lotus-maidens, for the ever-new child." ||20||

children.text: iti vanavalitaṃ chalaṃ vidhāya vrajasumukhīḥ saritaṃ praveśyamānā. |
children.translated_text: Having thus devised a ruse of forest wandering, making the beautiful-faced women of <s>Vraja</s> enter the river,

children.text: kamalacayanalakṣyataḥ svavāñchālasitavaśāḥ1 sa cakāra tatra tatra ||21||
children.translated_text: under the pretext of gathering lotuses, he made them subject to his own playful desire, here and there. ||21||

children.text: "kamalam idam aho mayā tu labdhaṃ kanakaruciprathitaṃ tvayā tu nīlam |"
iti vividhamiṣaṃ parasparaṃ tāḥ samam ajitena vihārasāram īyuḥ ||22||
children.translated_text: Thus, with various pretexts, those [<s>gopīs</s>] together with the Unconquered One (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) enjoyed the essence of sport. ||22||
"Oh, this lotus was found by me — golden in hue! But this blue one by you!"

children.text: hṛdi kim u kamalaṃ lalāga kiṃ vā harikara ity amukā viśaṅkamānāḥ |
children.translated_text: "What clung to my heart — a lotus, or <s>Hari</s>'s hand?" — doubting thus,

children.text: vrajajanisudṛśas tadā navīnāḥ sapulakaśītkṛtikāritām avāpuḥ ||23||
children.translated_text: the beautiful-eyed women born in <s>Vraja</s>, being novices, experienced horripilation and shivering. ||23||

children.text: atha vihasati tatra jihmanetrā murajiti cikṣipur āyudhābham ambhaḥ |
children.translated_text: Then, as the slayer of <s>Mura</s> laughed, those with sidelong glances threw water at him like a weapon;

children.text: sa ca tad akṛta tāsu kintu tāsāṃ tadapagamaḥ kriyate sma tasya tena ||24||
children.translated_text: and he did the same to them — but their [water-throwing] removed his [fatigue]. ||24||

children.text: harir asurasahasralakṣajetā svayam abalābhir ayaṃ vijetum iṣṭaḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Hari</s>, the conqueror of hundreds of thousands of demons, himself wished to be conquered by these tender women;

children.text: yad iha jayam avāpa tan na citraṃ yad atha jitas tad atīva citram atra ||25||
children.translated_text: that he conquered here is not wonderful — but that he was conquered, that is most wonderful indeed. ||25||

children.text: yadapi ca jalasecanena kīrṇas tadapi parābhavam api nāghaśatruḥ |
children.translated_text: Even though he was drenched by water-splashing, the enemy of <s>Agha</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) [regarded] even defeat [as victory];

children.text: iti bhrukuṭim adhāt tu vārṣabhānavy atha sa tu tatra babhūva citrakalpaḥ ||26||
children.translated_text: Thus the daughter of <s>Vṛṣabhānu</s> (<s>Rādhā</s>) furrowed her brows — and thereupon he became wondrously inventive.

children.text: harim atha sakalābalāvilāsāl laghu jagṛhur jitakāśitāṃ dadhānāḥ |
children.translated_text: Then the doe-eyed women swiftly seized <s>Hari</s> from all the play of the cowherd women, bearing the pride of conquest;

children.text: punar api hasitānunāpabhaṅgyā bahir avadhānam adhāpayan mṛgākṣyaḥ ||27||
children.translated_text: yet again, through gestures of laughter and coaxing, the doe-eyed ones directed his attention outward.

children.text: avahitavati jīvanādhināthe vṛṣaravijā drutam asya karṣaṇāya |
children.translated_text: When the lord of her life was attentive, the daughter of <s>Vṛṣabhānu</s> (<s>Rādhā</s>), to attract him swiftly,

children.text: taṭam aṭitavatīha2 kṛṣṇanāmāpy anugatatāṃ samavāpa rāgabaddhaḥ ||28||
children.translated_text: roaming along the bank — she, bearing even the name '<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>' (the dark one), attained the state of following [him], bound by passion.

children.text: 1. (a) ovaṣāḥ; 2. (a) aṭitavatīti
children.translated_text: [Textual notes]

children.text: drutam atha paricārikā murāriṃ vṛṣaravijāṃ savayastatīr amūś ca |
children.translated_text: Then the attendants swiftly [attended to] <s>Murāri</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), the daughter of <s>Vṛṣabhānu</s>, and her companions of equal age;

children.text: mṛdu mṛdu vasanena mārjitāṅgān akṛṣata vastravarān adhārayaṃś ca ||29||
children.translated_text: gently, gently wiping their limbs with cloth, they drew off [the water] and draped them in fine garments.

children.text: svayam atha vṛṣabhānujā svakāntaṃ mṛgamadakuṅkumacūrṇamarjitāṅgam |
children.translated_text: Then the daughter of <s>Vṛṣabhānu</s> (<s>Rādhā</s>) herself, anointing the limbs of her beloved with musk and saffron powder,

children.text: sulaghu vidadhatī jahāra jāḍyaṃ bahir abahiḥ punar ājahāra jāḍyam ||30||
children.translated_text: performing [the service] very lightly, dispelled his stupor outwardly, and then once more drew forth his stupor [of love].

children.text: atha ghusṛṇaviśeṣakāṃśuyuktaṃ laghutaraveśaviśeṣaśobhimuktam |
children.translated_text: Then the daughter of <s>Vṛṣabhānu</s> made her beloved [resplendent] with a distinctive saffron mark, with rays, wearing a lighter, specially beautiful attire, freed [of heaviness];

children.text: akuruta vṛṣabhānujā svakāntaṃ sa ca rucitām akarod amūṃ nitāntam ||31||
children.translated_text: and he in turn made her exceedingly beautiful.

children.text: kramukasitakarāñciparṇavīṭīr adita sakhī harirādhayor mukhāntaḥ |
children.translated_text: A <s>sakhī</s> (companion) placed betel-leaf rolls made of areca, white [lime], and leaf into the mouths of <s>Hari</s> and <s>Rādhā</s>;

children.text: yugalam api tayoḥ sakhījanānām adhita sukhaprathanāya vaktramadhye ||32||
children.translated_text: and the pair also placed [betel] in the mouths of the <s>sakhīs</s> (companions) for the spreading of happiness.

children.text: atha kamalakarāḥ sakāntakāntāḥ savilasitaṃ sadanāya gantukāmāḥ |
children.translated_text: Then, lotus-handed, with their lovely beloveds, with playful grace, wishing to go home,

children.text: vijitakamalapatracārunetrā virurucire nikhilena khelitena ||33||
children.translated_text: with beautiful eyes surpassing the beauty of lotus petals, they shone resplendent with all their play.

children.text: kvacid api hariṇā samaṃ vyadhus tāḥ puru kamalākamali prahāsayuktam |
children.translated_text: Somewhere, together with <s>Hari</s>, they played abundantly a game of lotus-play, accompanied by great laughter;

children.text: idam iha na vidus tu tena śaśvaj jitam akhilaṃ bhuvaneṣu kevalena ||34||
children.translated_text: but they did not know this — that by that [laughter] alone, everything in all the worlds was constantly conquered.

children.text: iti bahuvidhakhelamālayāntaṃ jagṛhur amūr amunā samaṃ samastāḥ |
children.translated_text: Thus, having taken up the garland of many kinds of play to its end, all of them together with him,

children.text: tadanu ca varaniṣkuṭasthadhiṣṇyaṃ praviviśur āviviśuś ca tasya bhāsi ||35||
children.translated_text: then entered the excellent bower that was their dwelling-place, and entered into his radiance.

children.text: maṇisadanam idaṃ vṛtīr1 atītaṃ varasarasīsarasīruhālimadhyam |
children.translated_text: This jeweled mansion, surpassing [all] enclosures, in the midst of rows of lotuses on beautiful lakes,

children.text: sukusumasukumāragarbhatūlīmiladupadhānaśubhaṃyumañjuśayyam2 ||36||
children.translated_text: with a lovely bed of soft cushions filled with the pollen of tender, beautiful flowers —

children.text: sarucinihitatālavṛntabhṛṅgārakamukhaśarmadavastusaṃstutāṅgam |
children.translated_text: its limbs praised by objects of comfort — fan-palm handles, bell-metal vessels, and the like — placed with taste;

children.text: drutataram aviśad viśaṃś ca śayyām adhivasati sma hariḥ smitāṃśuśobhi ||37||
children.translated_text: very swiftly he entered, and entering, occupied the bed — <s>Hari</s>, shining with the rays of his smile.

children.text: yugmakam
children.translated_text: A pair of verses

children.text: tam atha kusumacāmaraṃ dadhānā vṛṣaravijā svayam eva sevate sma |
children.translated_text: Then the daughter of <s>Vṛṣabhānu</s> (<s>Rādhā</s>) herself, holding a flower-fan (<s>cāmara</s>), served him;

children.text: anṛjudṛśam amuṃ balaṃ chalaṃ ca praṇayi sa tu praṇayan nināya śayyām ||38||
children.translated_text: and he, with a sidelong glance, [playfully using] both force and stratagem, lovingly, led her to the bed.

children.text: iyam api tata eva khedadambhād alasanibhasthititāṃ babhāja tasyām |
children.translated_text: She too, from that point, through a pretense of weariness, assumed the appearance of languor upon it;

children.text: tadanu savayasaḥ sacandratāmbūlakam anu śarma dadhus tayor dvayoś ca ||39||
children.translated_text: then the companions of equal age, with betel mixed with camphor, bestowed comfort upon both of them.

children.text: tadanu tad anumāya tena tasyā rahasi mithaḥ sthitivāñchitaṃ vayasyāḥ |
children.translated_text: Then, inferring through that [behavior] the mutual desire of those two to remain alone in private, the companions

children.text: samiṣam apagatāḥ kṣaṇaṃ tu kācin mṛdumardanam etayor vyadhatta ||40||
children.translated_text: departed with a smile for a moment; but one [companion] performed gentle massage for the two.

children.text: iyam api vigatā dvayasya nidrāṃ chalaracitāṃ chalam āracayya yat tu |
children.translated_text: She too departed; having fashioned a pretense-sleep of the pair, fashioning [her own] pretense [of leaving],

children.text: nayanayugalamīlanaṃ vihāya praṇayamayīm udamīmilan nijehām ||41||
children.translated_text: abandoning the closing of their pair of eyes, they opened forth their own desire, made of love.

children.text: iti bahuvidhākelibhir nidāghe vigatavati praviveśa vārṣikaśrīḥ |
children.translated_text: Thus, when the summer had passed with many kinds of delightful play, the splendor of the rainy season entered;

children.text: jaladavalayavidyutālilakṣmyā hariharidāratanūr vilāsam āpa ||42||
children.translated_text: with the beauty of the array of clouds and lightning, the forms of <s>Hari</s> and <s>Hari's</s> beloved (<s>Rādhā</s>) attained playful grace.

children.text: rucim iha kalayan vrajeśasūnur niśi niśi varṇayituṃ ruciṃ jagāma |
children.translated_text: The son of the lord of <s>Vraja</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), kindling beauty here, went night after night to describe [that] beauty;

children.text: idam avadadhatī ca vārṣabhānavy api savayastatir udyad ullalāsa ||43||
children.translated_text: and the daughter of <s>Vṛṣabhānu</s> (<s>Rādhā</s>) too, speaking of this with her companions of equal age, leapt up with rising joy.

children.text: iti ghanasamayasphuṭaprabhāte nijajananīhitaṃ payaḥ kṛtānnam |
children.translated_text: Thus, in the clear dawn of the rainy season, eating slightly the rice cooked in milk prepared by my own mother, mixed with pepper, and warm,

children.text: maricavalitam uṣṇam īṣad aśnann aham anurāmamukhaṃ sukhaṃ bhajāmi ||44||
children.translated_text: I enjoy happiness following <s>Rāma</s> (Balarāma) and others.

children.text: mama janitithir eṣyatīha bhādre vrajajanaśarma ca tena sārdham aṅga |
children.translated_text: My birthday festival will come here in <s>Bhādra</s> (August-September), along with the joy of the people of <s>Vraja</s>, O dear one;

children.text: dvayam api yad idaṃ jaganti dhinvan purataraparva taniṣyati prahṛṣya ||45||
children.translated_text: both of these, delighting the worlds, will cause an ancient festival to expand with jubilation.

children.text: 1. (b) ovṛter; 2. (b) ośayyām
children.translated_text: [Textual notes]

children.text: gṛhaśikharaśikhām athādhirūḍhāḥ kalayata niśy api goṣṭhavanyadhāma |
children.translated_text: Climbing to the pinnacle of the house, even at night, behold the dwelling of the cowherd settlement and the forest;

children.text: pratilavataḍidālidīptibhūmnā dina iva sarvam idaṃ muhur vibhāti ||46||
children.translated_text: with the abundance of the luminous splendor of lightning at every instant, all this shines repeatedly as if it were day.

children.text: nabhasi jaladavidyudālilakṣmīr bhuvi haritaḥ sphurad indragopakāntiḥ |
children.translated_text: In the sky, the beauty of the array of clouds and lightning; on the earth, the splendor of <s>indragopaka</s> (red insects) glittering among the green;

children.text: madanugabhavatīva kānanaśrītatim anupaṣakatāṃ sakhi prayāti ||47||
children.translated_text: as if intoxicated, the beauty of the forest has come forth in rows — behold it, O friend!

children.text: sthalakulam iha kūrmapṛṣṭhatulyaṃ nayanagatipradaratnaveśamadhyam |
children.translated_text: The group of high grounds here, like turtle-backs, in the midst of jewel-like pools visible to the eye,

children.text: vitatam abhinavaprarūḍhatārṇaṃ pari dhavalāgaṇapālanaṃ karomi ||48||
children.translated_text: extended, with freshly grown young grass — around them I perform the tending of the white herds.

children.text: girivaraśirasi vyudastapārśvāvṛtimaṇisadmani labdhadhenudṛṣṭiḥ |
children.translated_text: On the summit of the great mountain (<s>Govardhana</s>), in the jeweled pavilion surrounded on all sides,

children.text: bahuvidhaśatarañjamukhyakhelā vidadhad ahaṃ sakhibhiḥ sukhaṃ prayāmi ||49||
children.translated_text: having obtained the sight of the cows, performing many kinds of games beginning with chess, I go happily with my companions.

children.text: sravati salilam ambude tarūṇāṃ kuharagṛhe rasayan phalaṃ sakandam |
children.translated_text: When water pours from the cloud, savoring the fruit with its stalk in the cave-abodes of trees,

children.text: upasalilaśilāsanaḥ sadannaṃ dadhisahitaṃ sakhibhir vibhaktam aśnan ||50||
children.translated_text: seated on stones near the water, I eat the excellent food shared with my companions, accompanied by yogurt.

children.text: kvacid api girimūrdhni dhenuhūtiṃ vidadhad amūś ca mudā niviśya paśyan |
children.translated_text: Somewhere on the mountain-top, making the cow-call and joyfully settling them down and watching,

children.text: adhi vaḍabhigatābhir īkṣaṇīyaḥ satatam ahaṃ bhavatībhir atra tatra ||51||
children.translated_text: always visible to you women who have come through the foot-paths — here and there I [am present].

children.text: yugmakam
children.translated_text: A pair of verses

children.text: iha vahati kadambanīpayūthīśavalitaketakagandhasandhavātaḥ |
children.translated_text: Here, the wind bearing the fragrance of <s>kadamba</s>, <s>nīpa</s>, <s>yūthī</s> (jasmine), and <s>ketaka</s> (screwpine) mixed with rain

children.text: anubhavasaviviktataṃ ca yadvat tava mama cānubhavanti gandham alpam1 ||52||
children.translated_text: wafts; and just as [you] experience that distinctness of experience, so too you and I experience a subtle fragrance.

children.text: yadi pulakakulākulāsi kṛṣṇaṃ kanakapaṭaṃ paṭu māṃ nirīkṣya bhadre |
children.translated_text: If you are bristling with horripilation, O auspicious one, looking intently at <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> in golden garments,

children.text: ghanataḍidudayād vivardhamānāṅkuradharanītulanāṃ tadā prayāsi ||53||
children.translated_text: then, from the rising of lightning from the cloud, you approach the comparison with the earth bearing increasing sprouts.

children.text: ghanasamayam anudhvaniṃ plavādyā vidadhati te ca ghanā muhus tam atra |
children.translated_text: In the rainy season, the <s>plava</s> (cranes) and other [birds] produce their calls, and those clouds [answer] repeatedly;

children.text: niśamayitum amuṃ parasparaṃ ye sphuṭam aniśaṃ racayanti suṣṭhu puṣṭam ||54||
children.translated_text: those who, in order to hear one another, clearly and continuously produce [their sounds], richly and abundantly.

children.text: jaladam anu kaniṣṭhamadhyamukhyāḥ plavaśikhicātakanāmakāḥ prapannāḥ |
children.translated_text: Following the rain-cloud, the lesser, middle, and chief [birds] — named <s>plava</s>, peacock, and <s>cātaka</s> — have taken shelter;

children.text: taratamavidhinā tadekanandi dvayam aparas tu tadekajīvijīvaḥ ||55||
children.translated_text: in graduated fashion, the other [creature] delights in that alone — one whose very life depends on that alone.

children.text: aham api tad idaṃ vilokamānaḥ kila vimṛśāmi nijān ananyabhaktān |
children.translated_text: I too, beholding all of this, indeed reflect upon my own devotees of single devotion;

children.text: yadanu ca bhavadīyavṛndam etat paramatayā mama cittam āviveśa ||"56||
children.translated_text: and thereupon this group of yours entered my mind with supreme intensity."

children.text: iti vadati harau papāta vṛṣṭir visṛmaraśīkarabhāk tataś ca mukhyaḥ |
children.translated_text: As <s>Hari</s> was speaking thus, rain fell, scattering its drops; and then the chief [companions]

children.text: paṭakuṭam adadhur dvayasya khaṭṭām anu paritaḥ sadanaṃ paṭāvṛtaṃ ca ||57||
children.translated_text: placed a cloth-tent and a cot for the two, and a shelter covered with cloth all around.

children.text: bahir anu ghanagarjitaṃ savarṣaṃ gṛham anu talpavareṇyam alpaśītam |
children.translated_text: Outside, the thundering of clouds with rain; inside, upon the excellent couch, slightly cool —

children.text: tadanu vasitaśastavastram etanmithunam anusmara citta gaurakṛṣṇam ||58||
children.translated_text: then remember, O mind, this pair — the fair and the dark (<s>Gaura</s> and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) — dressed in charming garments.

children.text: iti bahuvidhasukhakhelayā prayāte ghanasamaye śaradā jagāma tāṃ ca |
children.translated_text: Thus, when the rainy season had passed with many kinds of joyful play, autumn arrived; and that [season] too

children.text: sphuṭam avakalayan purāvad ākhyad vṛṣaravijāṃ murajin niśi krameṇa ||59||
children.translated_text: <s>Murajit</s> (the Slayer of <s>Mura</s>, i.e., <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), clearly perceiving it as before, described it to the daughter of <s>Vṛṣabhānu</s> (<s>Rādhā</s>) gradually, night by night.

children.text: aharahar udaye śarat śaratpraveśe nijajananīnihitaṃ payaḥ kṛtānnam |
children.translated_text: Day after day at sunrise in autumn, upon the advent of autumn, eating the rice cooked in milk prepared by my own mother,

children.text: sahasuhṛd upabhujya2 dhenusaṅgād vanakalitaṃ bhavatīṃ vivicya vacmi ||60||
children.translated_text: having partaken with my friends, I discern you distinguished from the forest in the company of the cows, and speak.

children.text: vahad anunavam abhram acchabhāvaṃ praṇidadhatī kṣitir ātmanānucakre |
children.translated_text: The cloudless sky bearing the nature of purity, the earth emulated it with herself;

children.text: taducitam upajīvanīyabhāve mayi bhavatī bhavatīdṛg eva subhrū ||61||
children.translated_text: fitting to that life-sustaining state, you, O fair-browed one, are just like her in relation to me.

children.text: taḍidanuvalane gate payodād bata iti mānam ite tathā payode |
children.translated_text: When the lightning departs from the cloud — 'Alas!' — when the cloud too departs in pride,

children.text: tvadapagamadaśāṃ nijāṃ purāṇīṃ muhur aham asya tulām anusmarāmi ||62||
children.translated_text: I repeatedly recall the comparison with my own ancient state of your departure.

children.text: 1. (a) alpaḥ; 2. (a) upayujyaatha yadi kalayāmi tīranīravrajam anu khañjanahaṃsakañjakāntim |
children.translated_text: And if I observe the flock of wagtails, swans, and herons at the bank of the waterways,

children.text: varatanu bhavadāgatiṃ vitarkya bhramadaśayā bata vibhramaṃ prayāmi ||63||
children.translated_text: O beautiful one, conjecturing your arrival, I wander in a state of bewilderment, alas!

children.text: abhilaṣati madīyakeliśikṣāgurum iyam acyutavallabhākṣilakṣmīm |
children.translated_text: 'This row of lotuses, opening wide, desires the beauty of the eyes of <s>Acyuta's</s> beloved as the guru of its amorous skill' —

children.text: iti kila kamalāvalīṃ vidhūtām uru śapharīnikaraś carīkarīti ||64||
children.translated_text: thus indeed the shoal of fish sports around it.

children.text: jalam anuparamācchatāṃ nirīkṣya kṣaṇam anusandadhad antaraṃ yadāsmi1 |
children.translated_text: Gazing at the supreme clarity of the water for a moment, as I am contemplating the depth within,

children.text: pratiphalitam iha svam īkṣamāṇas tava manasā tulanām anusmarāmi ||65||
children.translated_text: seeing my own reflection here, I recall with my mind the comparison with you.

children.text: navanavapulinaṃ nirīkṣya tat tat padadalanāṃ viniṣidhya tatra cāham |
children.translated_text: Seeing the fresh sandbanks here and there, and forbidding the treading of [their] surface,

children.text: manasi vinidadhe sma hetum anyaṃ vacasi tad anyam idaṃ tvam eva vetsi ||66||
children.translated_text: I placed in my mind one reason, and [expressed] another in words — this you alone know.

children.text: pathi pathi kusumaṃ vicitya śaśvat kusumamayaṃ dhanurādikaṃ vidhāya |
children.translated_text: Gathering flowers on every path, constantly, fashioning bows and the like made of flowers,

children.text: pulinakulam adaḥ prapadya tasmin kusumaśarāya vayaṃ baliṃ dadāma ||67||
children.translated_text: reaching that cluster of sandbanks, upon it we make an offering to <s>Kusumaśara</s> (<s>Kāmadeva</s>, the Flower-arrowed God of Love).

children.text: kumudamukulam alpam alpanālaṃ śaratulitaṃ viracayya śilpaśāli |
children.translated_text: Making a tiny lotus bud with a short stem, comparing it with autumn, skillfully crafted,

children.text: dhanur api navaketakasya parṇān tricaturayogadṛḍhān dṛḍhaṃ sṛjāmaḥ ||68||
children.translated_text: and also bows from leaves of fresh <s>ketaka</s> (screwpine), firmly [bound] with three or four joinings — we firmly fashion them.

children.text: iti harir acalat priyāsahāyaḥ kusumacitiṃ vidadhad vicitrakeli |
children.translated_text: Thus <s>Hari</s> moved, accompanied by his beloved, making flower-offerings, in wonderfully varied play,

children.text: pṛthutanuviṣamacchadāṃs tanīyas tanulatikābhir itasmitān jahāsa ||69||
children.translated_text: laughing with faint smiles through slender creeper-like [women] at the broad-bodied [ones covered] with uneven leaves.

children.text: atha pulinam asāv apaśyad indoḥ pratitanuvat pulinasya tadvadindum |
children.translated_text: Then he beheld a sandbank, like a replica of the moon's [surface], and the moon [mirrored] in that sandbank;

children.text: kutukarasavaśād viśaṃś ca tasmin svam amṛtasiktanibhaṃ vidan nananda ||70||
children.translated_text: entering it from the force of curious delight, knowing himself to be like one bathed in nectar, he rejoiced.

children.text: avadad atha sakhītatir mukundaṃ "kusumaśaraḥ kva nu yaṃ prapūjayāmaḥ" |
children.translated_text: Then the group of <s>sakhīs</s> (companions) addressed <s>Mukunda</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>): 'Where is the Flower-arrowed One (<s>Kāmadeva</s>) whom we shall worship?'

children.text: harir avadad "ahaṃ sa eva sākṣād iti mama pūjanam eva tasya viddhi ||71||
children.translated_text: <s>Hari</s> replied: 'I am he himself, in person — therefore know that the worship of him is my worship itself.'

children.text: yadi kusumaśarasya śaktim asmin mayi manuṣe natarāṃ tadālivargaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'If you acknowledge the power of the Flower-arrowed One (<s>Kāmadeva</s>) in me, a human, even more so, O group of friends,

children.text: mama kusumaśarān sahasva sākṣād" iti kalayan sa tu kampate sma vargaḥ ||72||
children.translated_text: then endure my flower-arrows directly!' — thus reflecting, that group trembled.

children.text: atha vṛṣaravijāvadan "murāre śatrum iha bhaumayudhi tvam eka eva |
children.translated_text: Then the daughter of <s>Vṛṣabhānu</s> (<s>Rādhā</s>) said: 'O <s>Murāri</s> (Slayer of Mura), in the battle with the enemy <s>Bhauma</s> (Narakāsura), you alone,

children.text: parabalabahukoṭiśastram asyan jayam abhajatas tad idaṃ nicāyayasva2 ||73||
children.translated_text: hurling weapons of many tens of millions of the enemy's great forces, attained victory — now demonstrate that!'

children.text: upaparisaram asya tarhi sarvāḥ kusumaśarān kirann amūr asaṅkhyān |
children.translated_text: Then all [the gopīs] around his vicinity, showering innumerable flower-arrows,

children.text: abhinad ayam amūn śarān amūṣāṃ kusumaśarair uta kañcukāny avidhyat ||74||
children.translated_text: he split those arrows of theirs with his flower-arrows, and pierced their bodices!

children.text: harim atha jitakāśinaṃ babhāṣe hariramaṇīvitatiḥ smitaṃ dadhānā |
children.translated_text: Then the array of <s>Hari's</s> beloveds, bearing smiles, addressed <s>Hari</s> who bore the pride of victory:

children.text: "vayam iha yuvatījanās tad asmatparicitam eva vihāram ādiśasva ||"75||
children.translated_text: 'We here are young women — therefore command the pastime that is familiar to us!'

children.text: harir atha vihasan jagāda "yūyaṃ bharatamataṃ prati rājathātivijñāḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Hari</s> then, laughing, said: 'You are supremely expert in the doctrine of <s>Bharata</s> [on performing arts];

children.text: tad anusarata gītavādyanṛtyaṃ mama bhavatībhir udetu tāratamyam ||"76||
children.translated_text: therefore follow [the arts of] song, instrumental music, and dance — let the gradation between me and you, ladies, become manifest!'

children.text: drava iva harigānataḥ śilādyaṃ hariramaṇījanasīmakaṃ babhūva |
children.translated_text: From <s>Hari's</s> singing, even stone and the like became as if liquid; [his singing] became the boundary-marker of the community of <s>Hari's</s> beloveds;

children.text: harir ajani kathañcanāpi dhīraḥ sa ca na tathājani gānatas tu tāsām ||77||
children.translated_text: <s>Hari</s> somehow remained composed, but he could not remain so from their singing.

children.text: atha militatayā cakāra lāsyaṃ
children.translated_text: Then, joining together, he performed <s>lāsya</s> (graceful dance)

children.text: nijavanitābhir ayaṃ na cāpa sāmyam |
children.translated_text: with his own women, but did not attain equality [with them];

children.text: tam abhidadhur amūr vayaṃ na sandīpanim
children.translated_text: they declared: 'We did not find him as an inspirer —

children.text: abhajāma guruṃ kathaṃ nu vidmaḥ ||78||
children.translated_text: how then do we know him as [our] teacher?'

children.text: 1. (a) margin: yadāsti; 2. (a) nicāyayāṃ sma
children.translated_text: [Textual notes]

children.text: harir akuruta taṇḍunā praṇītaṃ naṭanam anena jahāra cittam āsām |
children.translated_text: <s>Hari</s> performed the dance led by <s>tāṇḍava</s> (vigorous dance), and by this stole the hearts of those [women];

children.text: iha jagadur amūr vayaṃ na padmātulitatamā yad ihāpi śikṣitāḥ smaḥ ||79||
children.translated_text: hereupon they said: 'We are not comparable even to a lotus — for we have been instructed even in this!'

children.text: vyatimilitatayātha rāsanṛtyaṃ vyadhiṣata tā dayitena tena sārdham |
children.translated_text: Then, joining together, they performed the <s>rāsa</s> dance with their beloved;

children.text: vilasitavaramādhurībhir eṣāṃ suravanitā mumuhur muhur muhuś ca ||80||
children.translated_text: by the sweetness of the excellent playfulness of these, the celestial women were bewildered again and again.

children.text: atha harir akarod ihāpi citraṃ javamahasā sa tathānaśe samastam |
children.translated_text: Then <s>Hari</s> performed a wonder here too — with the speed of great might, all of that vanished;

children.text: yad akhilamahilāḥ svapārśvalagnaṃ tam anulavaṃ bata menire nirīkṣya ||81||
children.translated_text: for all the women, seeing him clinging to their own side, considered him [present] at every instant, alas!

children.text: vilasitam idam ittham ācarantaḥ śramam upalabhya cirād amī niviṣṭāḥ |
children.translated_text: Having thus enacted this play, when they perceived fatigue after a long time, they all sat down,

children.text: vyajanasalilapānakāṅgarāgakramukapuṭādibhir āśritābhir iṣṭāḥ ||82||
children.translated_text: attended by [companions offering] fans, water, beverages, body-ointments, and betel-leaf rolls — [they were] beloved.

children.text: atha bhṛśam upalabhya śāntim etā harihariṇīnayanā niśāvasāne |
children.translated_text: Then, having fully attained peace, those doe-eyed ones of <s>Hari</s>, at the close of night,

children.text: vanam anuvihṛtiṃ mudā dadhānāḥ svam upavanīmaṇimandiraṃ sasarjuḥ ||83||
children.translated_text: joyfully bearing the memory of their forest pastimes, went to their own jeweled garden-pavilion. ||83||

children.text: atha muraripurādhikākhyayugmaṃ mṛduśayanaṃ pratilabhya valguśarma |
children.translated_text: Then the foe of <s>Mura</s>, having obtained a soft bed with the pair bearing the supreme name (<s>Rādhā</s>), and charming comfort,

children.text: atanuta śayanaṃ tathā yathā tat tanum api bhedam adhāt tanudvayaṃ na ||84||
children.translated_text: extended his rest in such a way that, though [forming] two bodies, neither the couch nor the pair of bodies admitted any separation. ||84||

children.text: atha girivaraparvaṇi svasṛṇāṃ
children.translated_text: Then, on the festive day of the great mountain (<s>Govardhana</s>), among his own sisters,

children.text: gṛhagataṃ parvaṇi kārtike māsi |
children.translated_text: at the household festival in the month of <s>Kārtika</s>,

children.text: bahuvidhamahasā1 saśarmapūrṇe
children.translated_text: filled with manifold splendor and full of happiness,

children.text: tadanu mukhaṃ mukharaṃ sukhaṃ karoti ||85||
children.translated_text: thereafter he makes the face [of all] eloquent with joy. ||85||

children.text: atha śaradanujā yadā ṛtuśrīr2 mṛdumṛduśītamayī samājagāma |
children.translated_text: Then, when the younger sister of autumn — the beauty of the [next] season, gentle and gently cool — arrived,

children.text: aśanavasanakānanādrikhelāśayanasukhādi hariḥ priyām uvāca ||86||
children.translated_text: <s>Hari</s> spoke to his beloved about food, garments, forest, mountain, play, bedding, comforts, and the like. ||86||

children.text: "surabhinavakaśālitaṇḍulībhiḥ purusitavaṣkayanīpayaskṛtānnam |
suparimalahariḥ plutaṃ samantād vikalitavalkalabījanāgaraṅgam |87||
children.translated_text: drenched all around with a flood of fine fragrance, mixed with tree-bark spices, seeds, and ginger,
"With fragrant fresh rice-grains of fine unhusked rice, cooked in abundantly boiled milk,

children.text: bahughṛtaparipakvapiṣṭabhedaṃ pravitatamaṇḍakaroṭikābhir iṣṭam |
children.translated_text: with varieties of flour dishes baked in much ghee, desirable with rounds of <s>maṇḍaka</s> (flat bread) and <s>roṭikā</s> (bread),

children.text: parikṛtadalitārdrakaṃ svamātrārpitam uṣasi svadate varoru mahyam ||88||
children.translated_text: with prepared, pounded fresh ginger — offered by my own mother in the morning — it delights me, O beautiful-thighed one! ||88||

children.text: yugmakam
children.translated_text: A couplet

children.text: tadanu ca jananī dadāti veṣaṃ mṛgamadakuṅkumacūrṇapūrṇavastram |
children.translated_text: Thereafter my mother gives me attire — garments filled with musk and saffron powder;

children.text: tam aham aharahaḥ sajan sarāmaḥ sahasakhivīthir atīva śarma yāmi ||89||
children.translated_text: wearing that, I, day after day, together with <s>Rāma</s> (Balarāma) and the lanes of friends, go to supreme happiness. ||89||

children.text: yadapi vividhatemanādimadhyaṃ dinam upalabdham ihāsti paṅkajākṣi |
children.translated_text: Even though the day is obtained here with various <s>tema</s> (wet) dishes and the like at the beginning and middle, O lotus-eyed one,

children.text: tadapi bhavati sārdrakaṃ ghṛtāntaḥkṛtapacaśarṣapaśākam ādarāya ||90||
children.translated_text: it becomes [complete] with moist preparations, ghee-infused, cooked with mustard and greens — for the sake of delight. ||90||

children.text: aharahar anudhenukañcukādicchavisavitṛcchavimitratācchabhāsaḥ |
children.translated_text: Day after day, with the beauty of un-milked young cow garments and the like, with splendor rivaling the sun's brilliance, with pure radiance,

children.text: sakhibhir akhilakeliśālihārītakarutakarmaṇi narmaśarma yāmaḥ ||91||
children.translated_text: with friends, in the delightful work of all pastimes including <s>śāli</s> (rice-games) and <s>hārītaka</s> (myrobalan), we go to playful happiness. ||91||

children.text: pariṇatatarajambhanāgaraṅgakramukamukhadyutiśoṇakānanāntam |
children.translated_text: Through forests whose ends are reddened by the splendor of ripe areca nuts, ginger, and oranges,

children.text: smitalasitakaṭiñjarādipuṣpapramuditasarvam ahardivaṃ bhramāmaḥ ||92||
children.translated_text: rejoicing in flowers like the smiling <s>kaṭiñjara</s> and the rest — we roam throughout the day. ||92||

children.text: calasakhi tad idaṃ vanaṃ nirīkṣemahi himaleśini3 mārgaśīrṣamāsi |
children.translated_text: O playful friend, let us behold this forest in the month of <s>Mārgaśīrṣa</s>, when there is a trace of frost;

children.text: paraparadivase tu śītaśīte nahi vihṛtir4 bahir aucitīṃ bhajeta ||93||
children.translated_text: but on the next day and the day after, when it is cold and very cold, outdoor play would not be fitting. ||93||

children.text: iti harivacanād anena sārdhaṃ vanam anugamya viramya ramya-rūpam |
children.translated_text: Thus, at <s>Hari</s>'s word, having gone with him to the forest and having rested, beholding its lovely beauty,

children.text: samucitaphalapuṣpasaṅgraheṇa pramadabhṛtaḥ pramadāgṛhaṃ samīyuḥ ||94||
children.translated_text: they returned to the pleasure-house of the women, bearing delight, with a collection of suitable fruits and flowers. ||94||

children.text: 1. (a) opa(rva)tayā; 2. (a) ṛtuśrīṃ; 3. (b) himane niśi; 4. (a) vikṛtir
children.translated_text: 1. (a) opa(rva)tayā; 2. (a) ṛtuśrīṃ; 3. (b) himane niśi; 4. (a) vikṛtir [variant readings]

children.text: iti mṛdutaratulikānukūlīkṛtaśayanaṃ nayanābhirāmayugmam |
children.translated_text: Thus, on the softest pillow-adorned bed, the pair delightful to the eyes,

children.text: madhuripuvṛṣabhānujāsamākhyaṃ na vapuṣibhedam avāpa nāpi citte ||95||
children.translated_text: known by the supreme names of the foe of <s>Madhu</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) and the daughter of <s>Vṛṣabhānu</s> (<s>Rādhā</s>), admitted no separation in body or in mind. ||95||

children.text: atha dhanur aparāṃśamīnarājāvadhi ravibhogagatāhasaṅghabhāge |
children.translated_text: Then, when the sun's course had entered the portion from <s>Dhanus</s> (Sagittarius) to <s>Mīna</s> (Pisces), the king [of fish/zodiac] — in that span of days,

children.text: muraripur avadat purāvad etāṃ vṛṣaravijāṃ sa nijāṃ vilāsalakṣmīm ||96||
children.translated_text: the foe of <s>Mura</s> spoke as before to this daughter of <s>Vṛṣabhānu</s> (<s>Rādhā</s>), his own playful splendor: ||96||

children.text: ghṛtadadhikṛsarārdrakādijuṣṭāḥ kaṭuvaṭakā vividhāni sandhitāni |
children.translated_text: "<s>Kaṭu-vaṭakās</s> (spicy fritters) prepared with ghee, yogurt, <s>kṛsarā</s> (rice-sesame dish), fresh ginger, and the like — various preparations —

children.text: aharahar udaye madīyamātrā mayi nihitāni bhṛśaṃ sukhaṃ vahanti ||97||
children.translated_text: every day at dawn, offered by my mother, placed before me, bear supreme happiness for me. ||97||

children.text: bahuvidham atha dugdhabāṣpapakvaṃ mṛdu mṛdu piṣṭakam iṣṭapūrṇam |
adhi dinadinamadhyamātmamātrā prahitam ahaṃ ramayan mudaṃ bhajāmi |98||
children.translated_text: day after day at midday, my own mother sends them, and I, delighting in them, attain joy. ||98||
And then various soft, soft <s>piṣṭakas</s> (flour cakes), cooked by steaming in milk, filled with desired [ingredients] —

children.text: ghusṛṇarucir atūlasūkṣmavastradvidalajakañcukayukpidhānavakṣaḥ1 |
children.translated_text: With saffron-hued, incomparably fine garments and a jacket of split cloth covering the chest,

children.text: pavanarahitagharmaśarmadātṛsthalam anu dhenvavanena śarma yāmi ||99||
children.translated_text: in a windless place that gives the comfort of warmth, I go to happiness with the cow-pasture. ||99||

children.text: śiśiram anu samastasattvajāte rutirahite kikhiṣu pragalbhavākṣu |
children.translated_text: After winter, when all living creatures have lost their sounds, when the peacocks become bold in their calls,

children.text: samavadad iha ko 'pi neti nūnaṃ sakhi hasitaṃ dayayā sahāyati sma ||100||
children.translated_text: someone here said 'Not so!' — surely, O friend, [even that] laugh was of compassionate joy. ||100||

children.text: śiśirajanuṣi durdine 'pi jāte mitirahitā dhavalāḥ sukhaṃ caranti |
children.translated_text: Even on bad days born of winter, the white [cows] graze happily without limit;

children.text: śṛṇu sakhi tadupāyam antyam ekaṃ mama muralījani yat tu vāyusūktam ||101||
children.translated_text: listen, O friend, to the ultimate means for that — it is the wind-hymn born of my flute! ||101||

children.text: śiśiram akusumāntaraṃ nirīkṣya srajam iha kundakṛtāṃ bibharmi citrām |
children.translated_text: Seeing that winter is without flowers, I wear a wonderful garland made of <s>kunda</s> (jasmine) here;

children.text: vipadi yad upajīvanaṃ tad eva pratipadam ādarabhājanaṃ vibhāti ||102||
children.translated_text: that which serves as sustenance in adversity — that very thing shines forth as an object of respect at every step. ||102||

children.text: iha drutam itam ahaḥsamūham ūhā-
children.translated_text: This collection of days swiftly passed here — others blamed [me]

children.text: viṣayatayā dadhataḥ pare nininduḥ |
children.translated_text: for holding it as the subject of imagination;

children.text: bhavadupasṛtivardhirātrivṛddher
children.translated_text: but from the growth of nights lengthened by your approach,

children.text: alam aham asya tu vaśmi2 dīrgham āyuḥ ||103||
children.translated_text: I am content — I celebrate its long life! ||103||

children.text: atha madhu ṛtur eṣyati praphullaṃ vananikaraṃ vidadhad yad ātataḥ prāk |
children.translated_text: Now the spring season approaches, making the groves of the forest blossom — that which was formerly spread wide;

children.text: hariharivanitākulaṃ praphullaṃ svayam abhavad bata paśya tasya vīryam ||104||
children.translated_text: ah, behold its power — [even before arriving], the forest overflowing with <s>Hari</s>'s women has itself blossomed forth! ||104||

children.text: prathamasamam athātra bhojanādyaṃ samucitam āpravidhāya kṛṣṇacandraḥ |
children.translated_text: First, as before, having properly arranged food and the like, <s>Kṛṣṇacandra</s>

children.text: niśi niśamayati sma vanyavṛttaṃ dinadinam apy atulaṃ vṛṣārkaputrīm ||105||
children.translated_text: tells the daughter of <s>Vṛṣabhānu</s> (<s>Rādhā</s>), night after night, the forest happenings, day after day, incomparably. ||105||

children.text: niśamaya kutukaṃ vane 'dya dṛṣṭaṃ vitaritari prasabhaṃ bibharti bhikṣuḥ |
children.translated_text: "Hear a curiosity seen in the forest today: a beggar forcibly carries [things] to the generous giver;

children.text: amadhujanuṣi puṇḍrake dvirephā muhur api jhaṅkṛtitarjanāṃ vahanti ||106||
children.translated_text: on a <s>puṇḍraka</s> (white lotus) not born of honey, bees repeatedly produce threatening buzzing! ||106||

children.text: kim iyam ahaha mādhavīti nāmnā
children.translated_text: What! Does this <s>mādhavī</s> (spring jasmine) — by this name

children.text: janaviditeti madāt praphullati sma |
children.translated_text: well-known to people — blossom from pride?

children.text: śiva śiva na vayaṃ madhoḥ kim itthaṃ
children.translated_text: O auspicious one! Are we not [the real] spring (<s>Madhu</s>)? Why then

children.text: kusumam adhuḥ kila saptalādayaś ca ||107||
children.translated_text: did the <s>saptalā</s> and other plants give their blossoms? ||107||

children.text: sa bakulasahakāraketakīnāṃ sakaruṇakiṃśukanāgakeśarāṇām |
children.translated_text: The rows of <s>bakula</s>, <s>sahakāra</s> (mango), <s>ketakī</s> (screwpine), compassionate <s>kiṃśuka</s> (flame of the forest), <s>nāgakeśara</s> (ironwood) —

children.text: tatir atiśuśubhe vilokya yāntu bhramarapikapravarā mahaḥ sajanti ||108||
children.translated_text: shone exceedingly; beholding them, the foremost among bees and cuckoos come, producing splendor. ||108||

children.text: malayajamarud eṣa ity abhikhyaḥ pavanagaṇaḥ pratipadya matkavanyām |
children.translated_text: This group of winds, known by the name 'sandal-scented breeze,' reaching my forest of poets,

children.text: manayujajayisurabhātiśastāṃ prasatikrīṇa ivātra mandamandam ||109||
children.translated_text: as if a purchaser of the extremely praised fragrance conquering the mind-born (<s>Kāma</s>), wanders gently, gently. ||109||

children.text: iti madhuṛtuvarṇanaṃ vitanvan madhuripur anyanijapriyājanānām |
children.translated_text: Thus, while describing the beauty of the spring season, the foe of <s>Madhu</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), of his own other dear ones

children.text: caritavivṛtim anyanāyikānāṃ3 caritamiṣāt kalayann amūṃ stute sma ||110||
children.translated_text: and other heroines — under the pretext of narrating their pastimes, praised this one [<s>Rādhā</s>]. ||110||

children.text: 1. (a) ovṛkṣaḥ; 2. (a) raśmi; 3. (a) margin: nāyikātām
children.translated_text: 1. (a) ovṛkṣaḥ; 2. (a) raśmi; 3. (a) margin: nāyikātām [variant readings]

children.text: kusumakulam idaṃ dadhāti tāvad bhramarapikādigaṇas tathā svarūpam |
children.translated_text: "This multitude of flowers blossoms, and the hosts of bees, cuckoos, and the like [maintain] their nature;

children.text: priyasahacaratā yadā priyāṇāṃ parasamaye śaratāṃ ca vajratāṃ ca ||111||
children.translated_text: the companionship of beloveds with their dear ones — when that proper time [is past], it becomes both autumnal and thunderbolt-hard. ||111||

children.text: ayi vidhumukhi saṅgatapriyāṅgi priyavirahād aparā dhṛtāvasādāḥ |
children.translated_text: O moon-faced one, one whose limbs are joined with her beloved! Other [<s>gopīs</s>], bearing grief from separation from their beloved,

children.text: uta kusumapikāditudyamānā dhruvam adhunā priyatāvaśā bhramanti ||112||
children.translated_text: being agitated by flowers, cuckoos, and the like, surely now wander under the power of love. ||112||

children.text: sphuradasahanatā mithaḥ sapatnyaḥ pathi rahasi priyam ātmanābhisṛtya |
children.translated_text: The co-wives, manifesting unbearable passion, meeting their beloved secretly on the path and in solitude,

children.text: diśi ca vidiśi ca sphurantam ārān nahi niranaiṣur amūḥ kva vā labheran ||113||
children.translated_text: shining in every direction and quarter from afar — those [<s>gopīs</s>] could not attain him, nor did they know where they might obtain him. ||113||

children.text: niyamitacaraṇān nikuñjadhāmni
children.translated_text: Some, with restrained steps in the bower-dwelling,

children.text: kvacana ca vāsakasajjikāyamānāḥ |
children.translated_text: being adorned for the <s>vāsakasajjā</s> (awaiting the beloved) [nāyikā type],

children.text: priyatamam anavāpya mānam āñcan
children.translated_text: not obtaining their most beloved, maintained their pride —

children.text: mukham iva mānadhanā hi dhanyanāryaḥ ||114||
children.translated_text: for those blessed noble women were indeed rich in pride, as if [pride were] their very face. ||114||

children.text: api ca tadaparās tu vāsasajjā
children.translated_text: And yet other [<s>gopīs</s>], adorned for the tryst,

children.text: muhur api cintanalabdhakalpatantrāḥ |
children.translated_text: repeatedly obtaining the plan of their imaginings,

children.text: priyatamam upalabhya cātra jāgrad
children.translated_text: and obtaining their most beloved here in wakefulness,

children.text: valitavad āpa sukhaṃ na cātra bhedam ||115||
children.translated_text: attained happiness as if in a trance — without any difference here. ||115||

children.text: api dayitatamena khaṇḍitāśā nahi kalahāntaritā babhūva kāpi |
children.translated_text: Even though their hopes were shattered by their most beloved, no [<s>gopī</s>] became a <s>kalahāntaritā</s> (one separated by quarrel);

children.text: ucitam api tad etad eva yasmād dayitatamaḥ katham anyathā ghaṭate ||116||
children.translated_text: for even that [shattering] was itself fitting, since how can the most beloved act otherwise? ||116||

children.text: vyavahitapadavīṃ mamāsti netuṃ nahi bhavatīm api kiñcanāpi vastu |
children.translated_text: There is no thing whatsoever that can lead me to a concealed path,

children.text: na puruṣam iha jāgarādyavasthātrayam api cetanayā viyoktum īṣṭe ||117||
children.translated_text: nor does consciousness desire to separate any man from the three states of waking and the like. ||117||

children.text: niśi sumukhi tad adya kuñjapuñjaṃ sahasavayastati sadravaṃ vrajāvaḥ |
children.translated_text: O beautiful-faced one, tonight let us go to that mass of bowers with our friends, moving swiftly;

children.text: iha hi kumudamudgarādipuṣpaṃ sitarucirociṣi rocamānam asti ||118||
children.translated_text: for here, flowers such as <s>kumuda</s> (night-lily), <s>mudgara</s> (club-flower), and the like are enchanting in their pure, beautiful radiance." ||118||

children.text: vidhur atha dayitānvitaḥ sakhībhiḥ saha sahakhelam iyāya puṣpadeśam |
children.translated_text: Then the creator (<s>Vidhu</s>) [i.e., <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>], accompanied by his beloveds and their friends, went to the flower-grove for play together;

children.text: sphuṭam iha tu vidhuḥ paraḥ savṛndas tadupari vandanamālikāyate sma ||119||
children.translated_text: clearly here the supreme moon, with its retinue, seemed to become a garland of worship above it. ||119||

children.text: adhi kusumavanaṃ virajamānaṃ harim atha kāntimatī vṛṣārkaputrī |
children.translated_text: Then, in the flower-garden shining brightly, the radiant daughter of <s>Vṛṣabhānu</s> (<s>Rādhā</s>) met <s>Hari</s>,

children.text: sukhakaralalitāviśākhikādipriyasavayastatibhiḥ samaṃ samayya ||120||
children.translated_text: together with groups of her dear age-mates such as the delightful <s>Lalitā</s>, <s>Viśākhā</s>, and others. ||120||

children.text: sukusumanikarānupadadānaṃ svam api tad apy anu tanvi yojayantī1 |
children.translated_text: Offering heaps of fine flowers step by step, and herself also adorning herself with those,

children.text: dvayam api tadanuvratakriyābhir dravatatibhiś ca mudāñci kurvatībhiḥ ||121||
children.translated_text: both [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s> and <s>Rādhā</s>], with acts of mutual devotion and with flowing [emotions], made the attendant [<s>gopīs</s>] burst with joy. ||121||

children.text: alam uparigapuṣpavṛndam icchuṃ2 svayam api tattadupagrahaṃ diśantī |
children.translated_text: Desiring the garland of flowers above, herself giving various kinds of assistance [to pick them],

children.text: drutam iva na kim asmadīya rājñyā vahasi nideśam iti smitāñcigīrbhiḥ ||122||
children.translated_text: with smile-tipped words: 'Do you not quickly carry out the command of our queen?' ||122||

children.text: prasabham iva ramām amūṃ bhujābhyāṃ
children.translated_text: As if forcibly holding that beautiful <s>Ramā</s> (<s>Rādhā</s>) in his arms,

children.text: hṛdi dadhataṃ3 muhur ūrdhvapuṣpahetoḥ |
children.translated_text: to his chest, repeatedly for the purpose of the flowers above —

children.text: sarud iva tadabhīṣṭam āpayantī
children.translated_text: fulfilling her desired [wish] as if it were a season [of joy],

children.text: sakalakalaṃ hasitaṃ vitanvatībhiḥ ||123||
children.translated_text: with the [<s>gopīs</s>] spreading all-encompassing laughter, full of art. ||123||

children.text: sukusumacayakūṭam īkṣayantaṃ svayam api taṃ tulitaṃ nicāyayantī |
children.translated_text: Making him look at the heap of fine flowers, herself making him weigh [the garlands],

children.text: vividhamatatayā prahāsabhedāc chalam api satyam api prajalpinībhiḥ4 ||124||
children.translated_text: with varied opinions, laughter of different kinds, with both jest and truth — by the chattering [<s>gopīs</s>]. ||124||

children.text: kusuma-viracanā-mayaṃ kalāpaṃ vidadhatam āśu ca taṃ pṛthak sṛjantī |
children.translated_text: Quickly making and separately releasing a garland made entirely of flower arrangements,

children.text: nutim anutim api dvaye pi tasmin samiṣa-vacaḥ pracayena tanvatībhiḥ ||126||
children.translated_text: spreading praise and criticism for both aspects of it — with a profusion of half-serious words by the [<s>gopīs</s>]. ||126||

children.text: 1. (b) tan niyojayantī; 2. (a) icchaṃ; 3. (a) dadhātaṃ; 4. (a) prajalpitībhiḥ
children.translated_text: 1. (b) tan niyojayantī; 2. (a) icchaṃ; 3. (a) dadhātaṃ; 4. (a) prajalpitībhiḥ [variant readings]

children.text: sva-racita-tad-alaṅkriyāṃ stuvānaṃ sva-racita-tat-tad-dalaṅkṛtiṃ stuvānā |
children.translated_text: He praising her self-made ornamental work, she praising his self-made ornamental work in turn —

children.text: nija-kṛti-janitā-mahattva-buddhiḥ prakṛtir iheti vihasya vādinībhiḥ ||127||
children.translated_text: with the [<s>gopīs</s>] laughing and saying 'The pride born of one's own creation — that is [merely] nature (<s>prakṛti</s>) here!' ||127||

children.text: vaśam akṛta guṇa-kriyāṅga-bhāva-prabhṛtibhir atra ca paśya citta citram |
children.translated_text: Here behold, O mind, a wonder: he, though uncontrolled by qualities, actions, limbs, states, and the like,

children.text: vahati patir adhīna-bhartṛkājñāṃ racayati karma vināpi tāṃ sa tasyāḥ ||127||
children.translated_text: the Lord carries out the command of one whose husband is dependent — and he performs his work even without her [commanding]. ||127||

children.text: aṣṭabhiḥ kūlakam
children.translated_text: A group of eight (verses)

children.text: harir iha janayan vasanta-rāgaṃ hari-vanitā-nikaraś ca suṣṭhu puṣṭam |
children.translated_text: <s>Hari</s>, generating the passion of spring here, and the multitude of <s>Hari</s>'s women, thoroughly nourished [by that passion],

children.text: abhinaya-maya-nṛtya-tāla-juṣṭaṃ vyativaśitaḥ sva-vaśīcakāra viśvam ||128||
children.translated_text: with dramatic dance keeping time — [they], though controlled by each other, brought the universe under their control. ||128||

children.text: iti bahu-vidha-khelayā rajanyāḥ praśamam iva pratipadya nāgarendraḥ |
children.translated_text: Thus, as if reaching the end of the night through manifold play, the lord of the city-dwellers (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>),

children.text: surabhi-kusuma-vṛkṣa-vāṭi-kāntaḥ kṣaṇa-śayana-kṣaṇam āpa kāntayā saḥ ||129||
children.translated_text: beautiful among the fragrant flower-groves, obtained a moment of rest and a moment of repose with his beloved. ||129||

children.text: maṇimayavaracatvarasya śayyām anu kusumānilalīlayā susevaḥ |
children.translated_text: On the bed of the gem-studded fine courtyard, well-served by the playful breeze of flowers,

children.text: paramatamasakhībhir asyamānabhramaratatiḥ sasukhaḥ sukhañcakāra ||130||
children.translated_text: with hosts of bees being fanned away by the dearest companions in the darkness, he, happy, made happiness. ||130||

children.text:
iti sarvartu-līlā
||3||
children.translated_text: Thus [ends] the pastimes of all seasons. ||3||

children.text: atha phalaniṣpattiḥ
children.translated_text: Now, the fruit-attainment (<s>phalaniṣpatti</s>).

children.text: ghoṣe sva-prema-koṣe pitṛ-mukha-sukhada-svīya-vṛndena dīvyan
children.translated_text: In <s>Ghoṣa</s> (<s>Vraja</s>), the treasury of his own love, sporting with his own group that gives joy headed by his father,

children.text: kaṃsena preṣitebhyas tam atibhayamayaṃ vīkṣya nighnan muhus tān |
children.translated_text: seeing those sent by <s>Kaṃsa</s>, greatly fearsome, he struck them down repeatedly.

children.text: hanti1 teṣām apaśyann adhi madhu-puri taṃ hantum añcan sa-vṛndam
children.translated_text: Not seeing [the end of] their [attacks], going to <s>Mathurā</s> to slay him, going with his retinue,

children.text: hatvā tam ghoṣam āgāt tad-atula-sukha-kṛd yaḥ sadā tam bhajāmi ||1||
children.translated_text: having killed him, he returned to <s>Ghoṣa</s> (<s>Vraja</s>), creating incomparable joy — him I worship always! ||1||

children.text: rādhādyāḥ kṛṣṇa-kāntāḥ svayam avataraṇaṃ kṛṣṇavat prāpya līlā-
children.translated_text: <s>Rādhā</s> and the other beloveds of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, having descended [to earth] like <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> himself, by the power of <s>līlā</s> (divine play),

children.text: śaktyā vismṛtya nityāṃ sthitim aparatayā jñāta-kṛṣṇās tathāpi |
children.translated_text: forgetting their eternal state, knowing <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> as separate [from themselves] — even so,

children.text: rāgād aspaṣṭa-kṛṣṇa-śrayaṇa-sukha-ratā prāntataḥ kṛṣṇam eva
children.translated_text: devoted to the happiness of resorting to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, though not clearly [perceiving him], out of passionate love, they ultimately

children.text: spaṣṭaṃ jagmuḥ sva-kāntaṃ tam ati-sukha-sudhā-sindhu-magnāntarāḥ smaḥ ||2||
children.translated_text: went clearly to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> himself as their own beloved — we are those whose inner selves are immersed in that ocean of supremely blissful nectar! ||2||

children.text: haṃho saukhyaṃ mura-dviṭ kaṭu-kaṭaka-ghaṭā2-preṣṭha-kaṃsādi-duṣṭān
children.translated_text: Aho! What happiness! The foe of <s>Mura</s>, having slain the wicked ones — <s>Kaṃsa</s> and the rest, the dearest of the fierce warrior-hosts —

children.text: hatvā tat-kliṣṭa-cittāṃ pitṛ-mukha-janatāṃ nirvṛtāṃ suṣṭhu cakre |
children.translated_text: thoroughly delighted the people headed by his father, whose hearts had been afflicted by them.

children.text: kiṃ cānyaḥ sva-priyāṇāṃ patir iti bahir akhyāti3-duḥkhāni hṛtvā
children.translated_text: Moreover, removing the sorrows of false reports that he was the husband of other women,

children.text: tat-tad-viśleṣa-pīḍācchid ayam atijagada-dṛṣṭi-goṣṭhe vibhāti ||3||
children.translated_text: he, who cut away the pain of separation from each, shines in the pasture-ground beyond worldly vision! ||3||

children.text: prātar mātuḥ sa-hastād aśana-sukha-kṛtī labdha-tātādy-anujñaḥ
children.translated_text: In the morning, having received food from his mother's own hand, the creator of happiness, having obtained permission from his father and others,

children.text: śrī-rāmādi-prasaktaḥ surabhi-gaṇa-śataṃ pālayan moda-yuktaḥ |
children.translated_text: attached to the blessed <s>Rāma</s> (Balarāma) and others, tending hundreds of fragrant cows, filled with delight,

children.text: sandhyāyāṃ gopa-gopī-sukhada-gṛha-gatiḥ sānurāgaṃ kṣapāyām
children.translated_text: at twilight returning home to give joy to the cowherds and <s>gopīs</s>, with love at night

children.text: tat-tad-dīvyad-vihāraḥ sphuratu tava manaḥ sarvadā kṛṣṇa-candraḥ ||4||
children.translated_text: performing his various pastimes — may that <s>Kṛṣṇacandra</s> (Moon-like <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) ever shine in your mind! ||4||

children.text: janmādyaṃ svīya-vṛttaṃ kavi-bharata-kalā-citra-yogena dṛśya-
children.translated_text: The deeds from birth onward, through the art of a poet like <s>Bharata</s>, through the yoga of painting, to be seen —

children.text: prāyaṃ tanvan sabhāyāṃ rahasi tu dayitā pūrva-rāgādy-udantam |
children.translated_text: mostly composing in the assembly, but in private [recounting] the tales of the beloved's <s>pūrvarāga</s> (initial love-awakening) and the like,

children.text: vargaṃ tat-tan-nisargaṃ nijam anu vijayī sarva-sāt-parva kurvan
children.translated_text: making each respective group completely his own according to their nature, victorious [over all], eager for the delight of sporting —

children.text: dīvya-dīvya-śriyābhir viharaṇa-kutukī nandatān nanda-sūnuḥ ||5||
children.translated_text: may the son of <s>Nanda</s> rejoice, with the splendors of his ever-divine sports! ||5||

children.text: yaḥ śrī-paryanta-yācyānvitir iha paśupa-śreṇi-bandhur yaśodānanda-
children.translated_text: He who has the attainment [of being] sought even by <s>Śrī</s> (Lakṣmī) to the end, the kinsman of the rows of cowherds, born as the very limb of <s>Yaśodā</s> and <s>Nanda</s>,

children.text: svīyāṅga-jātaḥ subala-mukha-sakhaḥ kiṃ ca rādhādi-kāntaḥ |
children.translated_text: the friend of <s>Subala</s> and the other companions, and moreover the beloved of <s>Rādhā</s> and the others —

children.text: sa śrī-gopāla-nāmā surabhi-kula-mahaḥ pālayan divya-kelir
children.translated_text: he, known as <s>Śrī Gopāla</s>, protecting the glory of the <s>Surabhi</s> (divine cow) family, of divine sport,

children.text: naktaṃ rāsādi-līlā-lalitatama-gatiḥ sarvadā syād gatir naḥ ||6||
children.translated_text: whose most graceful movements are the <s>rāsa</s> and other <s>līlās</s> (divine plays) at night — may he be our refuge always! ||6||

children.text: śrīmad-vṛndāvanendo madhupa-khaga-mṛgāḥ śreṇi-lokā dvijātā
children.translated_text: O moon of the blessed <s>Vṛndāvana</s>! The bees, birds, and deer; the groups of people; the twice-born;

children.text: dāsā lālyāḥ surabhyaḥ sahacara-halabhṛt-tāta-mātr-ādi-vargāḥ |
children.translated_text: the servants; the cherished <s>Surabhi</s> cows; the group of companions, the plough-bearer (<s>Balarāma</s>), father, mother, and the rest;

children.text: preyasyas tāsu rādhā-pramukha-vara-dṛśāś ceti vṛndaṃ yathordhvaṃ
children.translated_text: the beloveds, among whom the chief, beautiful-eyed ones are led by <s>Rādhā</s> — thus the assembly, in ascending order —

children.text: tad-rūpāloka-tṛṣṇak pramadam anudinaṃ hanta paśyāma karhi ||7||
children.translated_text: thirsting for the sight of his form, joyous — alas, when shall we behold [him] day after day? ||7||

children.text: 1. (a) margin: vantiṃ, hānīm; (b) hantum; 2. (b) oghaṭao; 3. (a) ākhyāti
śaśvad dhyāyati dūraga-sthiti mithaḥ sūkṣma-prathaṃ cāyati
children.translated_text: [The mind] always meditates when [he is] far away; when close, it subtly approaches each other;

children.text: prājyāntargatam ātta-narmas tu sakhī-madhya-sthitaṃ paśyati |
children.translated_text: it beholds [him] seated amidst companions, deeply immersed within, full of humorous sport.

children.text: rādhā-mādhava-nāma-dheya-mithunaṃ vighnān atītyāmitān
children.translated_text: The pair named <s>Rādhā</s> and <s>Mādhava</s>, having overcome limitless obstacles,

children.text: dāmpatye sthitam atra vā yadi rahaḥ prāptaṃ tadā kiṃ punaḥ? ||8||
children.translated_text: are established in conjugal love — or if they attain privacy, then what more [need be said]? ||8||
1. (a) margin: vantiṃ, hānīm; (b) hantum; 2. (b) oghaṭao; 3. (a) ākhyāti [variant readings]

children.text: rādhā-kṛṣṇa-yugaṃ muhur vighaṭanām uttīrya dāmpatya-bhāk
children.translated_text: The pair <s>Rādhā</s> and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, having repeatedly surmounted separation, possessing conjugal love,
